sections.title: Bereishit and the Three Foundations of Creation
sections.summary: The opening word of the Torah contains creation and points toward reverence, the covenant, and Shabbat.

topics.h: All Creation Is Contained in Bereishit
topics.en: In the beginning:, Within the word Bereishit is encapsulated the entirety of the Work of Creation, ) just as we find (Bereishit Rabbah, parashah 11), regarding everything that was created during the six days of Creation, ", terms such as 'the Work of Creation' and the like,. everything being designated by the name Bereishit., And the rationale is that everything was brought into existence through the utterance Bereishit, )., for Bereishit is likewise an utterance (as written in Rosh Hashanah 32a),. and subsequently each individual creation was actualized at its appointed time., And through the Torah, the Holy One, blessed be He, created the universe,. and consequently the entirety of the Torah is likewise incorporated within the utterance Bereishit., And Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai in Tikkunei HaZohar expounded seventy facets upon the word Bereishit, which represents the sum total of the Torah,. for 'there are seventy facets to the Torah.': And it is taught in Tikkunei HaZohar that there are three commandments latent within the word Bereishit:,': ) first: the fear of Hashem, according to this anagram 'reveres with shame' (yarei boshet; as written at the end of Tikkun 6);,: ) second: the covenant (brit), according to this permutation Bereishit – 'a covenant of fire' (brit eish; as written in the Introduction and Tikkun 23);,:. third: Shabbat, according to this anagram 'reveres the Sabbath' (yarei Shabbat)., And these three commandments constitute the deliberate intention of all Creation,. and Israel are sanctified through them.

topics.h: From Fear of Punishment to Reverence Before Hashem
topics.en: For within fear there is the fear of God (yirat Elohim), which is the lower dread of retribution, and this category of fear is not the ultimate purpose of Creation,:, as we find even concerning the inhabitants of Nineveh: 'and they covered themselves with sackcloth, etc., who knows, He may turn, etc.,', where it was exclusively the fear of punishment alone,:. as it is stated: 'and turn away from His fierce anger, that we perish not.'. And this was because they grieved over the physical pleasures of this world lest they be forfeited from them., And our father Abraham, upon observing that they interrogated him as to whether she was his wife or his sister,:, said unto Abimelech: 'Because I thought: surely there is no fear of God in this place,'. for the pagan nations restrained themselves after the Deluge strictly out of fear of punishment., However, true reverent awe of Hashem (yirat Havayah) is found solely within Israel, namely the fear of shame and embarrassment before His majesty,. for this constitutes the primary objective of Creation: that beings revere before Him. ).: And it is brought (Nedarim 20a): "', ''That His fear may be upon your faces' – this refers to shame, ', 'so that you do not sin, etc.,'. any man who possesses shame will not readily sin.' ): And it is taught (at the opening gloss of the Shulchan Arukh, Orach Chayim):,, when a person sets into his heart that the supreme King, the Holy One, blessed be He, Whose glory fills the whole earth, stands over him and beholds his actions, etc.,. immediately awe and humble submissiveness will envelop him in fear of Hashem, blessed be He, and he will constantly feel shame before Him. ).: And our Sages expounded (there, Nedarim 20a):. whoever lacks shamefacedness, it is known that his forebears did not stand at Mount Sinai., For at the Giving of the Torah all were present, even the souls destined to be born into physical bodies in future generations, as they expounded (Midrash Tanchuma, Yitro 11) on the verse 'and with him that is not here with us this day,', and all beheld His glory and His magnificent greatness, blessed be His Name,. and consequently they possess an intrinsic sense of holy shame. ):: And as they stated (Berakhot 28b): ", 'May it be His will that the fear of Heaven be upon you like the fear of flesh and blood,', for one who sees the face of a human being against whom he has sinned is ashamed before him, and so too may the fear of Heaven be upon you,. that he perceives how the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, stands over him and feels ashamed to commit sin., And this lofty fear is designated Reishit (the Beginning),:, as it is stated (Psalms 111:10): 'The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem,':, and it is written (Proverbs 1:7): 'The fear of Hashem is the beginning of knowledge,', for this represents the ultimate intention behind Creation,:. as it is stated (Deuteronomy 10:12): 'What does Hashem your God require of you, but to fear..'

topics.h: Brit Eish: The Covenant and the Struggle Against Desire
topics.en: So too is the second anagram Brit Eish ('Covenant of Fire'), for the primary aim of Creation was likewise for the preservation of the sacred Covenant,:. as it is stated (Proverbs 10:25): 'and the righteous is the foundation of the world.' ), And as written in the holy Zohar (Part I, 93a),, that once an Israelite is circumcised on the eighth day, we are bound inseparably to divine holiness at the root, and our true desire is solely to perform His will, blessed be He,. and therefore the Jewish people are titled Tzaddikim ('righteous')., And even if thereпоследствии arises some moral failing,. it stems solely from the external leaven in the dough (the evil inclination). For all base passions found among Israel arise solely from the spiritual forces of Amalek, who project evil lusts and seek to inject them into the Jewish heart;, and we are continuously battling against the evil inclination, and Hashem, blessed be He, assists us. and shields us within the shelter of His peace through Surrounding Light (Ohr Makif) so that they cannot prevail over us.:. And as it is written alluding to the mitzvah of Sukkah (Psalms 140:8): 'You have covered my head in the day of battle.' And this mirrors what our master Rabbi Simcha Bunim of Peshischa, of blessed memory, taught, on the verse (Deuteronomy 21:10): 'When you go forth to battle against your enemies, etc.,', that its inner literal sense refers to the spiritual war waged against the evil inclination and worldly lusts, )., for the evil inclination is termed the 'enemy' (as written in Sukkah 52a), and we battle incessantly against it, and Hashem will not abandon man into its hand, and to this alludes 'You have shielded my head in the day of weapons'—. meaning on the day of struggle against it., And it is designated 'a covenant of fire,', because whoever walks after the lust of his heart is condemned to the fire of Gehenna,:), as they taught (Pirkei Avot 4:2): 'and the consequence of a sin is a sin,', meaning that out of the very transgression itself the fire of Gehenna is forged,:, as it is stated (Isaiah 33:11): 'your own breath is a fire that shall consume you,' ): and as written in Bereishit Rabbah (parashah 6): ". 'a fire that issues forth from the body of the wicked and consumes them.', And the burning passion for sin is termed 'fire,':). as they said (Kiddushin 81a): 'fire blazes in the house of Amram.' And our father Abraham stands at the entrance of Gehenna and does not permit any circumcised man of Israel to descend thither (. (as written in Bereishit Rabbah, parashah 48).

topics.h: Shabbat: The Third Sanctity of Creation
topics.en: The third permutation is Shabbat Yarei ('reveres the Sabbath')., And the holiness of Shabbat is likewise reserved exclusively for Israel,:, as it is stated (Exodus 31:13): 'for it is a sign between Me and you,', and an idolater who observes Shabbat is liable to death, for they have no connection whatsoever to the sanctity of the Sabbath; ),: and as they stated in Midrash Rabbah (Devarim 1:21):,. a parable of a king and queen sitting and conversing intimately together; whoever comes and intrudes between them is liable to execution., And Shabbat is the ultimate purpose of all Creation, and it synthesizes all three of these commandments, for one who guards Shabbat is called 'one who reveres,':):. as they expounded (Ta'anit 8b): ''Those who revere My Name'—this refers to the guardians of Shabbat.':), And they taught (Yerushalmi Demai 4:1): 'The dread of Shabbat rests even upon an unlearned person (am ha'aretz),' as though he actually sees the King of kings standing over him throughout the entire Sabbath. and is filled with awe before Him lest he stumble, Heaven forbid, into any Sabbath prohibition., Furthermore, Shabbat is termed an 'ot' (sign) and termed a 'brit' (covenant),. for Shabbat is aligned within the mystical secret of the Covenant (Yesod), as written in the holy Zohar.

topics.h: The Three Shabbat Meals and the Patriarchs
topics.en: And the three meals on Shabbat correspond to the three holy Patriarchs,. who are the living roots of these three commandments., Our father Abraham is titled 'one who reveres,', for he constantly perceived the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, standing over him and observing his actions, since he had no mortal teacher to instruct him,: rather he began investigating on his own: 'Can one say that this illuminated palace lacks a guide, etc.', as written in Bereishit Rabbah (parashah 39), and from everything created within the cosmos he perceived that they are the handiwork of Hashem, blessed be He,:, and as it is stated (Isaiah 30:20): 'and your eyes shall see your Teacher,'. and he discerned Hashem, blessed be He, through every detail created in existence., And this is why Scripture notes that He appeared unto the Patriarchs by the Name El Shaddai, and as our master Rabbi Simcha Bunim taught, ).: that this divine Name alludes to what they stated (Chagigah 12a): ", 'I am He Who said unto the world: Enough (dai)!'. for the universe was expanding boundlessly outward until the Holy One rebuked it and brought it to a stand., That is to say: Creation occurred solely so that created beings would recognize His divinity, blessed be His Name, and the Holy One said unto them 'Enough', meaning that the dimensions need not stretch any further,. because Creation as it stands is fully sufficient to deduce and recognize His Godliness through it., And consequently, when our father Abraham recognized His divinity directly from Creation,. he continually perceived the King of kings standing over him., And this vision he merited specifically through circumcision, ),: as written (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashat Vayeira 47:7) that Abraham our father, peace be upon him, said: ",. 'Were it not for circumcision, whence would the Holy One have revealed Himself unto me, as in 'and from my flesh I shall behold God' (Job 19:26).', And he merited to become the native citizen (ezrach) of Israel even though he was not originally born in holiness, because through circumcision he became bound to the primordial supernal Root (Atika) which transcends human intellect, and he perceived the King of kings standing over him,. and stood in 'awe of shame' (yarei boshet) as stated.

topics.h: Yitzchak and the Sanctity of the Covenant
topics.en: And our father Isaac, peace be upon him, corresponds to Brit Eish ('Covenant of Fire'), for his attribute is constriction (Tzimtzum) and divine strength (Gevurah). to conquer and subdue all base passions and corrupt cravings in the world. And this is a supernal consuming fire devouring the base fire of lust and the evil inclination. And our father Abraham was required to wait until the age of one hundred years, so that Isaac would emerge into the world in extraordinary holiness and purity, ): as taught in Bereishit Rabbah (parashah 46): "', ''I am establishing cinnamon in the world, etc.',. So it was only after his blood was bound up, after his base inclination was nullified, and after bodily desire was extinguished, etc.', And it is known that cinnamon is supreme in its fragrant aroma, ).: as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Shabbat 63a):,. that when they kindled the wood of cinnamon trees in Jerusalem, its fragrant scent wafted throughout the entire Land of Israel., And the sanctification of the Covenant is termed a sweet fragrance,:):. as written in Eruvin (21b): ''The mandrakes yield fragrance'— these are the youths of Israel who have never tasted the taste of sin.' And the phrase 'youths of Israel' denotes this specific vulnerability induced during youth, wherein one rises and conquers his inclination,. and through this they emit a sublime, holy fragrance. And Isaac was the very first who was circumcised on the eighth day. and circumcised into the sacred covenantal status of Israel.

topics.h: Yaakov and the Completion of Shabbat
topics.en: And our father Jacob corresponds to the holiness of Shabbat, ): as stated in Bereishit Rabbah (parashah 11): ",. 'Abraham, regarding whom the observance of Shabbat is not explicitly recorded, etc.; Jacob, regarding whom the observance of Shabbat is recorded, etc.', And the meaning is: even though Abraham and Isaac certainly observed Shabbat, since Abraham our father, peace be upon him, fulfilled the entirety of the Torah,. nonetheless, the observance of Shabbat was not explicitly and specifically recorded concerning them., And therefore the Land of Israel was given unto them with defined boundaries and measure, meaning strictly so long as they remained physically within the Land of Israel;: however Jacob, regarding whom the commandment of Shabbat is explicitly documented: ", 'and he encamped before the city' (Genesis 33:18)—meaning he established Sabbath boundary limits (techumin) while it was yet day,. namely the two thousand cubits wherein he established a designated realm for the sanctity of Shabbat. And the reason for two thousand cubits constituting the Sabbath boundary, is that the heavenly measure of goodness exceeds the measure of retribution by five hundredfold; and we find conversely that a negative presence occupies four cubits, )., such as regarding a corpse, a harlot, heresy (Avodah Zarah 17a), and a foul odor (Berakhot 25a);. and the measure of divine goodness exceeding by five hundred times acquires two thousand cubits (4 × 500 = 2,000)., And therefore Jacob merited and inherited the world without bound or limitation,:, and it is written of him (Genesis 28:14): 'And you shall spread abroad to the west, and to the east, etc.,', meaning that he is empowered to burst forth his holiness into every place, even beyond the geographic borders of the Land,. such that wherever Israel may be dispersed, the Holy Shechinah abides in their midst., And the primary moment for the indwelling of the Shechinah within Israel is on the Sabbath day, ),: as taught in the holy Zohar (Part II, 63b): "' ',', ''Let no man go out of his place' (Exodus 16:29), and the inner secret of this word is written: 'Blessed be the glory of Hashem from His place' (Ezekiel 3:12),'. namely the lower Shechinah (Malchut) that rests within the Jewish heart.:), And it is written (Tikkunei HaZohar, Tikkun 6): 'Fortunate is he who prepares for Her a beautiful dwelling in his heart,', and that refers specifically to Shabbat.:)., For it is taught (Berakhot 8a) that the Holy One, blessed be He, has nothing in His world except the four cubits of Halakhah,. meaning that there the Shechinah resides ever since the Day the Temple was destroyed. And our holy Master (the Rebbe of Peshischa), of blessed memory, explained: that the meaning is: whoever conquers his evil inclination and withdraws from forbidden matters according to Halakhah, and accepts upon himself the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven, this is what is titled 'the four cubits of Halakhah,'. for this constitutes the essential objective of every halakhic teaching., And he constructs an abode for the Shechinah in his heart;, and throughout the entire Sabbath a person withdraws at every moment from any violation of Shabbat, since it is remarkably easy to transgress instantaneously in the prohibition of selecting (Borer) and the like,. and through this vigilance his heart becomes consecrated for the dwelling of the Shechinah., And the holiness of Shabbat is comparable to the holiness of the Temple, with the only distinction being that the Temple resides in space. whereas Shabbat resides in time.,

sections.title: Five Lights, Six Gifts, and the Oral Torah
sections.summary: The lights of creation and the six restored gifts illuminate the Written Torah and the Six Orders of Mishnah.

topics.h: Five Mentions of Light and the Five Books of Torah
topics.en: In the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 3:5): The five times the word 'light' is mentioned in the creation passage of 'Let there be light' correspond to the Five Books of the Torah: " ". ''And God said, Let there be light'— corresponds to the Book of Genesis, wherein the Holy One, blessed be He, engaged and created His world.', That is to say: holy souls were required to serve as receptive vessels for receiving the divine light, and these are all the souls that unfolded throughout the Book of Genesis across the succession of generations, until the twelve tribes of God were born,. and they are the primary vessels for absorbing the supernal light. ", ''And there was light'—corresponds to the Book of Exodus, wherein Israel emerged from darkness into great light,' which signifies the revelation of the light of the Torah in this world;, and the preceding Egyptian exile served as the prerequisite preparation for this, ).: as they stated (Berakhot 5a): ",. 'Three precious gifts, etc., were given through suffering: the Torah, etc.' ", ''And God saw the light, that it was good'—corresponds to the Book of Leviticus, which is filled with abundant laws,'. which represents the expansion and permeation of the divine light into all minute details. ". ''And God divided between the light and the darkness'—corresponds to the Book of Numbers, which separates between the generation leaving Egypt and those entering the Promised Land.':, That is: the generation of the wilderness represents the souls linked to the Written Torah, for there are six hundred thousand letters in the Torah, as is known;, whereas those entering the Land are the souls connected to the Oral Torah, –, as written (holy Zohar Part II, 137b) that Moses transmitted it to Joshua— which signifies the Oral Torah,. since the Written Torah he entrusted specifically to the Priests, the sons of Levi.:)., And concerning this they taught (Bava Batra 75a): 'The countenance of Joshua was like the face of the moon,', and this reflective aspect is designated 'darkness' and 'night',:). as they expounded (Sanhedrin 24a): ''He has set me in dark places'—this refers to the Babylonian Talmud.' And in Tanchuma (Parashat Noach 3) on the verse: ''The people walking in darkness have seen a great light'—. this is the great primordial light that the Holy One hid away for those who toil in the Oral Torah.' ), And in the Targum of Shir HaShirim and in Tanchuma (end of Ki Tisa 36):, that Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, knew the distinction between day and night upon the mount,. for by day God taught him the Written Torah, and by night the Oral Torah. ", ''And God called the light Day'—corresponds to the Book of Deuteronomy (Mishneh Torah), etc.,':, which parallels what is stated (Genesis 41:32): 'And for that the dream was doubled unto Pharaoh twice, it is because the thing is established, etc.,' signifying that through the repetition of the matter a second time, the illumination was definitively established for the sustenance of the world to be designated the 'light of day',. which is a thoroughly clarified, verified matter.

topics.h: Five Emanations and the Divine Flow of Light
topics.en: Now, these five lights stem from the vantage point of the Emanator (haMashpia), corresponding to the five divine attributes down to Yesod (Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod), and they flow forth and are channeled into each day of the week through the holiness of Shabbat,. except for Friday (Erev Shabbat), which serves as the active preparation for the arriving Sabbath.

topics.h: Six Blessings Lost Through Adam’s Sin
topics.en: Furthermore, it is taught in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 12:6):: Six things were stripped from Adam the First after his degradation:,, his radiance, his lifespan, and his stature;, the fruits of the earth—which denotes exquisite taste; and the fruits of the tree—which is the celestial fragrance of Gan Eden;:, and this is why Midrash Tanchuma records in its place: 'and he was expelled from Gan Eden', for what Bereishit Rabbah terms 'fruits of the tree' intends likewise the fruits of Gan Eden,:) as written (Bereishit Rabbah 41:9): ''Like the garden of Hashem'—with respect to trees';. and the celestial luminaries. And all of them are destined to be fully restored in the World to Come. ):, And certainly through the sanctity of Shabbat, which is a foretaste of the World to Come (Berakhot 57b),: we merit and taste these very six gifts:

topics.h: The Radiance and Gifts Restored Through Holiness
topics.en: His radiance'—this is the glowing countenance of Shabbat,:). as written (Bereishit Rabbah 11:2): 'He blessed it with the shining countenance of man.' ").: 'His lifespan'—as taught (Yoma 71a): "', ''And years of life and peace shall they add to you, etc.'—these are a person's years that are transformed from adversity to goodness,'. and through the holiness of Shabbat they are converted from wearying toil into tranquil rest and delight. ":)., 'His stature'— for it is taught in the Gemara (Kiddushin 31a): 'It is forbidden for a man to walk with an erect stature,', and as written in Bereishit Rabbah there on that verse;:, meaning as it is written (Leviticus 26:12): 'And I will walk among you'—I will stroll with you in Gan Eden, and consequently souls will then be permitted to walk with upright stature, since I shall stroll with you as equals,:), as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2): ''My undefiled'—My twin, neither greater than the other';:). and along the lines of (there, parashah 3): 'He did not cease cherishing her until He called her My sister.':. Might you think you shall not revere Me? Therefore Scripture adds: 'and I will be your God.', And this is likewise the spiritual nature of the holiness of Shabbat, wherein the commandment is to indulge it with every manner of delight,. and one whose head is bowed down possesses no expansive peace of mind (harchavat hada'at) to enjoy delight. ", 'The fruits of the earth'—this is the heightened flavor experienced likewise in the holiness of Shabbat, ) as taught in Bereishit Rabbah (parashah 11). that the Emperor was served cold dishes and yet found them delicious through the seasoning taste of Shabbat. ", 'And the fruits of the tree'— which is fragrance, is likewise restored through the holiness of Shabbat,:).,. as written in Shabbat (119a): 'The dishes of Shabbat emit sweet fragrance through a certain spice we possess, whose name is Shabbat.': And it is written (Genesis 27:27): 'as the smell of a field which Hashem has blessed'— ):, this is an orchard of apples, as they taught in Ta'anit (29b),:, and in Bereishit Rabbah (65:22) it is stated on this interpretation: the fragrance of Gan Eden entered along with him,. namely the fragrance of Gan Eden, the holy field of apples. ", 'And the luminaries'—meaning that the lights were diminished and severed from the light of the moon,. which alludes to the Oral Torah receiving illumination from the sun, the primary source (Mashpia), which is the Written Torah., And through the holiness of Shabbat they become unified within one another as in the World to Come,:, as it is stated (Isaiah 30:26): 'Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days,'. just as it was prior to the primordial sin.

topics.h: The Six Orders of Mishnah as Receptacles of Light
topics.en: And these six aforementioned restored things correspond to the illumination of the Six Orders of the Mishnah within the Oral Torah from the vantage point of the recipient (haMekabel), and for this reason they emerge in the number six, which also corresponds to the attribute of Yesod,. which binds and channels the flow of the five supernal lights unto the recipient. And they are infused from the holiness of Shabbat into all six working days of the week.

topics.h: The Six Orders in the Language of the Prophets
topics.en: Now, the sanctity of the Orders of the Mishnah our Sages derived (Shabbat 31a): upon the verse (Isaiah 33:6): 'And the stability of your times shall be a storehouse of salvations, wisdom, and knowledge':

topics.h: Zeraim: Faith and Spiritual Cultivation
topics.en: Stability/Faith' (Emunat)—this refers to the Order of Zera'im (Seeds), ). for he believes in the Life of the Worlds and sows (as Tosafot wrote). Now seemingly, idolaters also sow even though they lack faith!: Rather, precisely this is the magnificent virtue of the faith of Israel: even though he performs physical tasks that the natural order seemingly dictates, such as agricultural sowing where things sprout as nature takes its course, nonetheless he knows with complete certitude that everything is directed by the Creator's providence,. even a matter seemingly left to human initiative. ", ''Your times' (Itekha)—this refers to the Order of Moed (Festivals), in that there are designated times and seasons dedicated to divine service,:). as they stated (Shabbat 10a): 'The time for Torah is distinct, and the time for prayer is distinct.' ", ''Strength' (Chosen)—this refers to the Order of Nashim (Women), for this represents inner power and strength,:). as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Avot 4:1): 'Who is mighty? He who conquers his evil inclination.' ", ''Salvations' (Yeshu'ot)—this refers to the Order of Nezikin (Damages), for the primary need for divine salvation is against the four primary categories of damages. which arise through the leaven in the dough (the base inclination).

topics.h: The Four Exiles and the Four Injurious Traits
topics.en: And these four correspond to the four historical empires and exiles, that dominate over the souls of Israel through the four base traits in the psyche,,: and they are: idolatry, jealousy, lust, and honor—,: which manifest as anger, illicit desire, and haughtiness:, Babylonia corresponds to the spiritual archetype of idolatry, for Nebuchadnezzar erected the image of gold, and through this force he held dominion and destroyed the First Temple, in which era there existed within Israel the impulse for idolatry ):. until the Men of the Great Assembly eradicated it (as written in Yoma 69b)., The Kingdom of Media corresponds to lust,:):, as they stated (Berakhot 8b): 'For three things I love the Persians, etc., and they are modest in marital intimacy,', and even though this practice seems like saintly restraint,: in truth it is quite the reverse:,. because they are so utterly inundated in lust, they consequently feel disgraced and ashamed by it.: And therefore it is juxtaposed immediately afterward in the Gemara: "', ''I have commanded My consecrated ones' (Isaiah 13:3)—these are the Persians who are consecrated and designated for Gehenna,', meaning that even though on the surface it displays an appearance of holiness, )., and Israel are titled holy for genuine modesty (as written in Shabbat 86a),. yet they, on the contrary, are designated for Gehenna through it. And Greece embodies pride and arrogant haughtiness, in that they are wise in their own eyes,. and this is the essence of Greek philosophy—external alien wisdom. And Edom (Rome) is the archetype of wrath and murderous bloodshed.

topics.h: The Four Forms of Damage as Spiritual Symbols
topics.en: And one can suggest that the specific primary categories of damages likewise allude to these: ". 'Ox' corresponds to haughtiness—goring with the horn. ",. 'Pit'—corresponds to idolatry, 'broken cisterns' (Jeremiah 2:13). ",. 'Maveh' (tooth/spoil)—according to the opinion that it is the tooth, reflects the lust of consumption. ". 'Fire'—the blaze and fury of wrath.

topics.h: Kodashim and Taharot: Wisdom, Knowledge, and Purity
topics.en: Wisdom' (Chokhmat)—this refers to the Order of Kodashim (Holy Offerings),. for Kodesh (Holiness) is Chokhmah, as is known in the holy Zohar. ", ''And knowledge' (Vada'at)—this refers to the Order of Tohorot (Purities);, for Da'at signifies the Holy Spirit (Ruach HaKodesh),. as written in Rashi's commentary on Ki Tisa (Exodus 31:3) on the verse 'and I have filled him, etc., and with knowledge.', And unto the Holy Spirit it is impossible to arrive except through the purification of the heart,:, and concerning this King David, peace be upon him, pleaded: 'Create in me a clean heart, O God' (Psalms 51:12), because he was the master of all possessors of the Holy Spirit,. and he marks the inception of the Writings (Ketuvim) which were uttered through the Holy Spirit, as is known.,

sections.title: The Threefold Sanctity of Vayechulu
sections.summary: The expressions of the seventh day unveil different dimensions of Shabbat and humanity’s role in completing creation.

topics.h: Three References to the Seventh Day
topics.en: In the passage of Vayechulu there are three occurrences of the phrase ". 'on the seventh day.'. And in the Gemara (Shabbat 88a) they scrutinized: concerning that which is stated 'the sixth day' (Genesis 1:31): Why do I need the superfluous letter Hei?, And the Gemara expounded it as referring to the renowned sixth day of Sivan,. dependent on whether Israel accepts the Torah. And one must understand:, these three superfluous letters Hei in the word HaShevi'i ('the seventh'), what do the Sages expound concerning them?: However, this is likewise expounded according to this very exposition: ", 'If Israel accepts the Torah, etc.,', namely the renowned Seventh Day, which is the Sabbath on which Israel received the Torah, ):: as written (there, Shabbat 86b): ",. 'And everyone agrees that the Torah was given to Israel on Shabbat.' And from the perspective of Israel was written the renowned 'sixth'—, the sixth of Sivan, according to the reckoning of the lunar month which Israel sanctifies; whereas from the perspective of Hashem, blessed be He, was written the renowned 'seventh', alluding to the Sabbath of the Giving of the Torah, for the sanctity of the Sabbath is not dependent upon the calendar established by Israel,. rather it is inherently fixed and immutable.

topics.h: Rest as the Completion of Creation
topics.en: And it is written: 'And God finished on the seventh day' (Genesis 2:2), ),: in accordance with what is written in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 10:9): ", 'Shabbat arrived—rest arrived,', meaning that then Hashem, blessed be He, experienced divine pleasure and serene satisfaction in His universe, ),: and as written (Bereishit Rabbah, parashah 9:4): ",. 'My world, My world! Would that you find favor before Me at all times just as you have found favor before Me at this hour!', And this is why Scripture states Vayechal,:, which the Targum Yerushalmi translates as: 'and He yearned/cherished,'. and cited in the Abudarham that on this account Shabbat is designated 'the coveted of days.', And regarding this it is written 'on the seventh day', for the divine satisfaction of Hashem, blessed be He, was. over the future reality that Israel would receive the Torah on Shabbat. " And He rested on the seventh day from all His work'— ". Vayishbot is likewise an expression of tranquility and rest. " From all His work'— ", the word kol ('all') denotes every phenomenon opposite to the good, ) just as expounded (Bereishit Rabbah there, parashah 9) on the verse 'all that He had made, and behold, it was very good' (Genesis 1:31)—, as applying to every opposite of good, that it too shall become 'very good',. such as the evil inclination and its like.:, And so it is written (Isaiah 45:7): 'and creates evil,' ):,":, yet we recite in the liturgy: 'Who forms all,' using a euphemistic phrasing (Berakhot 11b),. for the term 'all' encompasses the opposite. And this transformation likewise occurs through Israel accepting the Torah on the seventh day. " 'And God blessed the seventh day'—, the term 'blessing' denotes multiplication and expansion,: like the primary blessings in the Torah:. the blessing over fish and the blessing over man. ), And this aligns with what is written in the holy Ohr HaChayim (Genesis 2:2), that the Holy One, blessed be He, imbued into the world vitality sufficient only to endure for six days, and He created the Sabbath day, and upon it Hashem, blessed be He, returns and infuses a soul-vitality into the cosmos. which sustains it for an additional six days. And this is 'and God blessed the seventh day'—. that it multiply and generate another six days. And this is likewise written HaShevi'i with the definite article Hei, alluding to the Sabbath of the Giving of the Torah, whereon Israel would accept the Torah. and become a unified nation of Sabbath guardians.

topics.h: The Three Dimensions of Shabbat Holiness
topics.en: And these three expressions correspond to the three dimensions of Sabbath sanctity: ", Vayechal corresponds to the sanctity of the Field of Holy Apples (Chakal Tapuchin Kadishin / Malchut), namely that Israel are fundamentally good in truth, and the souls of Israel are titled 'apples',. and the Congregation of Israel is the 'Field of Apples'. " Vayishbot mikol melakhto—, which indicates divine satisfaction even over the opposite of good, and this corresponds to the Ancient Holy One (Atika Kadisha / Keter), which is the transcendent utterance Bereishit, ):: and in accordance with what is written (Shabbat 89b): ", 'Though your sins be like these solar years that have been prearranged and proceeding since the six days of Creation, they shall become white as snow'; signifying that through repentance motivated by pure love, Hashem, blessed be He, will reveal that so it was orchestrated before Him, so that light should emerge out of darkness,. and willful sins are converted into merits. ", Vayevarekh—this blessing corresponds to the sanctity of Ze'ir Anpin, ), the letter Vav which is termed the 'sign of truth' (holy Zohar, start of Parashat Vayikra),:, and it is written (Proverbs 12:19): 'The lip of truth shall be established forever,'. that He channel the apprehension of holiness and vitality into the six workdays perpetually.

topics.h: Three Names of Elohim and the Work of Creation
topics.en: And likewise there is written in the passage three times the Name Elohim, which signifies that He is the Master of all forces;,". and the Work of Creation is termed 'the power of His works He declared to His people' (Psalms 111:6), as written in Bereishit Rabbah., Therefore, in the clause Vayechal and in the clause Vayevarekh the Name Elohim is recorded, because these two sanctities operate by virtue of the awakening from below (itaruta d'letata), from the side of Israel and Jacob who constitute the ultimate purpose of Creation;, and regarding this is written the Name Elohim Who is the Master of all powers,. and even this awakening from below originates fundamentally from Hashem, blessed be He., However, in the clause 'and He rested from all His work', which points to the profound rectification of 'though your sins be like these solar years, etc.', which corresponds to the sanctity of Atika Kadisha, the Name Elohim is not written, for it stems from a realm far higher than this,. the level of 'You were He before the world was created, You are He after the world was created.': Only corresponding to this is written subsequently the third occurrence of the Name Elohim: ", 'because that in it He rested from all His work which God created to make' (Genesis 2:3), which likewise teaches that Hashem, blessed be He, derives divine satisfaction, even from all that appears opposite to good; for so it arose in the Supernal Thought before Him in the primordial utterance:, that there must first be darkness, and subsequently light, for there is no light except that which issues from within darkness, and there is no true good except that which emerges from within evil (,. (holy Zohar, Part II, 184a).

topics.h: Asher Bara Laasot: Man Must Complete the Work
topics.en: And this is why it is stated: 'which God created to make'—, meaning that man must rectify and complete it, ): and as written (Bereishit Rabbah, parashah 11:6):, everything created during the six days of Creation requires further action, such as mustard which needs sweetening, etc., even man himself requires spiritual rectification;,", and this is derived from the word 'to make' (la'asot), as Rashi explained, ) and so is written in Midrash Tanchuma (Parashat Tazria 5). that human craftsmanship is beautiful regarding the mitzvah of circumcision. ", And likewise 'to make' denotes that man from his own initiative must rectify through repentance out of love, )., so that willful sins are transformed into merits as taught (Yoma 86a),. and then 'they shall become white as snow.' ): And as written in Midrash Tanchuma (there): ", 'You make him evil, etc., and how many difficult, bitter elements exist in the world far harsher than the evil inclination, yet you sweeten them, etc.,', and then Hashem, blessed be He, will experience divine satisfaction from all that seemed opposite,. when they are converted into actual merits., And since 'to make' is mentioned here concerning human exertion,. the Name Elohim is recorded here, Who is Master of all faculties., And for this purpose is the protracted length of the exile:, that all souls of Israel become refined through repentance from love to become merits,. not a single person among them missing., However, if Heaven forbid a person fails to clarify from his own initiative through repentance, then in the ultimate future Hashem, blessed be He, will reveal and clarify: ", 'And your people are all righteous' (Isaiah 60:21), and whoever is circumcised is designated righteous,. for 'none cast out shall be permanently expelled from Him.' And concerning this is written the clause 'and He rested from all His work', and the Name Elohim is not written in it—, which is the Name of the Work of Creation indicating that He is the Master of all forces—. since this transcendent sanctity stems from Atika, exalted on high beyond measure, as stated.,

sections.title: Beginning Bereishit Anew After Simchat Torah
sections.summary: The cycle of Torah reading renews its hidden sweetness and the vitality of Shabbat.

topics.h: From Simchat Torah to the New Beginning
topics.en: That we begin anew following Simchat Torah from Bereishit ): is based upon what is written in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 36): "' Let there be light'—this is Passover; '. 'and there was light'—this is Rosh Hashanah.', Meaning that on Passover was the preparation for the revelation of the light of the Written Torah, whose essential disclosure occurred on Shavuot, the season of the Giving of the Torah;, whereas on Rosh Hashanah is the actualized inception of light, namely the light of the Oral Torah,. for from Rosh Hashanah begins the renewal of the light of the Oral Torah. ): As taught in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 30): "' Let there be light'—this is the Right; '. 'and there was light'—this is the Left.' ): And so is taught there (Tikkun 21):, From the Right was given the Written Torah, and from the Left was given the Oral Torah, ). and so is written in the holy Zohar (Part II, 167a). And this signifies that on Rosh Hashanah following the flaw, began the renewal of the Oral Torah,. which represents the increase of wisdom to rectify immense indignation., And on Yom Kippur were the second Tablets given, ),: as taught (Shemot Rabbah, parashah 46:1): ", ''And in the second Tablets I grant you that there be contained within them Halakhot, Midrash, and Aggadot;:. this is what is written: 'that sound wisdom is double' (Job 11:6).' And on Sukkot the light of the Oral Torah becomes established through the Water Libation and the Simchat Beit HaShoevah;, and Shemini Atzeret is the wellspring eruption of Torah (nevi'u d'orayta), ). as written (there, Tikkun 13).

topics.h: The Sweetness Hidden in the Written Torah
topics.en: And it is brought in the holy Zohar (Part I, 240a): "' Out of the strong came forth sweetness' (Judges 14:14)— ', 'out of the strong' refers to the Written Torah, '. 'came forth sweetness' refers to the Oral Torah.', Meaning that the Written Torah is designated a lion, ):: and so was expounded (Berakhot 18b): "', ''and he went down and slew a lion, etc.' (II Samuel 23:20)—that he mastered the Torat Kohanim (Sifra),' which pertains to the priestly Book of Leviticus;, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is compared to a lion,:. as it is written (Amos 3:8): 'The lion has roared, etc.' And 'out of the strong came forth sweetness'—, the experiential taste in the words of Torah, which is the foundational essence of the Oral Torah,:, and regarding this is stated: 'sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb' (Psalms 19:11),. and as written in the holy Zohar there. ), And so was expounded (Midrash Tehillim 19:7). the six preceding verses as corresponding to the Six Orders of the Mishnah. ).: And this is what they taught in the Gemara (Pesachim 119a): ", 'One who reveals matters that the Ancient of Days concealed—, and what are they? The reasons and inner tastes of the Torah,'. meaning to taste the internal savor in the words of Torah., And in every single year one senses a renewed taste in the words of Torah,: and this is what is written in the holy Zohar and Tikkunim:, seventy facets to the Torah, corresponding to 'the days of our years are seventy years' (Psalms 90:10),. and there exist even further facets to the Torah for one who prolongs his days. ):: And as we find (Sanhedrin 103b):, King Menashe would expound fifty-five facets in the Torah, ), and Jeroboam —one hundred and three; meaning according to their misconception whereby they presumed their devotions were for Heaven,. they expounded every year a new facet in Torat Kohanim. However, for every individual in Israel there are seventy facets corresponding to our seventy years;, and even though there are years of early youth in which one possesses no conscious knowledge of Torah, nonetheless there radiates within him every year a renewed dimension in Torah, ), akin to what we find (Vayikra Rabbah, parashah 27:10), concerning the reason for circumcision on the eighth day, that there is no circumcision without an intervening Shabbat, where although the infant does not consciously feel the holiness of Shabbat, nonetheless the sanctity of Shabbat radiates upon him;. and so radiates within a child in every year a brand-new facet in the words of Torah.

topics.h: Seventy Facets in the Word Bereishit
topics.en: And in the Tikkunim seventy facets were enumerated within the single word Bereishit, and this is because within the utterance Bereishit the entirety of Creation is encapsulated;, and similarly they are designated the 'Seven Days of Creation',. and the Sabbath is titled Shabbat Bereishit., For within the word Bereishit all Creation is contained, and the Work of Creation encompasses all words of Torah, and Shabbat is the ultimate purpose of the creation of heaven and earth, and Shabbat is the comprehensive summary of the entire Torah;. and therefore he expounded seventy facets upon the word Bereishit. And so exist seventy facets in every word throughout the entire Torah.

topics.h: The Renewed Taste of Torah on Shabbat
topics.en: And immediately upon the onset of Shabbat, is the auspicious time to perceive the renewed taste in words of Torah. ):: For it is brought in the Gemara (Shabbat 31b):, The Holy One, blessed be He, created His world solely so that they revere before Him,: and it is written: 'The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem' (Psalms 111:10); ),: and in the holy Zohar (Part I, 5b): ",. 'Shabbat—the eve of Shabbat is fear, and fear abides upon it.' And similarly the holy Ari, of blessed memory, accounted, the Friday night meal to the holiness of our father Isaac, peace be upon him, which is the Dread of Isaac (Pachad Yitzchak),. for immediately upon the arrival of Shabbat there descends upon Israel dread and holy awe. And on this account we recite in the blessing of Me'ein Sheva: ", 'Before Him we shall serve in awe and dread,' even though in the weekday blessing of Avodah awe and dread are not mentioned;. yet at the entry of Shabbat dread and awe fall upon all Israel.:, And so they said: 'The dread of Shabbat is upon the unlearned person,'. and his testimony is trusted immediately upon the onset of Shabbat. ).: And this is what they taught in the Gemara (Yevamot 6a): ", You do not fear the Sabbath day itself, but Him Who warned concerning the Sabbath, etc.';, and what proof is there from Shabbat, seeing that dread is not written explicitly concerning it?, Rather Shabbat itself is fear, and fear abides upon it,. only that the reverence is directed unto Him Who cautioned over the Sabbath., And the appointed time to perceive the renewed taste in words of Torah, which is the Oral Torah, is on Shabbat,. for all agree that the Torah was given on Shabbat. And we read the weekly portions on Shabbat, wherein there is the disclosure of Atika. to merit the light of the Oral Torah which derives from the dew of Atika., However, the custom is to commence Parashat Bereishit on Simchat Torah, which is Shemini Atzeret in the Land of Israel, wherein occurs the wellspring eruption of Torah, which is the power that Moses our teacher bequeathed to Israel in Parashat Vezot HaBerachah, so that every single Jew can merit to sense the taste in Torah words, which is the core of the Oral Torah;. and therefore it is read on Yom Tov., And subsequently when Shabbat arrives, we commence anew in Parashat Bereishit. to merit the renewed illumination and taste in the Torah.,

sections.title: Tishrei, Nisan, and the Path to Redemption
sections.summary: The two traditions concerning creation and redemption illuminate repentance, Torah, and the cycle of the year.

topics.h: Why We Begin Bereishit in Tishrei
topics.en: We commence Bereishit following Simchat Torah, even though Nisan is the first of the lunar months, ), and Israel reckons time according to the moon, as written (Bereishit Rabbah, parashah 6:3); why then did they not institute starting Bereishit after Passover and concluding on Passover? ).: However, in the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah 11a): According to Rabbi Eliezer, that in Tishrei the world was created—in Tishrei they are destined to be redeemed;. and according to Rabbi Yehoshua, that in Nisan it was created—in Nisan they are destined to be redeemed.

topics.h: The Spirit of Mashiach in Creation
topics.en: And the essence is that in Parashat Bereishit it is written (Genesis 1:2): ", 'And the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters,':),. and in Midrash Rabbah (Bereishit Rabbah 2:4): 'This is the spirit of the Messiah, etc.', Meaning that when man was created upright so that he would not corrupt, yet nonetheless there would be power for the serpent to enter and induce degradation, facing this was created then the spirit of the Messiah, that an appointed time will arrive when the Messiah comes, at which point the world will be permanently rectified so that it can never again degrade, ):. when the Holy One, blessed be He, slaughters the evil inclination as written (Sukkah 52b).

topics.h: Rabbi Eliezer: Creation and Redemption in Tishrei
topics.en: And according to Rabbi Eliezer that the world was created in Tishrei,: the sequence is that redemption will transpire in Tishrei:, in that on Rosh Hashanah will occur the awakening of repentance through the sounding of the shofar,: ), as it is stated: 'If a shofar be blown in a city, will not the people tremble?' (Amos 3:6);, and subsequently Yom Kippur arrives to rectify all the past, and when they merit, there occurs then the holy Union;, and subsequently Sukkot, the season of our gladness,. and the apocalyptic war of Gog and Magog transpires on Sukkot., And even though through repentance the time of redemption is always present, ).:, as stated: 'Today, if you will listen to His voice' (Psalms 95:7), as written (Sanhedrin 98a), yet 'in its time' (be'itah) the awakening of repentance will stem from Hashem, blessed be He,:, and as it is stated (Ezekiel 36:26): 'and I will remove the heart of stone, etc.,':. and it is written: 'and I will cause you to walk in My statutes.'

topics.h: Rabbi Yehoshua: Creation and Redemption in Nisan
topics.en: And according to Rabbi Yehoshua that the world was created in Nisan, there was created then the spirit of the Messiah so that redemption occur in Nisan when it arrives 'in its time',: and the sequence will resemble the redemption from Egypt originating directly from Hashem: that there will be plagues, and Israel will be refined through all ten divine attributes,. and the redemption will proceed from Hashem, blessed be He. And therefore they instituted that they conclude the Torah in Tishrei;, and after Sukkot, even though we observe that complete rectification has not yet materialized, nonetheless the entire month is prepared and auspicious for repentance, ) and as we said concerning what is written in Midrash Tanchuma (Parashat Ha'azinu 1). that on this account its zodiac constellation is termed Libra / Scales (Moznayim)., And Shabbat is particularly primed for repentance,:, as stated (Psalms 92:1–2): 'A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day: It is good to give thanks / confess unto Hashem,', ) for whoever confesses and forsakes shall obtain mercy (Proverbs 28:13), as written (in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 19);. and through the observance of Shabbat they are immediately redeemed.

topics.h: The Renewal of Shabbat and the Future Redemption
topics.en: And we have already mentioned that it is written 'the burnt- offering of every Sabbath on its Sabbath' (Numbers 28:10), and likewise 'and from one Sabbath to another' (Isaiah 66:23), showing that every Shabbat possesses a distinct sanctity unique to that specific Sabbath, and that sanctity corresponds to the sanctity of the Torah portion read on that Shabbat;. and the sanctity of Parashat Bereishit is that souls merit the illumination of the spirit of the Messiah., Therefore we commence Bereishit on the final Sabbath of the month of Tishrei, such that it is inconceivable that they should read Bereishit in Marchesvan, unless Simchat Torah itself coincided with Shabbat. and the calendar rule of Lo ADU Rosh preventing it. For even though we observe that there have passed well over eighteen hundred years, and we have not yet merited to be redeemed, perhaps on this very Shabbat we shall merit to be redeemed immediately through an awakening of repentance from Above,. since the entire month of Tishrei is auspicious for this., In contrast to Nisan, where once we see that Passover has passed without plagues and the redemption sequence like the Exodus,. there is no spiritual context to commence Bereishit., And if redemption were to arrive through repentance initiated by Israel, ", as in 'Today, if you will listen to His voice',. there is no designated specific season for this at all.

topics.h: Repentance as the Path to Redemption
topics.en: And even according to Rabbi Yehoshua, the season of redemption achieved through repentance is designated uniquely for Tishrei,. wherein the awakening of repentance stems from Hashem, blessed be He. ):: Even according to his approach pursued in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 97b): "), 'Not through repentance and good deeds' (as will be elucidated elsewhere),. and each Master articulated one facet and they do not fundamentally disagree., And therefore they instituted that they conclude the Torah on Simchat Torah, and commence on the final Shabbat of Tishrei Parashat Bereishit, the sanctity of the portion being that they merit the light of the spirit of the Messiah,:, as it is stated: 'And the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters,': and in Midrash Rabbah: by virtue of repentance which is likened to water;:) and in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 36): 'over the face of the waters'—and there is no water other than Torah;, and Shabbat is auspicious for repentance as stated;, and likewise Shabbat is the appointed time to merit Torah, for all agree that on Shabbat the Torah was given;, and so too the Oral Torah, ),: as written in the holy Zohar (Part I, 47b): ", 'The seventh day—this is the Oral Torah, which is the seventh day,', namely Malchut is the mouth, we title it the Oral Torah; and perhaps we shall merit on this Shabbat the spirit of the Messiah. by virtue of the Torah and by virtue of repentance.,

sections.title: Why Bereishit Follows Simchat Torah
sections.summary: An extended examination of the months of creation, the times of redemption, and the renewal of Torah.

topics.h: The New Torah Cycle and the Seasons of Teshuvah
topics.en: We begin the book of Genesis immediately after Simchat Torah, even though Nisan is the first of the lunar months, ), and Israel reckons its calendar according to the moon, as written in Bereishit Rabbah (Parashah 6), so why did they not institute that we begin Genesis after Passover and conclude it on Passover? ).: However, in the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah 11a):, according to Rabbi Eliezer that the world was created in Tishrei, in Tishrei they are destined to be redeemed;,. and according to Rabbi Yehoshua that it was created in Nisan, in Nisan they are destined to be redeemed.,: And the deeper meaning is, that in Parashat Bereishit it is written: ", "And the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters,":, and in the Midrash Rabbah: "This is the spirit of the Messiah, etc.,", meaning that when man was created upright so that he would not corrupt, yet nonetheless the serpent would possess the power to enter and cause the corruption; concerning this was the spirit of the Messiah created then, so that a time would arrive when the Messiah shall come, when the world will be permanently rectified so that it can no longer be corrupted, for the Holy One, blessed be He, will slaughter the evil inclination, ):. as written in Sukkah (52b)., And according to Rabbi Eliezer that the world was created in Tishrei,: the order is that the redemption shall unfold in Tishrei:, in that on Rosh Hashanah there will be the arousal of repentance through the blowing of the shofar,: as it is said: "If a shofar is sounded in a city, will the people not tremble?", and afterward Yom Kippur comes to rectify all the past, and when they merit, the supernal union will occur then;, and afterward Sukkot, the season of our rejoicing,. and the war of Gog and Magog occurs during Sukkot., And even though through repentance the time of redemption is always viable,:, as it is said: "Today, if you will listen to His voice," )., as written in Sanhedrin (98a), ", yet when it arrives "in its appointed time" (be'itah), the awakening of repentance will emanate directly from Hashem, blessed be He,:, and as it is said: "And I will remove the heart of stone, etc.,":. and it is written: "And I will cause you to follow My statutes.", And according to Rabbi Yehoshua that the world was created in Nisan, the spirit of the Messiah was created then so that the redemption would take place in Nisan when it arrives "in its time",: and the process will mirror the redemption from Egypt originating directly from Hashem, blessed be He:, that there will be plagues, and Israel will be clarified through all ten spiritual attributes,. and the redemption will come unilaterally from Hashem, blessed be He., And therefore they instituted that they conclude the Torah in Tishrei and after Sukkot;, even though we see that the complete rectification has not yet occurred properly, nonetheless the entire month remains primed and uniquely potent for repentance, ) and as we mentioned based on what is written in Midrash Tanchuma (Ha'azinu). that on account of this its zodiac constellation is named Libra (the Scales)., And Shabbat is inherently primed for repentance,:, as it is said: "It is good to give thanks / confess unto Hashem,", for whoever confesses and forsakes his sin shall find mercy, ), as written in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer (chapter 19),. and through the observance of Shabbat they are immediately redeemed.:, And we have already explained that it is written: "The burnt-offering of every Sabbath on its Sabbath,", and likewise "and from Sabbath to Sabbath,", that every Shabbat possesses a distinct sanctity unique to that particular Sabbath, and this sanctity is the holiness of the Torah portion read on that Sabbath;. and the sanctity of Parashat Bereishit is that they merit the light of the Messiah's spirit., And therefore we begin Genesis on the final Sabbath of the month of Tishrei, such that it cannot be conceived that they would read Bereishit in Marcheshvan,. unless Simchat Torah fell on Shabbat with the calendar rule of 'lo ADU Rosh'., For even though we see that several more than eighteen hundred years have passed and we have not yet merited to be redeemed, perhaps on this Sabbath we will merit to be redeemed immediately through an arousal of repentance from Above,. and the entire month is uniquely auspicious for this., In contrast to Nisan, after we see that Passover has passed and there were no plagues nor a process of redemption like the Exodus from Egypt,. there is no basis to begin Genesis., And if redemption is to come through repentance from Israel's initiative—"Today, if you listen to His voice"—. there is no designated time for this at all. And even according to Rabbi Yehoshua, the time of redemption through repentance is designated specifically for Tishrei,. wherein the arousal of repentance will come from Hashem, blessed be He. ). Even according to his approach pursued in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 97b): "), "Not by repentance and good deeds" (as will be elucidated elsewhere),. and one Master stated one aspect and the other Master stated another aspect, and they do not fundamentally disagree. And therefore they instituted that they conclude the Torah on Simchat Torah, and begin Parashat Bereishit on the final Sabbath of Tishrei, for the holiness of the portion is that they merit the light of the Messiah's spirit,:, as it is said: "And the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters,":. and in Midrash Rabbah: "In the merit of repentance, which is compared to water.":), And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 36): "'Over the face of the waters'—and there is no water except Torah,", and Shabbat is auspicious for repentance as stated;, and likewise Shabbat is the time to merit Torah, for according to everyone the Torah was given on Shabbat;, and likewise the Oral Torah, ),: as written in the holy Zohar (Part I, 47b): ", "'The seventh day'—this is the Oral Torah, which is the seventh day,",. meaning Malchut is the mouth, which we designate as the Oral Torah. And perhaps on this Sabbath we will merit the spirit of the Messiah. in the merit of the Torah and in the merit of repentance.,

sections.title: The Shabbat Meals and the Divine Presence
sections.summary: The language of the holy meals expresses the distinct spiritual illuminations of Shabbat and Yom Tov.

topics.h: The Distinct Mysteries of the Shabbat Meals
topics.en: On Yom Tov we recite: "This is the meal of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah,":, while on Shabbat we recite: "The meal of the Field of Holy Apples and Ze'eir Anpin,": which are essentially one and the same theme as the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah:, the Holy One, blessed be He, being the aspect of Ze'eir Anpin,. and His Shechinah being the Field of Holy Apples. Yet there is added on Shabbat the meal of Atika Kadisha. And we must understand why the phrasing of the two meals on Shabbat changed, from the phrasing uttered on Yom Tov, inasmuch as they represent one identical concept?, However, the matter is, that the aspect of Atik is the bond that Israel possesses with Hashem, blessed be He, transcending mortal intellect and human comprehension;, and this corresponds to the crown of the head of tefillin, above the intellectual faculties,:, within which is written: "Hashem our God, Hashem is One";:. and within the tefillin of the Master of the World it is written: "Who is like Your people Israel, one nation".:, And concerning this supernal bond it is stated: "For Hashem shall be your confidence (be-khislekha),":, as brought in the Yerushalmi: "In matters wherein you are foolish/ignorant (kesil)," meaning even in a realm where man holds no comprehension, which lies completely above cognitive grasp; and as was fulfilled in our father Isaac, peace be upon him, when he sought to bless Esau according to his intellectual evaluation, and nonetheless there was brought before him the one who was truly worthy of the blessing through the meal,:, concerning which it is written: "And I ate of everything,":). and expounded in Bereishit Rabbah: "From all the goodness prepared for the righteous in the World to Come." And through this there radiated within him the aspect of Atika. from the primordial Root that transcends human comprehension., And the holiness of this attribute is likewise bestowed on Shabbat unto the souls of Israel, the Source that transcends human perception,:, as it is said: "To know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you";, and this dimension is termed Arikh Anpin, ): and as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Bereishit Rabbah, beginning of Parashah 21): ", "Great is the power of the prophets who compare the form to its Creator, etc.,. and upon the likeness of the throne was a likeness as the appearance of a man, etc.", And the bestowal of holiness from Above wherein there is some intellectual grasp. is termed, relative to that first higher dimension, Ze'eir Anpin., In contrast to Yom Tov, where the influx of holiness from Above in general is termed the Holy One, blessed be He;, and for this reason the title Shechinah on Yom Tov was altered as well, which represents the awakening from the side of the souls of Israel,:, as it is said: "I am Hashem Who dwells in the midst of the children of Israel,". namely the dimension of Knesset Yisrael., And on Shabbat, because there exists a supreme influx from Above, namely from the supernal dew that drips from Atika, the holiness of Knesset Yisrael is designated by the name Field of Holy Apples, meaning the dimension of a field that is seeded, bears fruit, and blossoms, through the dew that drips from Atika, and casts forth into the Field of Holy Apples,. unto the souls of Israel who are termed apples.,

sections.title: The Hidden Light and the Protection of Shabbat
sections.summary: The primordial light, the Tree of Knowledge, and the guarding of Shabbat reveal the struggle to separate good from evil.

topics.h: Primordial Light and the Second Shabbat Meal
topics.en: We recite at the morning meal of Shabbat: "May His light dwell within it,", meaning the Primordial Light,: as brought in Sefer HaBahir: ", "And a great light was created, etc., and the Holy One, blessed be He, foresaw that they could not endure it;, He took the seventh part and set it in its place, and the remainder He concealed for the righteous in the World to Come, etc.";, and this is "May His light dwell within it,". signifying that on Shabbat we can merit the light concealed for the World to Come., For Shabbat is a foretaste of the World to Come, ):. one-sixtieth of the World to Come (Berakhot 57b). ): And in the holy Zohar (in this portion, 46a): ", "'And that it was good'—to conceal it so that the wicked of the world would not benefit from it," ) and so it appears from the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 11). which expounded it from the verse: "And from the wicked their light is withheld.", And we must understand:, behold, even on Shabbat not every individual of Israel merits to feel the concealed light, only one who is worthy to merit;, so why was it hidden—let it remain manifest, and the wicked simply will not merit to enjoy its light? ): Furthermore, regarding the essence of the light it is stated (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 3): that the Holy One, blessed be He, wrapped Himself in it like a garment, and the splendor of His majesty radiated from one end of the world to the other, etc.;, and if so, if the wicked were to benefit from it and merit the light of the Holy One, blessed be He, they would no longer be wicked;, and while they remain wicked they surely would not benefit from it, so whichever way you look at it, why was it concealed? Indeed, in truth, an analogous difficulty arises:, concerning that which is said: "And now, lest he put forth his hand and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever";, and it is difficult: if eating of the tree of life operated as a metaphysical catalyst to live forever,:. surely it was in the power of the Holy One, blessed be He, to alter its nature: that he eat and not live!:, And in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu it is taught: "And the tree of life is nothing other than Torah";,:), and in the holy Zohar (Part II, 60b): "And 'tree' is Torah, and 'tree' is the Holy One, blessed be He";: and if so, the difficulty remains: let him eat and live forever!, However, the matter is, that because he ate from the tree of knowledge, an intermingling of good and evil was created, and had he eaten also from the tree of life afterward, the good within him would have merited that he eat and live forever,. while the evil within him would have intensified constantly. And in truth death was necessary for the evil, in order to separate the evil from the good, leaving it to the wicked, while the righteous inherit the good; and as the Ari of blessed memory wrote ).: concerning what they said (Chagigah 15a): ", "If the righteous merits, he takes his portion and his peer's portion in Gan Eden;. if the wicked is convicted, he takes his portion and his peer's portion in Gehenna.", For the righteous—"and your people are all righteous"—, and there exists opposite him a soul holding a good spark belonging to his share, and when he merits, he takes the good,. and the evil is separated unto the soul opposite him within the kelipah., And in the Generation of the Flood and the Generation of the Dispersion, the souls of Israel were intermingled there as well, for from them emerged all the exalted and holy souls;. only because it was intermingled among the seventy kelipot, evil gained dominance., And so wrote the Ari of blessed memory, that the souls of the Generation of the Flood were reincarnated in Egypt, and decreed upon them: "Every son that is born you shall cast into the river," and the souls of the Generation of the Dispersion were likewise in Egypt. and decreed upon them the labor in mortar and bricks.:, And this is what they said: once the Holy One looked upon the Generation of the Flood and Dispersion, etc., and had the light not been concealed, the good within them would have merited to enjoy the Primordial Light, and the evil would intensify repeatedly just as with the eating of the tree of life;, for since there was a mixture of good and evil, the good could merit the light and the evil within it would strengthen and empower them to do further evil through that very power;, and therefore He arose and concealed it from them,:. as it is said: "And from the wicked their light is withheld.": And this is likewise the intention of the holy Zohar cited above: ". "So that the wicked of the world would not benefit from it."

topics.h: Guarding Shabbat from Sin and the Light of Wisdom
topics.en: And on Shabbat, concerning which it is written: "Guarding the Sabbath from profaning it, and keeping his hand from doing any evil";:, and in the Mekhilta it is stated: that he is safeguarded from transgression;: and in Pri Etz Chayyim the wording is: that he is rescued from the accusation of the evil inclination;. and that is achieved through the observance of the lower Shabbat., And whoever merits through this the higher Shabbat, ): as written in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 48): ", "Two times is Shabbat mentioned here corresponding to the supernal and lower Shechinah, namely supernal Shabbat and lower Shabbat throughout their generations; fortunate is he who makes for them on Shabbat a dwelling in the two chambers of the heart, and the evil inclination is cleared away from there, etc.", then they are able to request "May His light dwell within it,". that he merit the concealed light that is revealed on Shabbat., And we request this during the second meal, the meal of Atika, which the Ari of blessed memory reckoned corresponding to the holiness of our father Abraham, peace be upon him, whose dimension of holiness is the light, ): as brought in Midrash Rabbah (in this portion): ", "'And darkness'—this is the Generation of Enosh; upon the face of the deep'—this is the Generation of the Flood, etc.;:, the Holy One, blessed be He, said: How long shall the world proceed in darkness?, Let the light come: 'Let there be light'—this is Abraham,". and it is the first utterance., Even though 'In the beginning' is also an utterance, it corresponds to the intellect concealed from all contemplation, and the utterance "Let there be light" alludes to the aspect of Chokhmah (Wisdom),. the beginning of the manifest revelation of something out of nothing., And this is the sanctity of our father Abraham, peace be upon him, who illuminated the world with his wisdom to recognize the providence of Hashem, blessed be His Name,":. as it is said concerning him: "Who raised up righteousness from the east," as written in Midrash Rabbah., Until he bound himself in this at the end of his days to the dimension of Atika, which is faith transcending mortal intellect,"':, as it is said: "And he believed in Hashem," regarding the glad tidings of children, even though he saw in his wisdom that there was no natural way for him to have children,:, as it is said: "For I called him one," for according to his nature he was in the status of one without children; yet through binding himself to the aspect of Atika which is Mazala (the supernal source), ), as brought in the holy Zohar (Part III, 79b), which is the Root transcending human comprehension,:)., as written in Megillah (3a): "Even though they did not see, their mazal saw,". and through the power of Atika, which is the realm of "Israel is not subject to planetary mazal," he merited children.:, Therefore we recite at the meal of Atika: "May His light dwell within it,". which is the sanctity of our father Abraham, peace be upon him. ", "With fine wine,", which alludes to the Oral Torah that is compared to wine,:, as it is said: "And drink of the wine that I have mingled"—the wine of the Oral Torah;, and this is the aspect of the wisdom of our father Abraham, peace be upon him, ): as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 61): ", "A father did not teach him and a master he did not have, rather the Holy One, blessed be He, made his two kidneys like two rabbis,. and they welled forth and taught him Torah and wisdom.",

sections.title: Adam’s Teshuvah and the Redemptive Power of Shabbat
sections.summary: The aftermath of Eden is understood through repentance, the serpent’s influence, and the higher and lower Shabbat.

topics.h: Adam’s Exile, Repentance, and the Two Sabbaths
topics.en: In the Zohar Chadash at the end of this portion:, Adam the First, once he was banished from the Garden of Eden, thought that he would die immediately, and he was weeping, supplicating, and returning in repentance, until the Holy One, blessed be He, accepted him in repentance and prolonged his days, etc.,. granting him His day, which is one thousand years.: And so it is written afterward: ", "And after they recognized their iniquity in what they had sinned, they embittered themselves over what they sinned, and she even more so because she had been the first to transgress, etc.;:. Rabbi Eliezer said: Eve returned to confess over that iniquity, etc.". Behold, Adam and Eve repented with complete repentance. And we must understand: why was the decree of mortality not entirely nullified? ):: And in the Gemara (Eruvin 18b): ". "Adam the First was a great pious man, etc., and sat in fasting for one hundred and thirty years, etc.". Yet concerning the Gemara, one could say this took place after he was sentenced to banishment and death, after the final decree., However, according to what is written in the Zohar Chadash, perforce they repented with complete repentance within that very day, to the extent that their repentance availed to prolong their days to one thousand years;, so why did repentance not avail to abolish the entire decree, behold, nothing withstands repentance, as written there?:). And in the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah 17a): "Great is repentance, for it tears up the final decree of a person.":, And according to the resolution of the Gemara: "This applies to an individual, that applies to a community,", it is difficult, for surely Adam the First, who encompassed all future souls, surely his repentance was equivalent to the repentance of an entire community!, And according to the Gemara's alternative resolution further on, distinguishing a decree accompanied by an oath, it is even more difficult, for originally there was no judicial decree, only a warning; )., and when he sinned in the tenth hour he was judged in the eleventh hour, as written in Sanhedrin (38a), there occurred immediately the final decree that he live one thousand years, and certainly Adam and Eve performed complete repentance, since otherwise they would have died immediately within that day; so why did their repentance not avail to cancel the decree entirely? ): However, we find in Midrash Rabbah (Parashah 19): "' – '. "'And I did eat (ve-akhalti)' is not written here, but rather 'and I will eat (va-okhel)'— I ate and I shall eat.", And we must understand: how could it be conceivable that Adam the First would assert that he would eat again, transgressing the command of the Omnipresent?, Yet the Midrash Rabbah seemingly disagrees with the Zohar Chadash that they repented,:. for the Midrash Rabbah concludes: "He was not expelled from Gan Eden until he blasphemed and reviled.": And it is brought in Bereishit Rabbah (Parashah 21) that the Holy One opened for him a gate of repentance: "' ', "'And now'—'now' denotes nothing other than repentance, etc.,'. yet he said 'lest (pen),' and pen signifies refusal.", However, it remains difficult according to the Zohar Chadash that they repented, why is it written "va- okhel" and not "ve-akhalti", as the Midrash Rabbah notes? However, the inner essence of the serpent's instigation is. that the serpent injected into his heart the capacity to feel bodily gratification.:, And it is written: "And the tree of life in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and evil";. and we have explained that this spiritual power of the tree of life and tree of knowledge was present within all trees of the garden., And had he tasted of the tree of life—meaning detached from bodily pleasure—, then he would have felt in all his eating from any tree he consumed the sanctity of the tree of life, which is eating in supreme holiness,: as it is said: "Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine that I have mingled"—, the bread of the Written Torah and the wine of the Oral Torah, ). as written in the holy Zohar (Part III, 271b)., However, once he ate of the tree of knowledge, meaning that he experienced bodily gratification within eating, through this an intermingling was wrought, and in all eatings that he consumed, he tasted of the tree of knowledge of good and evil through physical pleasure,. and this constitutes the instigation of the serpent. ): And this explains what they taught in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 24) and Tikkunei Zohar Chadash: ": The Rabbis said: The tree from which Adam the First ate was wheat;: and some Rabbis said: it was a grapevine;: and others said: it was a fig tree;. yet they did not disagree in their words, for all is truth, etc.", And it is difficult: how can all be truth and "both these and those are the words of the living God" in a factual historical dispute? ).

topics.h: Just as Rabbenu Tam found difficult regarding the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi
topics.en: Yehoshua on the date of Creation (Rosh Hashanah 27a, Tosafot)., However, according to what has been explained, it is resolved:, for all is truth, since whatever he ate he tasted the flavor of the mixture of good and evil,. only that the dispute is concerning where the initial corruption began. And our father Jacob, peace be upon him, was like Adam the First prior to the corruption,. who had no experience whatsoever of physical pleasure. ): And as Rashi wrote (Vayetzei, from Bereishit Rabbah): ", "Does not even the lightest of men refrain from speaking thus? Rather, solely to raise offspring did he say so,", meaning that he knew nothing of bodily lust, desiring only to bring forth righteous issue,:. and therefore felt no shame in this, just like Adam prior to the fall, concerning whom it is written: "and they were not ashamed." ): And therefore our father Jacob did not die (Ta'anit 5b);,": )., and likewise Rabbeinu HaKadosh who said: "I did not enjoy even with my small finger," as written in Ketubot (104a),:, it is taught in the Gemara: every twilight he would return home, and it is brought in Sefer Chasidim (section 1129) that he would discharge his household in Kiddush,:, unlike other deceased, concerning whom it is written: "among the dead, free";:. and it is brought that 'HaNasi' is an acronym for: he is a spark of our father Jacob., And this was present in Jacob who was born thus like Adam prior to the corruption, and as will unfold in the future when the Holy One brings the evil inclination and slaughters it, as written in the Gemara;. and likewise Rabbeinu HaKadosh who was a spark from the soul of our father Jacob, peace be upon him. However, within the rest of mankind there already exists the instigation of the serpent to feel bodily gratification. ): And on this they said (Midrash Rabbah, Tazria, according to the text of the Yalkut): ". "Even if one were the most pious among the pious, it is impossible that there not be in him some aspect of iniquity." )., And regarding Yishai father of David, Scripture explicitly implies that he died solely by the instigation of the serpent, as written in Shabbat (55a),. which means the involuntary sensation of bodily pleasure.:, And this is what is meant by: "And she gave me of the tree, and I ate / will eat,": which he uttered in the bitterness of his heart, exonerating himself:, what could I do, since I have already tasted of the tree of knowledge of good and evil, and henceforth whatever I eat I will feel within it bodily pleasure, which is the mixture of good and evil, so what could I do?, And furthermore, to overcome his base inclination one also requires the help of the Holy One, blessed be He, for without His help, man cannot prevail over it;, and as written, to eradicate the evil inclination entirely will happen only in the future when the Holy One slaughters it;,":. and this is why he said: "And I will eat further"—for I will inevitably eat again., And for this reason, even though the repentance of Adam and Eve availed, to prolong their days to nearly one thousand years—the day of the Holy One, blessed be He—, nonetheless to abolish the decree entirely was impossible; since there exists the mixture and one will feel physical pleasure,. death is indispensable to separate the good from evil, so that only good remains.
