And on Shabbat, even bodily enjoyment is sanctified in holiness, and causes no prosecution of the evil inclination, as the Ari of blessed memory wrote;, and particularly one who merits the higher Shabbat where the evil inclination is cleared away, as written in the Tikkunim,. just as will be in the World to Come. ).: And concerning this they taught (Shabbat 118a): ". "If Israel were to preserve two Sabbaths according to their laws, they would be immediately redeemed.". Two Sabbaths signify the higher Shabbat and the lower Shabbat., And even though the world is judged according to its majority, nonetheless every individual soul, when preserving Shabbat according to its halakhic sanctity, is able to merit the higher Shabbat, and be completely redeemed in his individual soul, and nullify the decree of death entirely, so that passing will be merely like sleep and awakening,. inasmuch as he merits that the evil inclination is cleared away completely.,

sections.title: Shabbat as Hashem’s Gift of Sanctification
sections.summary: The gift of Shabbat reveals a holiness bestowed upon Israel and shared through Moshe Rabbeinu.

topics.h: The Good Gift Hidden in Hashem’s Treasury
topics.en: In the Gemara (Shabbat 10b): ", "'To know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you,' etc., a good gift I have in My treasure-house, and Shabbat is its name,. and I wish to give it to Israel., One must understand: what is this 'good gift'?, If it refers to the mitzvah of Shabbat,. behold, they were already commanded concerning it!: And as for that which Rashi wrote in his commentary: ", "to make known that I desire to sanctify them,", this also requires understanding, for within every commandment there is sanctity, just as the Sages formulated the text of the blessing over the commandments: ", "Who has sanctified us with His commandments,": and they instituted this based upon what is stated: ". "'and perform all My commandments, and be holy unto your God.'" And once they were commanded regarding Shabbat,. there is automatically sanctity within it.: Rather, the concept of the 'good gift' is that which is stated: ", "'And the children of Israel shall observe the Sabbath, to make the Sabbath,' that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave the power to Israel. to introduce sanctity into the Sabbath. For this reason, Shabbat is termed the first among the sacred convocations: that is mentioned in Parashat Emor: ". "'and on the seventh day is a holy convocation.', Namely, that apart from the sanctity that is permanently fixed and established from Hashem, blessed be He, Hashem, blessed be He, gave the power to Israel. that they should introduce sanctity into the Sabbath., And this is what is meant by 'to make the day of Shabbat,'. and this is the essence of a gift—that it becomes truly one's own. ): And in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 6):: Three things were given as a gift to the world:,, the Torah, the celestial luminaries, and the rains,. and it cites verses wherein the terminology of 'giving' is written regarding them., Afterwards it cites six additional things wherein the language of 'giving' is written, and these six things are added each by a different authority,. while the primary three things were enumerated by Rabbi Yosi., And one must understand:, since the primary derivation is from the fact that the term 'giving' is written, why did Rabbi Yosi enumerate only three things, and afterwards each Sage added one further item?, However, the matter is according to what we have explained: that when the angels grew envious over the giving of the Torah:, and said: 'Set Your glory upon the heavens,' they were not envious over the Written Torah, which is written and laid out,. and they too are able to see it and study it. Rather, the core of the envy was over the Oral Torah, which was given over to Israel, to the extent that they proclaimed: 'It is not in heaven!' )::, and the Holy One, blessed be He, said: 'My children have triumphed over Me' (Bava Metzia 59b), and likewise: 'Who shall arbitrate? Rabbah bar Nachmani!'. and over this the angels were envious. And this is the essence of a gift—that it was given completely and entirely unto Israel. And this was the intent in Rabbi Yosi counting three gifts, corresponding to the first three Supernal Sefirot (Keter, Chokhmah, Binah),. from where the flow of the Oral Torah emanates., And he counted the celestial luminaries, for the Oral Torah corresponds to the Primordial Light, since the five times 'light' written in the passage of 'Let there be light'. correspond to the Five Books of the Torah, as written in Bereishit Rabbah., And the utterance 'Let there be light' corresponds to Chokhmah (Wisdom), according to what is stated in the Gemara that 'Bereishit' is also an utterance, and the Primordial Light was concealed for those who toil in the Oral Torah, ), as written (Tanchuma, Noach 3), and it is what shines from the supernal crown of the letter Yod which hints to Ayin (Nothingness), ), as written (Zohar Part III, 65b), unto the letter Yod which alludes to Chokhmah,. and this explains why he enumerated the luminaries. Likewise, the rains refer also to the Oral Torah,. and correspond to Binah (Understanding)., And the concept of the rains is based on what the holy Maggid of Kozhnitz of blessed memory wrote, ).: that what our Sages said (Ta'anit 7a), regarding the praises of the day of rain, that it is greater than the resurrection of the dead, and that it is greater than the day the Torah was given, ", asking 'which is dependent on which? etc.,'. all refers to Shemini Atzeret. ) And it is based on what is written in Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 13), that it is the flowing wellspring of Torah, namely to merit the light of the Oral Torah, to understand one matter from within another matter,. and discern how it is enfolded within the Written Torah., And this is termed 'rains', for it is overtly recognized as descending from the heavens, and not like dew to which the Oral Torah is compared, wherein it appears to the Sages that they are innovating in their hearts from their own intellect, when in truth they are the words of the living God. shining into their heart like dew whose descent from heaven is imperceptible., And 'the wellspring of the Torah' means that it is visibly seen to stem from heaven through the Written Torah, like the Oral Torah of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him,. which is Halakhah transmitted to Moses from Sinai., And 'Torah' likewise refers to the Oral Torah,. and corresponds to Keter Elyon (the Supreme Crown), which is the supernal dew of the Ancient One. And Rabbi Yosi counted Torah first,:, and cited from the verse: 'And He gave unto Moses,' for that was still prior to the sin of the Golden Calf, and all of the Oral Torah was enfolded within the First Tablets, and this was given unto Moses our teacher as a gift, and he acted with a generous eye and gave it to Israel, ).: as written (Nedarim 38a)., And this corresponds to Da'at, which is the inner dimension of Keter Elyon, which is the specific attribute and portion of the Oral Torah of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, and this is Halakhah transmitted to Moses from Sinai which he grasped through his profound analysis, and gave it to Israel as established rulings without an explicit rationale, for human beings lack the capacity to comprehend the ultimate reason for a Halakhah le-Moshe mi-Sinai, )'., as Rashi wrote (Gittin 14a, s.v. ke-hilkhata),:. and this is what the Gemara meant there: 'merely through sharp analysis.', Namely, that which he attained of halakhot through his sharp analysis, this was gifted to Moses, and he gave them to Israel as Halakhah le-Moshe mi-Sinai;. and it is named so because he knew explicitly that it was directly from Sinai just like the Written Torah. And this was by virtue of his attribute of Da'at, which is the inner essence of Keter Elyon., And this explains why Rabbi Yosi enumerated these three things,. representing the dynamic power of the Oral Torah granted unto Israel., And afterwards each Sage added one further item, and these are six things corresponding to the six lower sefirotic attributes, and all of them were given as a gift unto Israel,. who are the Congregation of Israel corresponding to the attribute of Malchut., And similarly the matter of Shabbat being a 'good gift',. means that which He gave to Israel the power to infuse sanctity into Shabbat.,":, And as is stated: 'Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it,' 'Observe it to sanctify it,' and this is through that which He imparted holiness into Israel,. and thereby they have the power to infuse holiness into the festivals. ): And as written in the Midrash (Shemot Rabbah, Parashah 15): ", "'And if a non-sacred vessel when filled from the holy becomes consecrated,. how much more so Israel, who are holy and sanctify the new month!' And likewise the sanctity that Israel introduces into Shabbat, for which reason it is also termed a holy convocation,. is by virtue of the holiness that Hashem, blessed be He, placed within them.:, And this is what Scripture states: 'To know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you,'—, a good gift I have in My treasure- house and Shabbat is its name, namely the holiness permanently fixed and established from Hashem, blessed be He, " 'and I wish to give it to Israel'—. that the power be given unto Israel to introduce sanctity into Shabbat. And with what does one sanctify it?, With food, with drink, and with clean garments, ). as written (Midrash Rabbah, Nasso, Parashah 10).,

sections.title: The Gift of Rest and the Inner Holiness of Shabbat
sections.summary: Shabbat rest is more than cessation from work: it is a revelation of divine holiness within Israel.

topics.h: Rest as the Expression of Inward Sanctity
topics.en: A day of rest and holiness You have given unto Your people.": In the Gemara: ". "'A good gift I have in My treasure-house and Shabbat is its name,' etc." And we explained that the 'good gift' is that Hashem gave power unto Israel. to introduce sanctity into Shabbat by placing holiness within them. However, according to this, the phrasing of the Gemara 'and Shabbat is its name' is not precise. And it is possible that it refers to the rest that He gave to Israel,. that there be spiritual tranquility in the heart. And this is why it says 'and Shabbat is its name'—. an expression of tranquility and rest. ), And it is based on what is written (in the holy Zohar Part I, 48b) which expounds the verse 'on the day Hashem gives you rest from your sorrow, etc.'. as referring to the Sabbath day., And this is derived because it is written 'on the day He gives rest' and not merely 'when He gives rest',. and from this it expounded that it refers to the Sabbath day which is a day of rest. And it cannot be conceived that a person should forget all his agony, even while he is still in the midst of harsh labor, unless Hashem, blessed be He, grants rest in the heart as a direct gift, just as He rested from all His work. For He had satisfaction on Shabbat from all Creation, even from that which appears as the opposite of good, as Bereishit Rabbah expounds on the verse: ", "'And God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good,'. so does He place within the heart of Israel tranquility from all opposite adversity as well. And at times it could be imagined that through eating, drinking, and indulging in Shabbat, )., and fixing one's meal over wine, as written (Berakhot 42a),. he drinks and forgets his poverty and all of his agony.:, And regarding this Scripture states: 'To know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you, a good gift I have in My treasure-house and Shabbat is its name,. and I wish to give it unto Israel.', Namely, that this tranquility comes about because holiness was placed within them, in that they recognize that everything is from Hashem, blessed be He,. and He is always watching for the ultimate good., And through this he possesses tranquility from all distress, " from 'your sorrow and your turmoil'—, namely from the depression of the evil inclination, ).: as is expounded (Temurah 16a): " that it may not grieve me'— lest the evil inclination prevent me from reviewing my learning, etc.;", ). and the turmoil of the evil inclination, over which one must agitate the good inclination (Berakhot 5a); " and 'from the hard labor which was worked upon you'—, that even while one is still immersed in the arduous labor, he will nonetheless have tranquility. because he recognizes that it is from Hashem, blessed be He, and is for the good.: And this is what we recite in the blessing of Me'ein Sheva: ", "and grants rest in holiness to a people laden with delight,". for the tranquility arises through the holiness that He places within the heart of Israel.: And in the blessing preceding the Shema: ", "Praise, glory, greatness, and honor shall they render unto God, King, Former of all,", for over this they render unique praise, in that He is 'Former of all,' which points even to the opposite of good,. as they formulated euphemistically in place of 'and Creator of evil,' reciting 'all.' ", "'Who bequeaths rest unto His people Israel in His holiness on the holy Sabbath day,' for He grants rest through the holiness that shines into the heart of Israel,. and not through wine and the like. ):. And this He gives unto Israel as an inheritance and heritage that knows no interruption (Bava Batra 129b).: And this is what we recite in Kiddush: ", "'and His holy Sabbath He bequeathed to us in love and favor, etc., You bequeathed unto us,'. for the tranquility He bequeathed to Israel through love and favor., Such that a Jew has tranquility amidst all that passes over him, knowing and recognizing that everything is from Hashem, blessed be He, Who watches for good, ". 'and as a father delights in the son.',:, And so in prayer: 'Unto Israel Your people You gave it in love, to the seed of Jacob,', for through the holiness of Jacob they merited an uninterrupted heritage, whose attribute is 'truth to Jacob,'. and 'the lip of truth shall be established forever.':. And on Yom Tov we say: 'and Your holy appointed seasons in gladness and joy You bequeathed unto us.', For joy can potentially degenerate into frivolity;, and only because Hashem grants joy and gladness in the heart as an uninterrupted heritage, thereby the joy is sanctified in holiness, ","'. 'Rejoice in Hashem,' 'Let Israel rejoice in its Maker.':, And as we explained regarding the verse: 'and you shall be solely joyful,', that it is a promise that joy will be in holiness with measured restraint, ",. 'solely' (akh) being an exclusionary term, ensuring it is not a frivolous joy.: And in prayer, which is a plea for mercy, we beseech: ", 'And bequeath unto us, Hashem our God, in love and favor Your holy Sabbath,',:. even though in Kiddush we render thanksgiving over the past: 'and Your holy Sabbath in love and favor He bequeathed / You bequeathed unto us.' Why then do we plead for this?, It is understandable regarding holiness, where we recite in Kiddush 'Who has sanctified us', and in the prayer we say 'Sanctify us with Your commandments'—for what reason? ):, Because it is an appeal for mercy, as written in the Gemara (Pesachim 117b), this is not difficult, for in holiness there are numerous ascending levels,:)., as written (Chullin 7a): 'Israel are holy,',):, and nevertheless Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi was termed 'our holy teacher' (Shabbat 118b), having been holy of holies, and yet Rabbi said concerning Rabbi Yosi that he is like non-sacred dust compared to holy of holies relative to Rabbi Yosi, ), as written (Yerushalmi Gittin 6:7 end); therefore it is fitting to pray for higher holiness. even while giving thanks over the past 'Who has sanctified us.' However, to plead 'And bequeath unto us, Hashem our God, in love and favor Your holy Sabbath', after having already given thanks over the past 'He bequeathed / You bequeathed unto us'. is difficult to understand., Yet in truth, within the tranquility possessed by Israel there are also many gradations, and each individual, according to what he merits, feels the rest and inner tranquility in the heart on Shabbat;. and over this we pray 'and bequeath unto us, etc.' Yet nonetheless, every single Jew merits tranquility on Shabbat,. and this is the good gift of 'and Shabbat is its name.', And over this we give thanks in Kiddush, and this is 'A day of rest and holiness You gave unto Your people' as a gift,. that the rest be enveloped in holiness through the holiness of Shabbat. And we enumerate all expressions of rest in the prayer corresponding to our father Jacob, peace be upon him, who merited the fundamental essence of rest, ): concerning whom Shabbat observance is stated in 'and he encamped' (as written in Bereishit Rabbah): " a rest of love and magnanimity,' as stated; " a rest of truth and faith'— ),: based on what is written (Zohar Part III, 230a): ", 'He is Truth and she is Faith,' for our father Jacob, peace be upon him, recognized the divine Unity in the attribute of Truth: ", 'You are He before the world was created, You are He after the world was created,',:. he being the Chariot to the Tetragrammaton which signifies this: Was, Is, and Will Be. And his children, the Congregation of Israel in this world, merit solely through the divine Name Adonai, and attain rest through faith; " 'a complete rest that You desire'—, that rest be rooted in His holiness,:, as written: 'Your children shall recognize and know that from You is their rest,':, and as written: 'Who bequeaths unto His people Israel in His holiness, etc.,' " and upon their rest they shall sanctify Your Name'—. as written 'praise, glory, etc.,' and as we have explained.: And afterwards we pray: 'And bequeath unto us, Hashem our God, etc., and let them rest upon it, etc.', upon the qualitative rung of this rest, to experience in each instance greater tranquility,. since there are numerous gradations in this, as stated.,

sections.title: Passing Through Waters and Fire with Hashem
sections.summary: The promise of divine accompaniment illuminates the passage from fear and spiritual danger toward protection.

topics.h: Divine Presence in the Waters and Fire of Exile
topics.en: Even though I walk, etc., I will fear no evil, for You are with me.': This is what Scripture declares in the Haftarah: ", "'When you pass through the waters, I am with you; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow you;. when you walk through fire, you shall not be scorched, etc.': And one must understand: does anyone literally pass through water and fire? And when Israel traversed the Sea and the Jordan, they crossed through a miracle upon dry land!, And likewise Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah were cast into the fire and did not walk through fire!:, Rather, Scripture alludes to the two impure husks (kelipot): Esau and Ishmael,. which are the generative roots of all seventy kelipot., And corresponding to water—the holy emanations of Lovingkindness (Chasadim)—, there exists parallel to this the kelipah of Ishmael,. which is the lust and physical appetite of this world, the 'raging waters.', And corresponding to fire—the holy emanations of Might (Gevurot)—, there exists parallel to this the kelipah of Esau,. which is jealousy and murder. And regarding this the prophet stated: that Hashem, blessed be He, will rescue Israel from these two kelipot:, that the raging waters shall not overflow you,. and the fire of Esau shall not scorch you.:, And Scripture states: 'For I am Hashem your God, etc., your Savior,' ): in the manner of what is written in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah, Parashah 21): ", 'My salvation'—on Yom Kippur,. which is the forgiveness of iniquities to repair the past after one has stumbled. " I gave Egypt as your ransom'—, stated in the past tense, for it refers to the exile of Egypt, wherein what Hashem placed in the heart of Pharaoh and his people to pursue Israel, even though they had already dispatched them and pleaded with them to depart, was because there still remained an accusatory indictment against Israel,: as stated in the Mekhilta: "', 'And the water was a wall (chomah) unto them'—written defectively without a vav (chemah),. indicating that supernal wrath was stirred against them. ) And in the Midrash (Shemot Rabbah, Parashah 21):. that there was an indictment against them at the Sea: 'These are idolaters, etc.', And for this, Hashem placed in the heart of Pharaoh that they pursue Israel, and the judgment fell that the Egyptians were drowned in the sea, because Hashem clarified that all allegations held against Israel, derived solely through the ambient evil present in Egypt,. and from that they introduced the 'leaven in the dough' into the hearts of Israel as well.:. And this is why Scripture states: 'I gave Egypt as your ransom.':, And afterwards Scripture states: 'Cush and Seba in your stead,' ), which appears to allude to the war of Zerach the Cushite against Asa (II Chronicles 14), wherein an army of a million warriors is mentioned,. and we find no such massive opposing force elsewhere. And we have already explained that a nation's military power stems solely from their possessing an accusatory claim, Heaven forbid, that there exists within Israel a trace of their specific kelipah,. and through that leverage they become empowered., And the kelipah of Cush is the blemish of the Covenant (immorality),:, originating from Ham who cohabited in the Ark (Sanhedrin 108b) and was stricken in his skin, and this was a breach of the Covenant since cohabitation was forbidden to them in the Ark,. and there is also an opinion that he castrated/sodomized him., And Cush was the firstborn of Ham, and Seba the firstborn of Cush;, and just as in the realm of holiness the holy root rests in the firstborn of Israel, so among them the prime defilement is concentrated in the firstborn;. and for this reason Cush and Seba are the generative root of the kelipah of covenantal blemish., And presumably there was then an indictment against Israel in this realm, and they were aroused to wage war against Israel;: and Asa prayed: ", 'Help us, Hashem our God, for upon You we rely, and in Your Name we have come, etc.', and then they were slain in a plague and became a ransom for Israel, in that Hashem clarified that from the kelipah residing in them, the leaven in the dough had penetrated into the hearts of Israel;:. and this is what is stated: 'Cush and Seba in your stead.':, And Scripture says: 'Since you were precious in My sight, you have been honored,' ): and it is stated (Zohar Chadash, Balak): ", "'It should have said "you are precious" (yakar); what is "you became precious" (yakarta)? It implies that he made himself precious through his own effort, etc.,, and I have loved you, for there is no divine love for any man in the world except for one who repents of his sins, etc., yet what shall I do, seeing that permission was given, etc.,' " and I will give Adam in your stead'—do not read Adam, but Edom;, and so it expounded 'and nations' (u-le'umim) as referring to Esau,:. mirroring the verse: 'and the one nation shall be stronger than the other nation.', And this is stated regarding the ultimate future, for so does Hashem prepare for every penitent a soul-ransom, from that which exists parallel to him in the kelipah, in the manner of what the holy Ari of blessed memory wrote:, on the teaching: 'he receives his portion and the portion of his counterpart, etc.,'. meaning the one standing opposite him who contains a holy spark pertaining to his soul.:, And this is what Scripture states: 'When you pass through the waters, I am with you, etc.,' " and 'when you walk through fire, you shall not be scorched'—. and it is not written here 'I am with you.', And this is because from the kelipah of Esau, which is murder and anger, nothing whatever will remain in the ultimate future,:. as it is stated: 'And there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau.':, And Scripture states: 'you shall not be scorched, neither shall the flame burn upon you,':. based upon what is stated: 'and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble.' ", 'It shall not burn upon you'—yet they will consume Esau in fire,:, and as it is stated: 'For behold, the day comes, burning as an oven, and all the proud shall be stubble, and the day that comes shall burn them up, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch,'. and this is 'there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau.' And their evil inclination is the very fire of Gehenna, and it consumes them,: as stated in the Midrash: ", "A fire that emerges from the body of the wicked and consumes them;:. what is the reason? For it is written: 'Your breath, as fire, shall devour you.'". And this is the fire of the evil inclination. And this is 'it shall not burn upon you'—yet it will burn within them., In contrast regarding the kelipah of Ishmael, ),: for it is brought in the holy Zohar (Part III, 138a): ", "The evil inclination is necessary for the world, etc.,. for without the evil inclination there would be no passionate joy in Torah study.', And even in the ultimate future this drive and passion will remain,. only that it will be purified of its wickedness.:, Concerning this Scripture states: 'When you pass through the waters, I am with you,'. for Hashem will refine it so that all passion is channeled into the delight of the Torah. ", 'And through the rivers, they shall not overflow you'— referring to the raging waters,. only that through this he will merit words of Torah., And so too King David, peace be upon him, concerning whom it was written that he stumbled in this matter, which was attributed to him solely to teach the path of repentance, )., that if an individual sins, etc. (Avodah Zarah 5a),:, proclaimed: 'Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil,' meaning this specific blemish which is titled 'evil' )., in the holy Zohar (Part I, 219b) and in the Gemara (Niddah 13a); " for You are with me'—:. mirroring the verse: 'When you pass through the waters, I am with you.' " Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me'— ).: and this reflects what we find (Sanhedrin 107a): ", 'Accept afflictions upon yourself,' and this is 'Your rod' when He raises the rod of chastisement; " ", 'and Your staff'—that out of this a support is fashioned, )., which is expounded as referring to words of Torah, as stated (Chagigah 14a), ". 'they comfort me.': And the ultimate fruit of this will be: ", 'and I shall dwell in the house of Hashem for length of days,': for this was his entire yearning: ", 'that I may dwell in the house of Hashem all the days of my life,'. for on Shabbat all Israel dwell in the house of Hashem, in the palace of the King.:. And concerning this he declared: 'One thing have I asked, etc., that I may dwell in the house of Hashem all the days of my life.', And over this he said 'for You are with me,', that from the evil inclination there shall be made a passionate longing for Torah, ". 'and I shall dwell in the house of Hashem for length of days.',

sections.title: The Patriarchs and the Gathering of Israel
sections.summary: The three patriarchal attributes and the three Shabbat meals point toward the unification of Israel.

topics.h: The Three Patriarchs and the Gathering of the Dispersed
topics.en: May the Rock command His lovingkindness, etc., ". from four directions to be gathered unto Him.": In the Haftarah it is stated: ", "'Fear not, for I am with you;. from the east I will bring your seed, and from the west I will gather you., I will say to the north: Give up; and to the south: Hold not back, etc.'. He enumerated all four directions., For in holiness they correspond to the four supports of the Chariot, which are the three Patriarchs and King David, peace be upon him, who is the fourth support of the Chariot, ),. as stated in the holy Zohar (Part I, 248b).: And parallel to this, there exist in impurity three kelipot:,. envy, lust, and honor.: And the sanctity of the Patriarchs stands counter to these three kelipot:, for Abraham our father, peace be upon him, his attribute is Lovingkindness and love of creatures, and he stands opposite the kelipah of Esau, which is envy and murder, he being a hater of creatures, ): as stated (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 63): ". "hatred of human blood in his body.", And Isaac our father, peace be upon him, his attribute is the Awe of Isaac,. counter to the kelipah of Ishmael, which is lust and illicit desires. And Jacob our father, peace be upon him, is the middle bar, which integrates the holiness of Abraham and Isaac, and he stands against the kelipah of Amalek, which is the kelipah of the dog, ), as stated in the holy Zohar (Part II, 65b), that it is the inner essence of ox and donkey, the kelipot of Esau and Ishmael;: and the inner essence of "shor" ( and "chamor" (: -, Vav (6 =, Mem-Vav (46 =, in gematria equals "kelev" (52 =,, and he is a barking dog, brazen hounds, for at the Exodus from Egypt 'peoples heard and trembled,'. yet he stood to battle them, paying no heed to any of this., And the kelipah of Amalek is the kelipah of arrogance, ): and so it is explicitly stated in the Midrash (Nasso, Parashah 10): "' A man's pride shall bring him low'—this is Amalek, etc.";, and opposite him stands Jacob our father, peace be upon him, who was lowly in his own eyes,:, as is stated: 'How shall Jacob stand? For he is small,':, and said regarding himself: 'From whence (Me-Ayin / the Nothingness) shall my help come,' ). as stated (Bereishit Rabbah, beginning of Parashat Vayeitzei)., And furthermore there is a fourth kelipah, and that is heresy;, and opposite it stands Gog and Magog, who will gather from all seventy nations, )70 = ', which in gematria equals 'Gog u-Magog' (70), and he comes 'against Hashem and against His anointed,' ).: for regarding all other nations they said in the Gemara (Menachot 110a end):, that 'they call Him the God of gods,', whereas he will assemble all nations against Hashem and His anointed,. and he will arise at the very end, when the Messiah has already arrived., And opposite him in holiness stand King David, peace be upon him, and the Messiah, who will be David himself,:, he being the Chariot for the attribute of Malchut: 'she is Faith,'. and they correspond to the four directions of the world. ),: And Shabbat, concerning which it is brought in the holy Zohar (Part II, 204a): " ", 'Shabbat—the letter Shin is the mystery of the three Patriarchs,' etc., corresponding to the three sanctities of Shabbat,. which are the sanctities of the three meals., And in the Third Meal, which corresponds to Jacob our father, peace be upon him,. Israel merit the holiness of Jacob our father, peace be upon him., And afterwards on Saturday night, which is the first night of the week,:, concerning which it is written: 'and the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters,': and in Bereishit Rabbah: 'this is the spirit of the King Messiah'; ". 'the waters'—in the merit of repentance, which is compared to water. ):, And David is 'the man who established the yoke' of repentance (Moed Katan 16b), and the Messiah will be the unique individual who repents ):, for whose sake the entire world is forgiven (Yoma 86b),. for he will inspire an awakening of repentance throughout the whole world, within all Israel., And on Saturday night is the feast of King David, the Messiah, and then will be the completion of the rectification from all blemish. arising from the kelipot of Esau and Ishmael, which encompass all kelipot. " And the goat shall bear upon itself all their iniquities'—, the iniquities of the simple one (Tam / Jacob), ). as stated (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 65).: Therefore we recite at the Third Meal: ", 'May the Rock command His lovingkindness, to gather His congregations,. from four directions to be gathered unto Him.', And through the observance of Shabbat, the son of David arrives immediately, ): as stated (Shemot Rabbah, Parashah 25):, for it is said: 'Today, if you will hear His voice,'. and Shabbat is weighed equivalent to all the commandments.,

sections.title: Prayer at an Auspicious Time
sections.summary: David HaMelech’s prayer joins supplication for true salvation with the discipline of blessing and adversity.

topics.h: What to Request During an Auspicious Time
topics.en: And as for me, may my prayer come to You, Hashem, at an acceptable time.', King David, peace be upon him, instructed us:, when we pray during an acceptable time, for what should we pray?:, That the prayer be: 'O God, in the abundance of Your lovingkindness,', for since we can effect abundant lovingkindness during an acceptable time, we beseech that within the abundance of kindness He bestows upon us, there be also the attribute of containment/restraint (tsimtsum),. which is denoted by the Name Elohim, the Awe of Isaac., Namely, that the lovingkindness should not impair one's service of Hashem, blessed be He,: just as King Solomon, peace be upon him, prayed: ",. "'Poverty and wealth give me not, lest I be sated and deny.' ):: And so our Sages of blessed memory instructed us (Bava Batra 25b): ", "He who desires to become wealthy, let him turn north," for one who desires wealth, and that this wealth should not compromise his service of Hashem, blessed be He, must hold fast to the attribute of reverence, the Awe of Isaac;, and this is 'let him turn north'—the northern direction, the dimension of Gevurah, ". 'and from the north comes gold.' " Answer me in the truth of Your salvation'—, that the salvation be established upon the path of truth, ", and 'the lip of truth shall be established forever,',. that it endure for eternal worlds, for the World that is entirely boundless. However, whatever lacks the quality of truth— ", 'a false tongue is but for a moment,'. for all transient life of this world is termed 'for a moment.', Therefore we recite this verse during Minchah on Shabbat, for it is taught in the holy Zohar that the Will of all Wills (Ra'ava de-Ra'avin) is present then,. and one can effect all divine goodness, abundant lovingkindness.:. And upon this we plead: 'O God, in the abundance of Your lovingkindness,' as noted above.:, And regarding the blessings it is written: 'And all these blessings shall come upon you, and overtake you,': and they cite in the name of our master Rabbi Bunim, of blessed memory for the World to Come: ", 'and they shall overtake you in your place,' meaning that you not be altered through the bounties, kindnesses, and blessings;, and this is that there be 'Elohim in the abundance of Your kindness,'. that they forget not that it is Hashem your God Who gives you strength to acquire wealth. And so we pray in the supplication of Rav: following the ten expressions of life: ", 'a life wherein You fulfill all our hearts' desires for good,' ): for so we find in Midrash Rabbah (Bemidbar, Parashah 1):, that regarding Israel Scripture speaks conditionally, saying 'according to all his ways, whose heart You know,'. that if it were fitting for him, He would grant it to him, etc. And this signifies likewise that the bounty he requests should not harm him. ):: And on Shabbat we find (Shabbat 118b):, regarding one who delights in Shabbat, that they give him the desires of his heart,. and 'for good' is not appended.: And the reason is: on Shabbat, everything a Jew requests is inherently for good,. and will not harm him. ): And this clarifies what is brought (Tanchuma, this parashah):, that one does not fast on Friday, for the honor of Shabbat surpasses a thousand fasts;, because honoring Shabbat is biblical while a fast is rabbinic,. and honoring Shabbat comes and overrides it, see there., And seemingly the second rationale is sufficient,. that biblical honor of Shabbat overrides a rabbinic fast., However, because he prefaced that the core purpose of a fast is forgiveness and mercy, and he might come to withhold from honoring Shabbat, and if so, what does it avail that Shabbat honor is biblical, when we still require forgiveness and mercy?, And to this he stated that honoring Shabbat surpasses a thousand fasts, and through honoring Shabbat he can attain all the desires of his heart, and that everything will be for the good, and he no longer requires penitential fasts and pleas for mercy;, why then should he withhold from the biblical honor of Shabbat?. and automatically biblical honor of Shabbat comes and overrides the rabbinic fast., And conversely, in the admonitions it is likewise written 'and shall overtake you,': and it appears also in the aforementioned manner:, that he should not be displaced from his spiritual standing through it, ):: along the lines of what is stated (Eruvin 41b):. that there are three things that turn a person away from the mindset of his Creator., And since Hashem sends afflictions solely for our ultimate benefit,:, as is stated: 'As a man chastens his son, etc.', He does not send afflictions that would turn him away from the mindset of his Creator, rather that through the afflictions he should merit eternal life,: ):. as is stated: 'and reproofs of instruction are the way of life' (see Berakhot 5a). And likewise: 'Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me.',

sections.title: Transforming Bitterness and Darkness into Good
sections.summary: Closeness to Hashem makes it possible to discern the hidden good within painful and difficult realities.

topics.h: When Bitterness Is Transformed Through Divine Nearness
topics.en: Even though I walk, etc., I will fear no evil, for You are with me.' From the beginning of the psalm until here: he speaks in the third person: ", "'in green pastures He makes me lie down,' ", 'He leads me,' " He guides me';: and here he begins to speak in direct address: ", "'for You are with me,' ", 'Your rod and Your staff,' ", 'You prepare,' ". 'You anointed.', Namely, King David, peace be upon him, was secure in his soul, that if he should err in anything, he would rectify it immediately, ).: as is stated (Berakhot 19a): ", "'If you saw a Torah scholar who committed a sin, do not harbor doubts behind him,. for he certainly repented.' And then he rectifies so that he can recognize the working of the Creator, blessed be His Name, and can speak in direct address, and it will become better than beforehand, ):: as is stated (there, 34b): ",. "'In the place where penitents stand, completely righteous ones do not stand.', And the concealment exists solely to make it 'very good,' ): as is stated (Tanchuma, this parashah): ", You say it is bad; who can make it good?': The Holy One, blessed be He, said:: Many bitter things I created, and you sweeten them:,. lupine, mustard, caper bush.' Namely, that the penitent is drawn with extra strength, in a single hour and in a single moment cleaving to the Holy One, which we find in Abraham 'elderly, advanced in days,', and he did not enter those supernal days until he aged, ), as stated in the holy Zohar (Part I, 129b),. and this is 'for You are with me.' And King David, peace be upon him, was confident,. that if anything befell him, it would only be wandering in order to sweeten it and make it very good., For all the works of Creation require rectification, ): as is stated (Tanchuma, Tazria 5): ", "'Which work is more praised? The work of flesh and blood; does one eat raw wheat?'. and man through his actions produces fine loaves.' ),: And it is brought in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah, this parashah 3:8): ", "'From the beginning of the world's creation the Holy One foresaw the deeds of the wicked and the deeds of the righteous, etc., yet I do not know in which of them He delights, etc.;:. since it is written: "And God saw the light that it was good"— behold, in the deeds of the righteous He delights, etc.'": And one must understand: how is it possible to imagine that Hashem desires the deeds of the wicked?,", However in truth it is not written 'in the wicked,' but 'in the deeds of the wicked', and when they are rectified through repentance out of love, wherein intentional sins are transformed into merits,: mirroring the creation of the world: ", first darkness and then light, ): as stated (Shabbat 77b) ),: and in the holy Zohar (Part II, 184a): ". "there is no light except that which emerges from darkness, etc.", And in the first utterance darkness is mentioned, for 'He makes darkness His secret place,', since the first utterance corresponds to Keter Elyon, which is intellect concealed from every thought, and from this a person might go astray, Heaven forbid, without seeing and without knowing, since he possesses no grasp or comprehension;. and afterward when he rectifies, it becomes 'very good.':. And this is what is written: 'and I shall be whiter than snow.' And lest you say that Hashem prefers this path—that one bring light out of darkness?: Upon this the Midrash states:. behold, Hashem delights primarily in the deeds of the righteous. ): And as stated (in Tanchuma, this parashah): ", 'That God made man upright,', the Holy One, Who is termed righteous and upright, created man in His image. only so that he be righteous and upright like Him. And why did the Holy One create the evil inclination?, Only in order to sweeten it and overcome it,:. and as is stated: 'with all your heart'—with both your inclinations, the good and the evil., And through Shabbat,: wherein it is written: 'And God saw everything that He had made, and behold, it was very good, and there was evening and there was morning, the sixth day, etc.', everything becomes 'very good,' ) as is expounded (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 9). concerning every opposite of the good, that it too becomes very good. " Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me'—, namely through words of Torah which are titled 'staff', ).: as stated in the Gemara (Chagigah 14a): "',. "'Stay'— these are masters of Scripture; 'staff'—these are masters of Mishnah, etc." " 'You prepare a table before me'—, this too refers to words of Torah, ).: in the manner of what we find (Kiddushin 46b): ", "'Here is a table, and here is meat, and here is a knife, yet we have nothing to eat,'" which means a Mishnah is taught yet one cannot explain it;. and so too halakhic rulings are titled 'Shulchan Arukh' (a set table)., And for the penitent Hashem unlocks the words of Torah that they radiate unto him, for 'there is no light except that which emerges from darkness,'. because through the concealment he caused it to become very good. ". 'For You are with me'—that he is empowered to speak in direct address.: And nevertheless King David, peace be upon him, pleaded: ", 'Only goodness and lovingkindness shall follow me,': returning to speak in the third person: ". 'and I shall dwell in the house of Hashem for length of days.', And as stated in the Midrash, that Hashem delights in the deeds of the righteous, for Hashem God made man upright, to be righteous and upright like Him;, He merely created the deeds of the wicked,, namely the concealment, 'He makes darkness His secret place,' so that if a person should wander in darkness, He can illuminate for him from within the darkness. and sweeten the bitter and the evil.: And nevertheless it is far better: ", 'Only goodness and lovingkindness shall follow me all the days of my life, '. and I shall dwell in the house of Hashem for length of days.',

sections.title: Creation, Divine Peace, and the Rectification of Evil
sections.summary: The sequence of creation and the sanctity of Shabbat culminate in the revelation of peace.

topics.h: The Creation of Darkness and the Making of Peace
topics.en: May He Whose peace it is place upon us blessing and peace.":, It is written: 'Former of light and Creator of darkness, Maker of peace and Creator of evil,. I am Hashem, Who makes all these.', Now behold, the opposite of light is darkness, and the opposite of evil is good,:, and Scripture ought to have said: 'Maker of good'; so why use the phrasing 'Maker of peace and Creator of evil'? Furthermore, we do not find during the creation of the world the creation of 'evil';, for darkness is at least mentioned in the utterance of Bereishit,. yet evil is not mentioned., And so our master Rabbi Ber (the Maggid of Mezeritch) of blessed memory questioned in Rimzei Torah: that in Creation nothing is mentioned except 'good' and 'very good,', until the incident of the sin,:. wherein it is written: 'the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil.': And the Men of the Great Assembly formulated: ", 'Maker of peace and Creator of all,' ):. as stated (Berakhot 11b)., However, the matter is, that in the first utterance—Bereishit being also an utterance, ). as stated (Rosh Hashanah 32a)—:, it is written: 'unformed and void, and darkness was upon the face of the deep,' (,. (and in the Midrash, Bereishit Rabbah 2:5) these are the deeds of the wicked.:, And that is what is written: 'He makes darkness His secret place,', for the first utterance corresponds to Keter Elyon which is concealed from every thought,. and within this a person can err since he is in darkness., Yet Israel arose in the Primordial Thought, " Bereishit'—for the sake of Israel who are called 'first';,. and when one wanders, he rectifies immediately through the light. And the utterance 'Let there be light' corresponds to the attribute of Chokhmah.,, And it is known that Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah reside in brain, heart, and liver;, and the Neshamah in the brain is not blemished at all,:, as is stated: 'The soul You gave within me is pure,'. and when one blemishes, the Neshamah departs.:', And afterward the third utterance: 'and let it divide the waters from the waters,'. corresponds to the attribute of Binah—the heart., And so within man, the Ruach which resides in the heart,: there exist the two cavities of the heart: ", 'a wise man's heart is at his right, but a fool's heart at his left,', and this is the primary arena of battle, ).: as stated (Berakhot 5a): ". "A person should always stir up the good inclination against the evil inclination.", And since division/strife commenced, it was not said on it 'that it was good' on the second day, ). because the fire of Gehenna was created upon it (Pesachim 54a);, for Gehenna itself was created before the world was created,. only the fire of Gehenna was created on Monday.:, And it is written: 'and their fire shall not be quenched,',", and it is not written 'and the fire of Gehenna', but 'their fire', namely the fire of the evil inclination, which is burning fire, ).: as stated (Kiddushin 81a): ":, It emerged from him like a pillar of fire; he said to it: See that you are fire!" ):: and so we find (Yoma 69b): ":,. "It came forth like a fiery cub from the Holy of Holies; the prophet said: This is the inclination, etc., this is Wickedness." ),: And it is brought (Bereishit Rabbah, this parashah 9:8): ", "'There is neither day nor Gehenna, rather a fire emerges from the body of the wicked and consumes him,:. as it is said: "Your breath, as fire, shall devour you."', And since 'good' is not mentioned regarding the creation of the evil inclination, it is defined as evil, ):: as stated (Shabbat 149b): ", "'Anyone whose fellow is punished through him..':, for it is written: 'To punish the righteous is also not good,', and 'not good' means nothing other than evil,':, and it is written: 'evil shall not dwell with You,':). and as stated (Sukkah 52a): 'The Holy One called it evil.' And this is what is meant by 'and Creator of evil'—. that He created the evil inclination which is termed evil. ).: And opposite this they said (Chagigah 15a): ",, He created righteous ones, He created wicked ones, He created Gan Eden, He created Gehenna";,", he did not say here 'the deeds of the wicked,' but 'wicked ones',. for through the creation of the evil inclination one may stumble into actual wicked deeds.:, Yet from the perspective of Hashem: 'Dominion and fear are with Him,' ),: and they expounded in the holy Zohar (Part III, 12b): ", 'Dominion—this is Michael; and fear—this is Gabriel;, the foundation of this one is of water, and the foundation of that one is of fire, and the Holy One makes peace between them, etc.';, only from man's perspective does primary discord arise, and it is the antithesis of peace,. and this is 'Maker of peace and Creator of evil.', And within this 'that it was good' is not mentioned,. since warfare and strife began. ),: And they said (Bereishit Rabbah 4:6): ", "'And if concerning a division which is for the preservation of the world it was not said "that it was good"',", for the firmament was created to divide between waters and waters, meaning between body and soul, since the physical body is termed 'earth', ):: as is stated (Sanhedrin 91b): "',. "'He calls to the heavens above'—this is the soul; 'and to the earth'—this is the body.":. However from the side of Hashem everything is one: 'He makes peace in His heights.', And evil was created solely in order to sweeten it, ). as stated (in Tanchuma, this parashah). ): And in the holy Zohar (in additions to Parashat Balak, 206b)::, Rabbi Eleazar opened: "'Since you were precious in My sight, you have been honored, etc.', for any man who abides in sin before the Holy One is debased, etc., and after he reconsiders and turns from his sin, now he has become precious through his own effort,:, and the Holy One calls regarding him: "Since you were precious in My sight, you have been honored, etc.",. meaning that afterward through repentance he becomes 'very good.', And like the parable of the Baal Shem Tov concerning a prince redeemed from captivity, who is more precious before the king than the prince who resides beside him constantly;:):. and as they said (Berakhot 34b): 'to the far, and then to the near.' " And I have loved you'—, for the Holy One has no such love for any person in this world except for one who repents of his sin,. and regarding this: 'and I have loved you.', And this is because he is drawn with extra strength, ),. as stated (Zohar Part I, 129b).:, And upon this they stated: 'Maker of peace and Creator of evil,'. this being the division which serves the preservation of the world and its settlement, created on the second day., And after one repents of his sin He makes it good,. as stated in Tanchuma, that He created the evil to sweeten it. ).: And regarding this they taught (Pesachim 54a):,", even though 'that it was good' was not said of it, He integrated it on the sixth day,:, as it is said: 'And God saw everything that He had made, and behold, it was very good,'. in that from every opposite will sprout forth that which is very good. ),: And as stated in the holy Zohar (Part II, 184a): ",. "there is no light except that which emerges from darkness, nor good, etc.": And this is why the Men of the Great Assembly formulated: 'and Creator of all'—, an exalted, euphemistic expression,. for 'all' alludes to the opposite of the good. ":, ):, And on Shabbat, concerning which it is brought: 'Whoever delights in Shabbat is given the desires of his heart' (Shabbat 118b), and it did not specify 'for good', because all desires of a person on Shabbat are inherently for good, ). for the honor of Shabbat surpasses a thousand fasts (Tanchuma, this parashah). ):: And this is what they said in the Gemara (Shabbat 118b): ",. "Whoever observes Shabbat according to its halakhah, even if he served idolatry like the generation of Enosh—he is forgiven."., And behold, they enumerated (Yoma 86a) four categories of atonement, and for severe transgressions—repentance and Yom Kippur suspend and afflictions cleanse;, and one who serves idolatry like the generation of Enosh commits a desecration of the Name, which only death cleanses!, Yet through delighting in Shabbat for the sake of Heaven,. it is superior to a thousand fasts., And in penitential regimens fasts are specified for every sin, this being to shield oneself from afflictions by willingly taking afflictions upon oneself, recording the arrangement of fasts and their precise number for each transgression;, and through the honor of Shabbat he rectifies all, and he is forgiven even if he served idolatry like the generation of Enosh, and they grant him all the desires of his heart,. for everything is for good.: Therefore at the conclusion of Shabbat we pray: ". 'May He place upon us blessing and peace.'

sections.title: Motzaei Shabbat and the Sixfold Language of Salvation
sections.summary: Verses recited around Havdalah carry the blessing of Shabbat into the coming six days.

topics.h: Six Expressions of Salvation at Havdalah
topics.en: Prior to Havdalah we recite verses of salvations, and within them six times the expression of salvation,:, and the sixth: 'I will lift the cup of salvations,', which alludes to a double salvation, wherein a seventh is enfolded; ) and as the Midrash alludes (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 88), in the dream of the chief butler wherein 'cup' is mentioned four times, and parallel to them Hashem gives Israel to drink four cups in the World to Come,. counting there 'I will lift the cup of salvations' as two., And the seven salvations reflect the seven days of the festival of Sukkot, wherein we cry out each day 'Hoshana', and the seventh day is called Hoshana Rabbah, and then is the time of the water libation,:. as it is said: 'And you shall draw water with joy from the fountains of salvation.', Namely, the dimension of supernal waters which are termed the fountains of salvation; for the lower waters represent the yearning and longing for salvation, in repentance and prayer from the aspect of the arousal from below,:. as is stated: 'Pour out your heart like water, etc.' And this unfolds during the final forty days culminating on Yom Kippur;, and during the seven days of Sukkot is the time of the water libation, which is the flow of holiness from Above into all seven holy emotional attributes,. that their emergence be from the source of the fountains of salvation. And likewise throughout all seven days of the week, the holiness of the Sabbath day radiates upon the six working days. to sanctify the personal attributes that they reside in holiness. And for this we mention at the departure of Shabbat six expressions of salvation, and seven are enfolded within them, so that all six working days be enfolded in the sanctity of the past Sabbath,. to purify and sanctify the attributes that they emerge from the fountains of salvation., And Sunday, which corresponds to the holy attribute of Chesed, requires salvation to be guarded from its opposite, which is 'one corresponding to the other', )., these being the seven names of the evil inclination mentioned in the words of our Sages (Sukkah 52a),. counterpoised to the seven holy attributes. And its first name, which the Holy One called it, is 'evil', which is the inclination of lust termed evil,. counter to the lovingkindness of holy love. And likewise across all seven attributes,. salvation is needed to be protected from the opposing force confronting holiness, one against the other.: And this is the entire mission of man in this world:, to be continually yearning for salvation, ).: as stated (Shabbat 31a):. that in the ultimate future they ask a person: 'Did you yearn for salvation?', And the primary counsel is through setting fixed times for the Oral Torah, especially during the long nights of the winter season of Tevet, for night was created solely for rigorous study, ). as stated (Eruvin 65a and in Tosafot).: And the order following the inquiry 'Did you yearn for salvation?' is: ",. 'Did you analyze with wisdom? Did you understand one matter from within another?', And the primary intent relates to the Oral Torah, for the six questions correspond to the Six Orders of the Mishnah:. which were expounded upon the verse: 'And the faith of your times shall be wisdom.., etc.': And corresponding to 'salvations' is the question: 'Did you yearn for salvation?';: and corresponding to the word 'wisdom' is: 'Did you analyze with wisdom?'; ", and 'knowledge' (da'at) alludes to understanding one thing from within another, for this is the true essence of Da'at:,. when one unites wisdom in his brain with understanding of the heart, as is known.

sections.title: Rosh Chodesh and the Renewal of Israel
sections.summary: The moon’s sanctification is linked to Israel’s special understanding of Torah and the rhythm of revelation.

topics.h: Kiddush HaChodesh and the Renewal of the Oral Torah
topics.en: Sanctification of the New Moon is the first commandment given to Israel in Egypt, and it was not spoken directly to them, but only to Moses and Aaron, and He did not state that they should say this to all Israel; nonetheless, 'This month shall be unto you'—, means unto the whole of Israel, ): and as stated in the Midrash Rabbah (Shemot, Parashah 15): ". 'The New Moon is unto you, etc.', Only the formal sanctification was entrusted to the leaders of Israel alone, and if the preeminent authority of the generation is in the Diaspora, having left no equal in the Land of Israel, he sanctifies and fixes the month there, ). as is related regarding Rabbi Akiva (Berakhot 63a).,. And nowadays we establish it based upon the sanctified calendar of Hillel the Latter, as is known.: And this is just as is stated in the Midrash there: that Hashem did not desire to sanctify it Himself, – for that would be sanctifying for Himself—, rather, He sanctifies Israel, and by virtue of their being holy, whatever they sanctify becomes consecrated,. like a non-sacred vessel into which one places holy matter., Therefore they consecrate it,:, as is stated: 'And you shall be holy unto Me, for I am holy,'. see there in the commentary Matnot Kehunah, who is pressed. And it appears that the meaning is:, that through your being holy, thereby 'I am holy';: and in this manner commentators explained that which is taught: " My holiness is above your holiness'—. that through your holiness I become sanctified from above.:, And it is said: 'Yet You are holy, enthroned upon the praises of Israel,',. meaning, established through the praises of Israel, see there., The inner meaning is well known, that the sun and the moon allude to the Holy One and His Shekhinah, ).: and as stated (in Sotah 10a): ", 'Samson' (Shimshon) is named after the Holy One,:, as it is said: 'For a sun and a shield is Hashem';:, and it is said: 'For Hashem your God is a consuming fire,', and likewise the sun is a celestial body of fire,:, and this is 'and the day that comes shall burn them up,' ): and as is stated (Nedarim 8b). that He extracts the sun from its sheath, etc. ( And in Shemot Rabbah there:), the nations reckon by the sun, which is of fire, and are destined to be judged by it;, while Israel reckon by the moon, which is of light, and thus they inherit the light,:, as it is said: 'Light is sown for the righteous, etc.',":. and it says: 'Arise, shine, for your light has come,' see there., Namely, idolaters call Him 'the God of gods,' ). as stated (end of Menachot 110a), on the verse 'My Name is great among the nations,'. meaning that they presume He exercises no providence in the lower realms at all. However, the prime purpose of the world's creation, is to manifest the honor of His kingship in the world,:, as it is said: 'Hashem made everything for His sake,' ): and our Sages said (Shocher Tov, Tehillim 148): ", 'for His praise,'. and this is His holy Shekhinah residing in the lower realms., And Abraham our father, peace be upon him, was the first to publicize this in the world, ), as our Sages wrote (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashat Chayei Sarah 59:8), on the verse 'God of the heavens and God of the earth':, that until now He was God of heaven alone, etc., and now 'God of the earth'—. for he proclaimed His providence in the lower realms. ): And it was said on this (Bereishit Rabbah, end of Parashah 30):: that the Holy One said to him: ", "'Rather than illuminating for Me from Mesopotamia, come and illuminate before Me in the Land of Israel, etc.', For this is defined as illuminating before Him,. by spreading the glory of His sovereignty over all Creation., And this parallels the moon, which receives its luminescence from the sun;:, and this is 'Arise, shine,'— that Israel illuminate before Him; and whence do they draw this light?:. Via Hashem: 'your light'—He shines upon them. ) And in this manner they expounded in Midrash Rabbah (Tetzaveh, end of Parashah 36): regarding the Menorah: the Holy One illuminates the whole universe,. yet commands that they illuminate before Him., For oil represents Chokhmah (Wisdom),. and the light of the oil is the light of the Torah., And Hashem illuminates through the light of the Written Torah, and Israel illuminate through the Oral Torah,. which is what they innovate through analysis., And in truth, these too are the 'words of the living God,' ).:, as stated (in Eruvin 13b) and so brought (Bava Batra 12a),. and see there in the Ramban that it stems from the Holy Spirit and is superior to prophecy. Nevertheless, Hashem delivered this over to the Sages, as if they are the ones generating this illumination; and by virtue of 'your light has come'—, that which Hashem shines into their hearts,. thereby they shine back before Him., And Scripture states 'Arise, shine' first,. for in overt manifestation they are the ones actively illuminating.:, And upon this the Midrash stated: 'You will yearn for the work of Your hands,'— that Hashem yearns for them,. that it be ascribed to the children of Israel, that they are the luminaries., And this matter is the dedication of Aaron, ), as stated in the Midrash (beginning of Parashat Beha'alotekha), for he is the root of the Oral Torah,:, as it is said: 'They shall teach Your judgments to Jacob, etc.',:, and said: 'And you shall come unto the priests.. according to the Torah they teach you, etc.',:. and said: 'The lips of the priest.. and they shall seek Torah from his mouth, etc.', And the sun and the moon likewise allude to the Written Torah and Oral Torah,. since they receive the illumination from the Written Torah., ): And therefore they stated in the Midrash HaNe'elam (Zohar Part I, 97b): that the Holy One comes on Rosh Chodesh, to hear teachings of Torah from the souls of the righteous, for then shines the illumination of the Oral Torah, and Hashem yearns for the work of His hands;, and therefore He handed the sanctification of the New Moon to the Sages,. for they are the ones who radiate the light of the Oral Torah., And this is the revelation of the Shekhinah within the hearts of Israel,: for this is the essence of the light of Torah:, to illuminate the heart with the knowledge of God,: as is stated regarding the ultimate future: 'And they shall no more teach every man his neighbor,. for they shall all know Me, etc.', And King David, peace be upon him, said to King Solomon, peace be upon him, who is the root of the lower wisdom of the Oral Torah,, the root of Malchut, the mouth of the Oral Torah,:, saying to him: 'Know the God of your father, etc.',. and this is 'from His mouth come knowledge and understanding.':), And it is said (Mishlei 9:10): 'and the knowledge of the holy ones is understanding,', and Binah (Understanding) is the Oral Torah, understanding one concept from within another, and this is the 'knowledge of the holy ones'—the intimate awareness of Him, blessed be He,. which is attained via the Oral Torah., And Da'at (Knowledge) is the Holy Spirit, as Rashi wrote in Parashat Ki Tisa, and it is the profound perception of the Oral Torah as mentioned above;, and therefore it is called 'knowledge of the holy ones', for 'holy ones' are those who possess the Holy Spirit,. their holiness emanating directly from His holiness., And Israel were chosen so that all of them would be on this level,:, and as it is written: 'For a holy people are you,':, and it is said: 'Israel is holy unto Hashem,',":. and said: 'You shall be holy,' 'and you shall be holy.': And so they are termed in the Gemara in the chapter 'Rabbi Akiva' and in the first chapter of Chullin: ". 'Israel are holy.', And for this purpose the Giving of the Torah took place,:. as it is said: 'And you shall be unto Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.', And the priests are the dedicated holy ones, ":, as is said at the beginning of Parashat Emor: 'They shall be holy, etc.', ", 'He shall be holy unto you.. for I Hashem sanctify you,':. and in Parashat Korach: 'the one whom Hashem chooses is the holy one.':, And Korach's assembly claimed: 'For all the congregation are holy, and Hashem is among them,', for this is genuine holiness—when Hashem dwells among them,. and in ultimate truth it is so., And in the ultimate future it will be fully realized, and all will be a kingdom of priests, and 'the priest's lips shall keep knowledge,'. and then 'all of them shall know Me, etc.', And at the Revelation at Mount Sinai all of them were on this level, as stated in Shir HaShirim Rabbah on the verse 'Let him kiss me';, yet afterward, even though holiness permeates all Israel, nevertheless gradations exist, and they needed to receive the transmission from Moses and Aaron, ):: as stated (in Eruvin 54b): ". 'How was the order of the teaching of the Mishnah, etc.' ): And on this it is said (in Shemot Rabbah, Parashah 15): "' Send Your light and Your truth, etc.'—, these are Moses and Aaron,:, as it is written: 'Your Thummim and Your Urim, etc.',: and said: 'The law of truth was in his mouth, etc.';:,. and it says: 'This month shall be unto you'—this is what Scripture states, etc., see there., And this means that this is the essence of the New Moon's sanctification delivered to them,. that through it they radiate into the hearts of the children of Israel., And Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, is the root of the light of Torah,:, as it is said: 'And she saw him that he was good,' ). for when he was born the entire house was filled with light (Sotah 12a);, and that it become permanently ingrained in the heart is via Aaron, the best man of the Queen (Shekhinah), who draws souls near to the Torah;, and this is 'the Torah of truth that was in his mouth,': and the lip of truth is that which endures forever. Until here from his holy handwriting.

sections.title: Marcheshvan: Awe, Judgment, Rain, and Rectification
sections.summary: The spiritual character of Cheshvan calls for awe of Heaven, acceptance of Torah, and the repair of earlier failings.

topics.h: Cheshvan, the Sense of Smell, and True Awe
topics.en: It is stated in Sefer Yetzirah: ". "He crowned the letter Nun with smell, etc., and Cheshvan in the year.", ): In the holy Zohar (Part II, 91a): ", 'The letter Nun is the mystery of revering the Holy One, and knowing that there is judgment and there is a Judge, and there is good reward for the righteous and retribution for the wicked, because its esoteric mystery is the lower Hei';, and it is known that the lower Hei represents Malchut, ): and so it is in the holy Zohar (Acharei Mot 66b): ",". 'A bent Nun—this is the Matronita (Shekhinah/Malchut),' see there. ", And 'a king by justice establishes the land,',. which corresponds to the Divine Name Adonai, the royal law of judgment.:, And in the discourse Petach Eliyahu: 'Tzedek is known as Din (Judgment)', and this is 'there is judgment';, and so one must revere,: for concerning a king it is said: 'You shall set a king over you..'—, that his dread be upon you;:. and it is said: 'And if I be a Master, where is My fear?' And in Cheshvan the judgment of the generation of the Flood began, who sinned abundantly and did not fear God, proclaiming that there is neither judgment nor Judge,: as is written: 'And they say unto God: Depart from us, etc., ". what is the Almighty that we should serve Him, and what profit should we have if we pray to Him?' And until the completion of the Temple's construction by King Solomon, peace be upon him, the imprint of the judgment of the Flood remained present in the world, ) as written (Tanchuma, Noach 8) that every year in the month of Cheshvan torrential waters poured down for forty days;, and for this reason the month of Cheshvan is named in Kings (I Kings 6:38) at the completion of the Temple ", the 'month of Bul' without the letter Mem (spelling, flood),. for upon the completion of the Temple, the forty days marking the Flood ceased. For the ultimate intent of Creation, is to be an abode in the lower realms, for the Shekhinah to dwell upon earth;, and through the sin of the Flood generation and the Dispersion, the Shekhinah departed,. and through the construction of the Temple, She returned., In the Holy Temple, the indwelling of the Shekhinah was permanent, as Jacob named the site of the Temple a 'house', signifying an established domicile for the manifestation of His Shekhinah;, and from there awe goes forth to the world,:, as is said: 'that you may learn to fear Hashem, etc.', not merely fear of punishment, but genuine awe, for wherever His Shekhinah is unveiled, awe descends,:. as stated: 'And with great awe—this refers to the revelation of the Shekhinah.': And as stated in the gloss of the Rema at the beginning of Orach Chayim: when a person takes to heart, that the King of kings, the Holy One, stands over him and sees his actions,. awe and subjugation from the dread of Hashem instantly fall upon him, etc., And the letter Nun denotes falling, ).: as is stated (Berakhot 4b):, that the letter Nun was omitted in Ashrei because in it lies the downfall of Israel, etc.,:, in the West (the Land of Israel) they recited: 'Fallen, she shall rise no more, etc.':, and it states there: nonetheless David supported them via the Holy Spirit,: as it is said: 'Hashem supports all who fall';:, and it is written: 'the fallen tabernacle of David', for a sukkah is a temporary dwelling, meaning that even when it seems fallen He supports it,. continually drawing down His royal presence into the world., And the fall is solely for the sake of ascent,:, as is stated: 'For seven times a righteous man falls and rises up,':. and for the future it is written: 'I will raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen.' ): And it is brought (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 17):, the beginning of downfall is sleep;, one sleeps and does not labor in the Torah, for through sleep one is distanced from Hashem,:, as it is said: 'Slothfulness casts into a deep sleep,'. slacking off from the service of Hashem. ): And it is brought likewise in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 9): "', "'And behold it was very good'—this is sleep; is sleep really 'very good'? Rather, because he sleeps a little,. he rises and labors in the Torah abundantly." Namely, that he rectifies the fall itself, so that it becomes an aid to the service of Hashem,. and from it he draws strength to serve Him.: And so afterward in the month of Kislev: ". 'He crowned the letter Samekh with sleep, and Kislev in the year.', And it said 'He crowned the letter Nun with smell', for one who possesses the fear of Hashem has the sense of smell,:, in the manner of the verse: 'And his scent shall be in the fear of Hashem,'. that he will smell and judge., Now, every month has a unique matter to engage in, and in the month of Marcheshvan the spiritual work is to strengthen oneself to begin rising from the fall,: and to bring oneself into sanctity through the fear of Hashem.

topics.h: The Month of Rain, Judgment, and the Yoke of Torah
topics.en: It is brought from the holy master Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Rimanov of blessed memory, that in the month of Marcheshvan the majority of harsh decrees occur,. because then the kingdom of the House of David was divided., And presumably this is not merely for punishment,. rather it is a uniquely propitious time to rectify this. ).,: And the matter is, as taught in the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah 11b):, according to Rabbi Yehoshua, on the seventeenth of Iyar the Flood began;, and according to Rabbi Eliezer, that in Tishrei the world was created,. that day was the seventeenth of Marcheshvan.:, And it is taught: Our Rabbis taught, the Sages of Israel reckon for the Flood according to Rabbi Eliezer, and for astronomical cycles according to Rabbi Yehoshua;: and Rashi and Tosafot explained: ". 'for the Flood'—for the calendar years of the world we count from Tishrei like Rabbi Eliezer., And one must understand according to this the expression 'for the Flood',:, for it should have said 'for years' or 'for the years of the world', " and why adopt the phrase 'for the Flood', which has long passed?, However, it seems that there is an allusion in this, ): for it is taught (Tanchuma, Noach 8): you find that from that time, until Solomon built the Holy Temple, forty days of rains fell each year in the manner of the Flood, and when Solomon built the Temple he prayed for mercy upon them, and they ceased from the world, etc.,:. as it is said: 'in the month of Bul, etc.', Namely, the generation of the Flood were originally fit to receive the Torah, for the soul of Moses our teacher was present then, ):: as the Gemara alludes (Chullin 139b): " Where is Moses indicated in the Torah? ', 'Inasmuch as he is also' (be-shagam = 345) equals Moses,:. and it is written: 'and his days shall be a hundred and twenty years.' ),: And so it is explicitly written in the holy Zohar (Part III, 216a): that Moses was destined to receive the Torah in the generation of the Flood, etc.; ): and so is written in the Midrash (Shemot Rabbah, Parashah 30): "' And the knowledge of Your ways we do not desire'— that they did not want to receive the Torah,. which are the ways of the Holy One.":, And it is written: 'On that day all the fountains of the great deep burst open, etc.', and in the holy Zohar (Part I, 117a) they hinted regarding this: to the sixth millennium: the gates of wisdom above. and the wellsprings of wisdom below. Namely, at that time during the days of the Flood there burst open 'all the fountains of the great deep'—, the wellsprings of lower wisdom, the Oral Torah; ", and 'the windows of heaven'—the gates of wisdom, the Written Torah; for then they were fit to receive the Written Torah, within which the entire Oral Torah was enfolded, just as Moses our teacher received later from Mount Sinai,:, as stated: 'Moses received Torah from Sinai and transmitted it to Joshua', which refers to the Oral Torah, for the Written Torah he handed to the priests, the sons of Levi, ),. as stated in the holy Zohar (Part II, 137).:, And it is written: 'And the rain was upon the earth forty days', for He brought them down in mercy, that if they repent, they would be rains of blessing, as Rashi explains;, which is Torah, ).: as brought in the Gemara (Bava Kama 17a): ". 'Water is nothing other than Torah.', Yet because they did not repent and corrupted their ways, they turned into raging waters and were judged,:. and as written afterward: 'And the Flood was forty days.' Namely, in Tishrei 'Let there be light' occurred—, this is Rosh Hashanah, ) as stated in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 36); ): and so written in Midrash Rabbah (Parashat Acharei Mot): ", 'My light' on Rosh Hashanah, for then begins renewal in words of Torah —'Torah is light'— until Shemini Atzeret, which is the flowing wellspring of Torah, ), as stated in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 13), for then the light of the Oral Torah is set, innovation in Torah; and from then is the forty-day span. to receive this flow and renewal in Torah permanently. ).,: And likewise regarding the rainy season, it is taught (Ta'anit 6a):, the first rain (Yoreh) falls in Marcheshvan, ", 'Yoreh'—it instructs (moreh) people to plaster, etc., and it also alludes to instructing people. to take upon themselves the yoke of Torah in truth., And so wrote the Maggid of Kozhnitz of blessed memory, that what is stated in the first chapter of Ta'anit regarding the stature of the day of rain refers to Shemini Atzeret, which is the wellspring of Torah (. (as explained in Bereishit, Discourse 9).: And this is what it meant: that from that hour until Solomon built the Temple, they had forty days of rains marking the waters of the Flood; namely, that if they merit— words of Torah become fixed in their hearts with renewal, during the forty days from Shemini Atzeret, which is the wellspring of Torah;, and if they do not merit, Heaven forbid, it turns into waters of flood, until Solomon built the Holy Temple,:, and it is written: 'For out of Zion shall go forth Torah, and the word of Hashem from Jerusalem', "):, the word of Hashem'—this is Halakhah, as stated (Shabbat 138b); ). and there sat the Chamber of Hewn Stone whence Torah issued to all Israel (Sanhedrin 86b);, and then there was revealed to King Solomon all lower wisdom of the Oral Torah—the wisdom of Solomon, and he prayed for mercy upon them and they ceased,. transforming into rains of blessing, an influx of Torah.:, And this is what they said: the Sages reckon for the Flood according to Rabbi Eliezer, for even though the physical world was created in Nisan, nonetheless the season for the influx of Torah, which are the Flood waters when merited and transformed into rains of blessing, an influx from the wellspring of Torah,. is fixed in Cheshvan according to Rabbi Eliezer., And the task in the month of Marcheshvan is to assume the yoke of Torah in truth; and the essence of the yoke of Torah is in the study of the Oral Torah, which entails great exertion and sleepless nights, and one who covets wealth and pleasure cannot master the Oral Torah, ). as is stated (Tanchuma, Noach 3).: And we learned: 'Whoever accepts upon himself the yoke of Torah, they remove from him the yoke of the kingdom, etc.';, and therefore most harsh decrees threaten in this month, so that people will embrace the Torah in truth;,: and the waters will become rains of blessing from the wellspring of Torah, as stated.

topics.h: The Letter Nun, Spiritual Discernment, and the Flood
topics.en: In Sefer Yetzirah: ". "He crowned the letter Nun with smell, etc., and Cheshvan in the year, and the small intestines in the soul, etc.", And in the commentary of the Ra'avad of blessed memory, when he correlated twelve faculties against twelve tribes, he linked smell with Joseph,, for when he withstood temptation his fragrance spread from one end of the world to the other, see there,. yet he did not explain the underlying root.:, And it appears rooted in the verse: 'And his scent shall be in the fear of Hashem,':. and regarding Joseph it is written: 'I fear God.' ):: And this is what the Gemara stated (Eruvin 21b): "'. "'The mandrakes yield fragrance'—these are the young men of Israel who have not tasted the flavor of sin." And from the phrase 'young men of Israel' it indicates this specific blemish (immorality) which youth and bachelorhood tend to cause; ).: and so it is brought in the Gemara, Sotah (49a): ",:,. "'I perceive a pleasing scent'; he said to him: 'My son, purity exists within you.'":, And this too is based upon: 'And his scent shall be in the fear of Hashem,':. and it is written: 'The fear of Hashem is pure, enduring forever.'
