And when one possesses the olfactory sense in perfection, it demonstrates that he possesses fear of God and purity,:. and therefore it was declared concerning those untainted by this blemish: 'The mandrakes yield fragrance.', And it said 'He crowned the letter Nun with smell', ),: based on what is written in the holy Zohar (Part II, 91a): ", 'The letter Nun is the mystery of fearing the Holy One, etc.,. for its esoteric mystery is the lower Hei.', And the Divine Name corresponding to Malchut is the Name Adonai, ), as stated in the holy Zohar (Part III, 11b), which denotes awe,:. as is said: 'And if I be a Master, where is My fear?': So too the attribute of Malchut points to awe:, the Sabbath of Friday eve is awe, resting within her, ),. as stated in the holy Zohar (Part I, 5b)., And the connection to this month is, that the labor therein is to accept the yoke of Torah in truth,. whereby they remove from him worldly burdens, as we said. Namely, that the Torah of Shemini Atzeret, –, —the wellspring of Torah—be ingrained in the heart,. as we explained. ),: And it is brought (Midrash Rabbah, Berakhah 11:6): ",: "'By your lives, all wisdom and the entire Torah is one simple matter:, whoever fears Me and performs the words of Torah,. all wisdom and the entire Torah is in his heart.',':, Whence? For it is said: 'The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem, good understanding to all who do them'; ', 'The fear of Hashem is pure, enduring forever'; '. 'Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom.', He cites these three verses, to prove that the essence of wisdom is fear of God, and to fulfill the words of Torah, ).: as stated in the Gemara (Berakhot 17a): "', To those who study them' is not said, but 'to those who do them'—, to those who perform them for their own sake,:. as it is said: 'A good understanding have all those who do them.'", And he cites 'The fear of Hashem is pure, enduring forever', for through awe the words of Torah become fixed for all eternity, since fear of God endures forever,. and the fear of Hashem is wisdom.: Therefore it said: ". 'He crowned the letter Nun with smell, and Cheshvan in the year.', And in this month the Flood occurred, ): and it is taught in the Gemara (Niddah 13b): regarding the blemish of the Covenant: ". 'they are offspring of the Flood.', And this month is the season to rectify the blemish of the Flood;, and this specific defect causes servitude, ): as stated (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 84): " Let us go and follow the way of the world;,. Canaan who sinned, was he not cursed to be a slave, etc.?', And the blemish of Canaan stems from his birth from Ham, ).: for it is taught in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 70a):: one authority says he sodomized him; ):, and he cohabited in the Ark (as written there, 108b), and this was also a breach of the Covenant. since marital relations were forbidden to them., And from him issued Canaan, cursed to be a slave,. for this sin precipitates enslavement., And the tribes suspected Joseph of not being free of this flaw, because he alleged that they cast eyes on the daughters of the land, as written in Bereishit Rabbah;, and they knew within themselves that they were pure in this, and presumed that he was compromised therein, for 'whoever invalidates others—disqualifies through his own blemish',. and for this reason they sold him as a slave. And whoever rectifies this blemish during this month propitious for it. will be spared from servitude., And the primary rectification is attained through the attribute of awe and reverence,: which constitutes the inner labor and theme of this month, as stated.

topics.h: Repairing the Serpent’s Influence Through Torah
topics.en: And it said 'and the small intestines in the soul', ),: which is based on what is written in the holy Zohar (Part II, 148b): ", 'Everywhere this Serpent stalks following the mystery of the Woman of Valor,. seeking to become the Harlot Woman, etc.', The primordial Serpent is thus termed the 'Harlot Woman', and the core seduction of the Serpent at the outset, was via the lust for eating, to implant in man's heart the lust to experience bodily pleasure; )., and afterward he cohabited with Eve and injected defilement into her (Shabbat 146a), and because all humanity descended from Eve, this pollution entered into her offspring as well,. and through the Serpent's defilement this moral blemish is induced., And this month, which was formed with the letter Nun, whose esoteric secret is the lower Hei— ",", 'a Woman of Valor', the 'fear of Hashem', is therefore the season to rectify this defect, and automatically the root corruption of the Serpent is repaired— the Harlot Woman that originated through eating;:. and this is why it says: 'and the small intestines in the soul.', And likewise, through fear of God words of Torah are inscribed in the heart, which is the ultimate purpose for which the inclination was created—, that passion be directed toward words of Torah, ).: and as stated in the Gemara (Sukkah 52a): ". "'If this vile one confronts you, drag him to the study hall.' ", 'Vile one' is the title of the evil inclination of lust for the Harlot Woman, ).: and as stated in the Gemara (Shabbat 152a): ", "'A woman is a vessel full of filth, etc.',": and the counsel is: 'drag him to the study hall'—, that he channel the passion into words of Torah, for for this purpose the inclination was created,. which is the deep drive to become passionate delight for Torah., And as it will be in the ultimate future, when the drive will remain purely for the delight of Torah, ): as stated in the Midrash HaNe'elam (Zohar Part I, 131a): ", for without the evil inclination, there would be no ecstatic joy in Torah learning';: and so is written in Tanchuma, Bereishit::, the Holy One said: 'You make it evil, etc.', for Hashem created the impulse –, —as an impetus of zeal for Torah,. so that there be radiant joy in Talmudic analysis. And this is 'drag him to the study hall'—. the setting where novel insights of the Oral Torah are forged., And this is the prime undertaking of this month, formed with the letter Nun, which signifies awe, and through the potency of smell, to rectify the defect of the Serpent in eating and lust, and that words of Torah be embedded in the heart,. to take upon oneself the yoke of Torah in truth.,

sections.title: Noach, the Generations, and the Purpose of Torah
sections.summary: The Flood generation, Noah’s righteousness, and the eventual reception of Torah reveal the path of human repair.

topics.h: These Are the Generations of Noach
topics.en: These are the generations of Noah.": In Midrash Tanchuma (Parashat Noach 1) it opens: ", "'Blessed be the Name of the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, Who chose Israel, etc.,, and gave us the Written Torah with hinted, concealed, and veiled teachings, and explained them in the Oral Torah, etc.',. and elaborated extensively upon the Oral Torah, see there. And one must understand the connection of the Written Torah and Oral Torah to this parashah. ): And it will be understood based on what we learned (Avot 5:2):, There were ten generations from Adam until Noah, to make known how great is His patience, etc.;, ten generations from Noah until Abraham, etc.,. until Abraham our father came and received the reward of them all., Now behold, in every context the number ten corresponds to the Ten Commandments, which correspond to the Ten Sefirot. that Hashem, blessed be He, emanated for the creation of the world. And there were ten generations from Adam to Noah to rectify the entire blemish of Adam the First's sin and to become refined in all character traits;, and then, in the Generation of the Flood, it was originally fit for the Giving of the Torah, ) as written in Midrash Rabbah (Mishpatim, Parashah 30), ), and in the holy Zohar (Part III, 216b), and the soul of Moses our teacher was present then,:. as hinted: 'be-shagam' (345 = has the gematria of Moshe (345 =. And they would have merited the Written Torah and the Oral Torah,: which were hinted at in that which is stated: " all the fountains of the great deep burst open’—, the wellsprings of wisdom below (the Oral Torah), " and the windows of heaven were opened’—, the gates of wisdom above (the Written Torah), ), as written in the holy Zohar (Part I, 117a),. and then they would have rectified the entire blemish of the Serpent as will be in the ultimate future. Yet through their continually provoking Him, these waters were transformed into raging waters, and they were all washed away in the waters of the Flood,. and none remained of them except Noah. And for this reason, in the ten generations before the Flood, there is calculated for each person a sum total encompassing all the days of their lives, because in the life they lived after fathering the head of the generation, they possessed no renewed, independent life; for the entire essence of their life was merely that one person emerge who counted in the tally of generations, from whom Noah emerged and the world was rebuilt;, whereas from what they lived afterward and fathered sons and daughters,. no remnant survived from this, since they were wiped out in the Flood. And the life they lived after fathering the head of the generation was subsumed, with the life they lived beforehand, and through this they were termed with the terminology of 'life';,. and since all the days of their lives were tallied together, it is written 'and he died.', In contrast, in the ten generations from Noah to Abraham in this parashah, remnants survived also from what was fathered, after they fathered the head of the generation;, for from the sons and daughters nations survived,":, and they possess vitality, as stated: 'and You preserve them all,' as is known; yet they are not comparable to the life lived before fathering the head of the generation,. from which descended and emerged Abraham and his seed, who are eternal life., And since the two lifespans are not comparable to one another, therefore the life lived beforehand was not combined together with the life lived afterward;, and since all the days of their lives were not calculated together,. therefore 'and he died' is not written regarding them., Except regarding Noah, who did not father any children at all after the Flood, and the life he lived after the Flood was subsumed, within the lifespan he lived until fathering Shem, Ham, and Japheth, from whom the world was built, and the years he lived afterward did not constitute a separate, renewed line of vitality;:. therefore it is written regarding him: 'And all the days of Noah were, etc., and he died.',, And likewise with Terah, who after living seventy years and fathering Abram, Nahor, and Haran, did not father any further children, and there was not in the life he lived afterward any separate renewed root of vitality,:,. and therefore all his days were calculated together, and it is written: 'and Terah died in Haran.', And likewise the ten generations from Noah to Abraham are also in the number ten,. being fit to rectify the entire blemish. And the Mishnah states 'to make known, etc.' that all the generations went on provoking Him, until Abraham our father came and received the reward of them all, which the Mishnah did not say regarding the earlier ten generations;, for from these ten generations a spiritual remnant endured, and all the holy sparks that were within them Abraham our father received;, in that he was tested with ten trials, which likewise correspond to the Ten Sefirot,. and he withstood them all and became refined in all character traits. ):, And he merited to fulfill the entire Torah before it was given (as stated in Yoma 28b),:,. meaning even the Oral Torah, as they said there: 'even Eiruv Tavshilin.', Moreover, the entire Torah as a whole, since he was not explicitly commanded concerning it, rather his two kidneys were transformed like two rabbis, welling forth and teaching him Torah and wisdom, ), as stated (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 61), and this is the aspect of the Oral Torah. which wells up in the heart from the words of the living God.: And this is what the Tanchuma stated afterward concerning the preeminence of the Oral Torah: " ‘Because no one learns it, except one who loves the Holy One, blessed be He, with all his heart, with all his soul, and with all his might, etc.’;, and love is the attribute of Abraham our father, peace be upon him,:, as it is written: 'Abraham My beloved,', and he loved the Holy One with all his heart, all his soul, and all his might,. and merited the Oral Torah., And just as in the Generation of the Flood it was the time for Torah to be given through the soul of Moses our teacher, namely the Written Torah within which the Oral Torah was also enfolded, just as occurred at the Giving of the Torah;. so in the Generation of the Dispersion (Dor HaFlagah) it was the time for the revelation and expansion of the Oral Torah., And the primary expansion of the Oral Torah was in Babylonia, ) as they said (Sukkah 20a);, therefore when they sensed in Shinar that it was a place fit for the revelation and expansion of the Oral Torah, they built a tower counter to the Holy Temple, which is the place whence Torah goes forth to all Israel (:); (as stated in Sanhedrin 86b);. and they made, in parallel 'one corresponding to the other,' a tower for the expansion of their vanities., And at that time Abraham our father, peace be upon him, was forty-eight years old,: )' as Rashi wrote (Shabbat 10b, s.v. she-yeshivatah);, and then Abraham our father recognized his Creator, ) as written (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 30);. meaning that he merited the entire Oral Torah. And afterward there were four years until the two thousand years of Torah began. And the four years that preceded correspond to the first three Sefirot and the attribute of Chesed, which is the attribute of Abraham our father, peace be upon him;, and afterward began the two thousand years of Torah in the attribute of Gevurah, for the Torah comes from the side of Gevurah (, (as stated in Zohar Part III, 80b), and this refers to the Oral Torah, ),: as stated in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21) and in the holy Zohar (Part II, 167a): ". ‘and from the left was given the Oral Torah’.:, And this is what it said: ‘until Abraham our father came and received the reward of them all’—, meaning their holy sparks and their vitality, which is the holiness of the Oral Torah,. and Abraham our father merited it.: And this is what Rashi wrote in his commentary: ", 'until Abram there was the burning wrath of the Omnipresent', for once Abraham our father came there was no longer burning wrath, since he merited and took the reward of them all, and this was written after the first trial;:. and this is what the Mishnah meant by: ‘to make known how great is His patience, etc.’: And in Tosafot Yom Tov he wrote that there are two kinds of wrath:, there is one where He delays anger and in the end destroys everything as in the Flood,. and there is one where He delays anger and it does not come to fruition in total destruction, etc. And the holy master of blessed memory (the Chozeh of Lublin), said in the name of the holy master of Lublin of blessed memory,: who explained that which our Sages said: ", ‘Whoever says that the Holy One, blessed be He, overlooks sins, his entrails shall be surrendered, rather He is patient and collects what is His’—:. that the meaning is: He raises up His wrath. ) Now this dictum is mentioned in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 67) regarding the single cry that Jacob caused Esau to utter, etc.,, and where he was held accountable, see there,: and there the reading is: ‘He is patient and collects what is His’; ) and so it is mentioned in the Yerushalmi (Shekalim 5:4), regarding Nechunya the well-digger whose son died of thirst, )., and as stated also in our Babylonian Talmud (Bava Kamma 50a),:. and there the text reads: ‘He is patient and collects what is His.’ And in both places it implies that the meaning of 've-gavei deileih' is:. that He collects His due afterward to repay him. And certainly the words of the holy master of blessed memory are true.: And according to what was explained, both interpretations are true:, for 've-gavei deileih' means He elevates His own, just as here with Abraham our father who received the reward of them all, and merited the entire Oral Torah of the Generation of the Dispersion, and burning wrath was removed from the world;, and automatically He collects His due, for once he received from them their root vitality and the holy sparks within them, in the mystical secret of 'and You preserve them all,'. their vitality was uprooted from the world.,":. And this is what it meant: 'to make known how great is His patience, etc.,' and as explained., And this is the connection of this teaching to Parashat Toldot Noach: that the core of the parashah is how Abraham our father received the Oral Torah. which was intended for the Generation of the Dispersion., And on Shabbat is the time of the Written Torah, ):: as they said (Shabbat 86b): ", ‘for all agree that on Shabbat the Torah was given to Israel’, and it is the time of abundance in the Oral Torah, ),: as stated in the holy Zohar (Part I, 47b): ", ‘On the seventh day—this is the Oral Torah which is the seventh day’,. namely Malchut: 'the mouth—we call it the Oral Torah.',

sections.title: The Four Divine Gifts and the Rectification of the Flood
sections.summary: Torah, suffering, sacrifice, and prayer are paths by which the blemishes of earlier generations are healed.

topics.h: Torah and Afflictions as Remedies for Sin
topics.en: In Midrash Tanchuma (Parashat Noach 1): ", ‘These are the generations of Noah, blessed be the Name of the King of kings Who chose Israel, etc., and gave us the Torah, etc.’, and elaborated upon the praise of the Oral Torah; and to understand the connection to the parashah. and to that which is stated: 'These are the generations of Noah.' ) Indeed, it is brought in Midrash Rabbah (Shemot Rabbah, Parashah 30): that the Holy One, blessed be He, sought to give the Generation of the Flood four things:,, Torah, afflictions, the service of sacrificial offerings, and prayer,. yet they did not desire them, etc. Namely, Hashem willed to return them to goodness. and to provide remedies against the evil inclination of man's heart from his youth., And afflictions serve as atonement for the past, ). as they stated (Avodah Zarah 4a): on the verse 'Only you have I known, etc.': one who loves him exacts payment from him little by little;, and also to awaken him for the future,:, as it is stated: 'He who spares his rod hates his son, but he who loves him disciplines him early,':. and it is stated: 'For whom Hashem loves He reproves, even as a father, etc.', And sacrifices likewise atone for the past, ): and as stated (Midrash Rabbah, Pinchas):, no person remained in Jerusalem with a sin in his hand, the morning daily offering atoned, etc.;, and for the future, through this one draws close to Hashem, blessed be He, ):: and in the manner they said (Zevachim 7b): ". ‘once the advocate has appeased, the gift enters after him’.: Moreover, such is the way of the evil inclination: today it says.. and tomorrow it says do thus.. (:), (as stated in Shabbat 105b), and at first Scripture calls it a traveler, and ultimately calls it a guest, etc., and one draws sin with cords of vanity until afterward it becomes thick like wagon ropes (:), (as stated in Sukkah 52b), for transgression draws transgression, ): and once one commits a sin and repeats it, it seems to him as permitted (Yoma 86b);, and when the prior sin is forgiven through a sacrifice,. the inclination cannot overpower him.: And Torah is the essential antidote: ". ‘drag him to the study hall’. –: And prayer—based on what they said: that without the Holy One helping him, he could not overcome it;, and Hashem stands ready to assist each individual,. provided that man prays to Him for this., And had they repented, Moses our teacher would have brought down the Torah to them, and the waters of the Flood would have turned for them into the waters of Torah;, yet they refused to accept these four things,: and as stated in Midrash Rabbah there from the verse: ", ‘And they said to God: Depart from us, etc.’,. all four of the aforementioned things being hinted at there.

topics.h: The Souls of the Flood Generation Reborn in Egypt
topics.en: And it is brought in the writings of the Ari of blessed memory, that the souls of Israel who were in Egypt under backbreaking labor and who received the Torah, were the souls from the Generation of the Flood and the Generation of the Dispersion, among whom were great souls,. only that good and evil were intermingled within them. For from the eating of the Tree of Knowledge, confusion occurred within souls as well, and even the pure soul was mixed with the lower one, until Abraham our father came, and merited to be the father of the souls of Israel,, and then the pure souls, the souls of Israel, were separated into a treasury of their own, ). as written in Tosafot (Avodah Zarah 5a) that 'until all the souls in Guf are completed'—,. refers to the souls of Israel which reside in a unique treasury of their own, see there., Now behold, what caused the Generation of the Flood to have 'the wickedness of man great in the earth', was due to the abundance of worldly good they possessed, having neither the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven nor the yoke of worldly labor;, for they did not even need to toil in the field, ) as written (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 34), that once every forty years they would sow, and they were merely eating, drinking, and acting frivolously, and excess ease brought them to rebel and sin (.); (as written in Sanhedrin 108a);, and so we find regarding Abraham our father, when he traversed places where people were eating, drinking, and acting frivolously,: he said: 'May it be that I have no portion in this land' (, (as stated in Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 39), because worldly occupation precedes Torah, in that through plowing during the plowing season, etc., toil in worldly occupation likewise makes one forget sin;, and when people do not engage in labor and spend their days in ease amidst worldly pleasures,. this brings directly unto sin.

topics.h: The Covenant and the Redemption of the Flood Generation
topics.en: Now behold, it is known that the primary sin of the Generation of the Flood, lay predominantly in the blemish of the Covenant (immorality),: as it is stated: 'for all flesh had corrupted its way, etc.'; and Abraham knew that his seed would stem from the souls of the Generation of the Flood, who stumbled in the sin of blemish of the Covenant, and the Land of Israel does not tolerate such sinners,: as the Torah warned: ", ‘After the doings of the land of Egypt, etc., shall you not do’, " that the land vomit you not out, etc.’;, and the doings of Egypt meant they were immersed in licentiousness,:. as stated: 'whose flesh is as the flesh of donkeys, and whose issue is like the issue of horses.': Therefore, when the Holy One, blessed be He, told him: ", ‘I am Hashem, etc., to give you this land to inherit it’,:. he asked: 'Whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it?', For even though he believed that Hashem would certainly give the land to his seed,:, nonetheless he asked: 'Whereby shall I know that they will endure within it?' Through what power will they overcome so as not to stumble again in the sin of the Flood generation, that the land should not vomit them out,. and that the land be unto them an everlasting inheritance?': And to this Hashem answered him: ", ‘Know of a surety that your seed shall be a stranger, etc., and they shall serve them, and they shall afflict them’, and through servitude and affliction they will be clarified and cleansed from the sin of the Flood generation;, for regarding the sin of blemish of the Covenant the judgment is to become a slave,. just as we found regarding the tribes who judged Joseph to sell him as a slave., Now he was the root of the holiness of the Covenant, yet he required refinements, since they suspected him of the reverse, because he brought an evil report about them that they cast their eyes upon the daughters of the land;, and they knew within themselves that they were pure of this, so they said that 'one who invalidates others disqualifies through his own blemish',. and certainly he harbors this flaw. ): And as brought (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 84)::, They said: Let us go and follow the way of the world;, Canaan who sinned, was he not cursed to be a slave? And the sin of Canaan was in blemish of the Covenant which Ham committed (.:); (as stated in Sanhedrin 70a, 108b);,. this one too—come, let us sell him!, And he was sold to Egypt, which was the epicenter of licentiousness, and there he was proven through trial to be pure and guarded, and all of Israel were fenced against immorality in his merit, ),. as our Sages of blessed memory taught (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:12)., And Egypt was 'the nakedness of the earth', and thither they were exiled to demonstrate that they were completely pure in this;, and when this was clarified, they were redeemed, ) as stated (Shir HaShirim Rabbah there). that they were redeemed from Egypt because they were strictly guarded against forbidden relations. And through servitude and affliction, they rectified the sin of the Generation of the Flood, and as the Ari of blessed memory wrote, that for souls from the Flood generation it was decreed: 'Every son that is born you shall cast into the river', and Moses our teacher rescued them, ):: as stated (Sotah 12b): ", ‘Six hundred thousand footmen, etc.’;:. Moses said to them: 'For my sake were you all saved.' And for the souls from the Generation of the Dispersion. they subjected them to hard labor 'with mortar and with bricks.', And after they were refined in Egypt, were redeemed, and merited to receive the Torah, they no longer required servitude and affliction, only to be toiling in Torah. and to undergo the rigors of Torah. And in place of their toil in the bondage of mortar and bricks, and what they suffered from being cast into the river, they merited afterward the waters of Torah. and the analytical reasoning of the Oral Torah through a fortiori arguments (kal va-chomer) and clarifying halakhot (libbun hilkhata). And counter to the Tower of Babel. they merited Jerusalem and the Holy Temple., And that which the Generation of the Dispersion used unity and peace to rebel against the Omnipresent, they merited afterward, once refined, for the sharpness of Torah,:, concerning which it is written: 'et vahev be- sufah'— that during the dialectic debate Torah scholars appear like enemies to one another, yet do not depart from there until they become beloved friends to one another (:) (as stated in Kiddushin 30b). once the halakhah has been clarified to them. And this is why Midrash Tanchuma elaborated in this parashah, in praise of Israel and the Torah, for in truth from that generation and from their souls,: were replanted the souls of Israel, the receivers of the Torah, as stated.

topics.h: The Midrash on the Spiritual Purpose of Suffering
topics.en: And this is likewise the intent of Midrash Tanchuma in what it wrote: ", ‘These are the generations of Noah—: so opened Rabbi Tanchuma bar Abba: ', "The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, etc." (Proverbs 11:30);, when a man departs from the world without children he is sorrowful;: the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, etc.: You have a fruit more beautiful than children, etc.—:, the Torah, concerning which it is written: "The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life", '. 'children' it does not say, etc.’, And seemingly it bears no relevance to that which is stated: 'These are the generations of Noah, etc.', for behold, Noah had children and the entire world emerged from his seed!, And when the Torah wished to hint that a person's primary offspring are his good deeds, it ought to have hinted this regarding one who died childless, and not regarding Noah, who left behind children!, However, it comes to teach us lest we err, that since only Noah and his seed survived, and he is the father of the whole world, they should be considered his true descendants— for this is not so; for those who are called 'the descendants of Noah' (Bnei Noach), have no connection to the reception of the Torah, the mitzvot, and the holiness of Shabbat;:, and on the contrary, it was said to them: 'and day and night they shall not cease',. because through their leisure and cessation from work they would add sin through idleness., And the seed of Israel are not named after him at all, for Abraham our father was the first of proselytes, )., as stated (Chagigah 3a), and a convert who undergoes conversion is like a newborn child (.), (as stated in Yevamot 22a),. and he merited to be the first father to all souls of Israel., And the souls that were to receive the Torah were set aside in a unique treasury,:, and the essential generations of Noah are that which is written: 'Noah was a righteous, wholehearted man',. for a person's real descendants are his good deeds., And it comes to teach us that even one who has children should know that this is not the ultimate purpose, and should see to bear the fruit of Torah and mitzvot which are termed 'the fruit of the righteous is a tree of life',. and they are a person's true generations.

topics.h: Earlier Generations Redeemed Through Later Merit
topics.en: And afterward it concludes in Midrash Tanchuma: " And whence do we know that even the early ones were saved in the merit of the later ones?:, For it is said: "And Noah found grace, etc.";, by what merit? In the merit of his generations,:. as it is said: "These are the generations of Noah".’ ),: And so is written in Midrash Rabbah (end of Parashat Bereishit 29:5) and there in Parashah 26 (26:6):, not that he was personally worthy,. rather the Holy One foresaw that Moses was destined to arise from him., And seemingly there appears a contradiction from its beginning to its end, for at the opening it stated that his generations are his good deeds!: However in truth they stated in Bereishit Rabbah regarding Noah: ", ‘in his generations’—in his generations he was righteous,. yet had he lived in the generation of Moses, etc., he would not have been considered righteous. And he was rescued solely in the merit that from him would issue the Jewish nation, receivers of the Torah, and Moses our teacher, and the like., And since it was necessary that one survive for the preservation of the world so that they emerge from him,. he remained, who was righteous in his generations. However the Torah came to teach us, that in truth the righteous are not called after his name, for they are called the children of Abraham who was like a newborn child;, and one who vows against the descendants of Noah is permitted to Jews, since once Abraham was sanctified they were designated after his name (.); (as stated in Nedarim 31a);, and his essential offspring was that which he refined himself in his good deeds, which are a person's true generations;, and to teach us that the essential fruit is the tree of life,. which is words of Torah and good deeds.

topics.h: The Torah as the Culmination of Divine Mercy
topics.en: And afterward, having elaborated in praise of the Torah,: it concludes in Midrash Tanchuma: " ‘Is it because Hashem is righteous that "He watched over the evil"? Rather the Holy One, blessed be He, performed charity with Israel, by advancing and exiling the captivity of Jeconiah before the captivity of Zedekiah, so that the Oral Torah should not be forgotten from them, and they sat with their Torah in Babylonia until this day, and neither sin nor worm held dominion over them, etc.’;, for the primary expansion of the Oral Torah began after the exile, for 'in much wisdom is much grief' (Ecclesiastes 1:18),. in that through much grief much wisdom was multiplied., And then were the Men of the Great Assembly who multiplied sharp insights of Torah, and through this sins did not dominate them, for the primary dominion of sins occurred because they slackened in Torah,. and automatically the evil inclination gains power to seduce., However, one who takes upon himself the yoke of Torah— words of Torah are healing and rectification for every iniquity and sin; ), and even regarding the blemish of the Covenant, where the holy Zohar (Part I, 219b) was stringent, his intent was only that one cannot rectify it to transform intentional sins into merits;, nevertheless through repentance and Torah it avails to be spared from punishment at least,. and 'the former things shall not be remembered, nor come into mind.',

sections.title: The Four Gifts and Their Divine Attributes
sections.summary: The divine names illuminate the four pathways of Torah, affliction, service, and prayer.

topics.h: Torah, Suffering, Service, and Prayer
topics.en: In Midrash Rabbah (Mishpatim, Parashah 30):: The Holy One, blessed be He, sought to give them four things:,, Torah, afflictions, sacrificial service, and prayer;, yet they did not desire them,: as it is said: "And they said unto God: Depart from us"—these are afflictions; " And the knowledge of Your ways we do not desire"—this is Torah; " "What is the Almighty that we should serve Him?"—these are the sacrifices; ". "And what profit should we have if we pray to Him?"—this is prayer.: Scripture mentions here in the verse two Divine Names:, the Name 'E-l' ( and the Name 'Shaddai' (, )345(. both of them together have the gematria of Moshe (345 =., The Name 'E-l' corresponds to the attribute of Malchut, ),: and as stated (Zohar Part I, 8a): ":, the glory of the Bride which is called E- l, as it is written: "E-l has indignation every day"’; ),: and it is taught (Zohar Part II, 91a): ", ‘The letter Nun is the mystery of fearing the Holy One, blessed be He, and knowing that there is judgment and a Judge, etc., and punishment for the wicked, because its mystery is the lower Hei’, for from the attribute of Malchut stems judgment, ",". 'the law of the kingdom is law,' as is known.: And this is what it meant: 'And they said to E-l: Depart from us'—. these are the afflictions that come through this Name. ", 'And the knowledge of Your ways'—this is Torah, namely the Oral Torah;, for the Written Torah represents the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He, in that He fulfills the commandments first, ), as written in Midrash Rabbah there and in the Yerushalmi (Rosh Hashanah 1:3),. and commanded us to walk in His ways and observe His commandments and statutes., And 'the knowledge of Your ways' is the Oral Torah,: and as stated in Rashi's commentary in Parashat Ki Tisa: " and in knowledge’—this is the Holy Spirit (Ruach HaKodesh);. namely a spirit drawn from that supernal Holiness, as stated in the holy Zohar., And the Oral Torah comes through the Holy Spirit, ). and as the Ramban wrote (Bava Batra 12a); ):: and so was expounded (Megillah 14b): "', ‘"And Esther put on royal apparel"—that the Holy Spirit clothed her’, meaning the Oral Torah, the aspect of Malchut: 'the mouth is the Oral Torah';:, and concerning this it is stated: 'my speech shall distill as the dew', and the Recanati explained (Parashat Ha'azinu) from the root of 'He has performed His word',:, as we say in the Midrash Rabbah: 'He tore His royal purple robe', and likewise 'imrati'—the royal garment which is the Holy Spirit;. and this is why the Oral Torah is termed 'the knowledge of Your ways.', And since the soul of Moses our teacher was present then, and it was fitting that Torah be given through him to them (, (as stated in the holy Zohar Part III, 216b), and then all of the Oral Torah would have been revealed to them. which was enfolded within the Written Torah with Moses our teacher.: And so it was hinted in the verse: 'all the fountains of the great deep burst open'—, the wellsprings of wisdom below, ), as written in the holy Zohar (Part I, 117a), that had they willed to receive the Torah, all lower wisdom, the Oral Torah, would have been revealed to them;, just as they merited at the Giving of the Torah through Moses our teacher, ):: for it is taught (Nedarim 22b):, Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the Five Books of the Torah, etc., and within them was enfolded the entire Oral Torah, and they would have merited to comprehend all the light of the Oral Torah directly from the Torah;:. and this is what it meant: 'And the knowledge of Your ways we do not desire.', And this refers likewise to the Name E-l,. Malchut: 'the mouth—we call it the Oral Torah.', Namely, afflictions to rectify the past which derive from this attribute, that there is judgment and there is a Judge;, and the Oral Torah to rectify for the future, ),: as written (Zohar Part I, 202a): ", ‘for you have no word to shatter the evil inclination other than Torah’, and this is the Oral Torah, ):: as written (Sukkah 52b): ", ‘If this vile one confronts you, drag him to the study hall’,. and that is the place where novel halakhot are innovated. And the Book of Deuteronomy (Mishneh Torah), which is from the root of the Oral Torah, ), as written in the holy Zohar (Part III, 261a); and so there was written in Deuteronomy the narrative of the Second Tablets, which contain Midrash, Halakhot, and Aggadot, ) as written (Shemot Rabbah, Parashah 46);, and all the admonitions in Deuteronomy, ):: concerning which they said at the end of Megillah (31b): ", ‘Moses spoke them from his own mouth’, in all of them the four-letter Name Havayah is mentioned, for in truth the afflictions stem solely from mercy, to arouse awe in man that he repent, like a father who roars loudly, ). and as written in the Zohar Chadash (Ki Tavo).:, Yet they said: 'To E-l: Depart from us,' ):. refusing even the minimal measure of afflictions mentioned in the Gemara (Arachin 16b). And both of them—afflictions and the Oral Torah—. derive from this Name, which is the attribute of Malchut.

topics.h: The Divine Name Shaddai and the Covenant
topics.en: And afterward regarding service, which is sacrificial offerings, the Name 'Shaddai' is mentioned, which corresponds to the attribute of Yesod Olam, ), as written in the holy Zohar (Part III, 11b);, and through this attribute the union of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shekhinah is effected,:, as it is stated: 'for all that is in the heaven and in the earth',:, and its Targum translation: 'which takes hold in heaven and on earth', meaning that the Foundation of the world which is called 'Kol' (all) holds onto Tiferet which is called heaven, and to the earth which is called the Congregation of Israel, ). as written in the holy Zohar (Part I, 31a end)., And since there is union with the Name Havayah which is mercy, afflictions are not required to atone for the past, and sacrifices suffice to rectify the entire past; and for the future, prayer likewise suffices, that Hashem, blessed be He, assist us, for without the Holy One helping him, he could not overcome the inclination, and prayer is required for this, ): as written (Shemot Rabbah, Parashah 38): ", ‘"Take with you words"—words means nothing other than words of Torah’, meaning to rectify for the future, and as we explained from the holy Zohar that there is no word to break the evil inclination other than Torah;:, they said to Him: 'We do not know Torah',:, He said to them: 'Weep and pray before Me', for Hashem desires that man pray before Him and call unto Him from the straits, to assist him in overcoming the evil inclination,. and then Hashem will not leave him in its hand.:, And they said: 'What is Shaddai that we should serve Him?' refusing sacrifices to rectify the past; " And what profit should we have if we pray to Him?'—, arguing that since the Holy One granted free will to man,. prayer will not avail to be saved from the accusation of the evil inclination.

topics.h: Moshe, the Divine Names, and the Gift of Shabbat
topics.en: And for this reason the gematria of these two Names (E-l + Shaddai = 31 + 314 = 345) is Moshe, whose allotted portion was Shabbat,:, as written: 'Moses rejoiced in the gift of his portion',. for with him the divine union was constant., And just as on Shabbat an Israelite is considered the entire day as performing a mitzvah, since he is always accustomed to labor, yet desists for the sake of the sanctity of Shabbat, his entire Sabbath day is like one confronted with sin who is saved from it, which is credited as performing a positive mitzvah (:); (as stated in Kiddushin 39b); and the entire Sabbath day is the union of the Holy One and His Shekhinah,. just as at the moment of performing a commandment., And with Moses our teacher the union of the Holy One and His Shekhinah occurred continuously on all days,:, and as it is written: 'And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him', meaning that he took with him the essence of the holiness of Joseph the Righteous, who is the Chariot for the attribute of the Righteous One, Foundation of the World, and His Name;. and this is 'Moses rejoiced in the gift of his portion', which is Shabbat.,". And according to this allusion, the name Moshe is the gematria of 'E-l Shaddai', as explained.

topics.h: Shabbat Humility and the Rectification of the Week
topics.en: And on Shabbat a Jew becomes humble and contrite of spirit, when he reflects upon everything that passed over him during the workdays,. as we explained regarding the verse cited at the start of Seder Eliyahu Rabbah applying this to Shabbat., And he does not require physical afflictions, for dread and awe fall upon him, and a great groan suffices to render him contrite of spirit,. and his heart breaks within him and he repents out of fear of Hashem., And likewise he merits words of Torah, the Written Torah,: as stated: 'and all agree that on Shabbat the Torah was given to Israel';, and likewise it is the time to merit an influx into the Oral Torah, ),: as stated (Zohar Part I, 47b): ". ‘the seventh day—this is the Oral Torah, etc.’, And likewise we merit sacrifices,:, for we recite: 'And the additional offering of this Sabbath day we shall prepare and sacrifice before You in love', and we explained that even though we do not offer the Musaf in this era, and even if the Temple were rebuilt right now we could not immediately sacrifice this specific Musaf,, nonetheless, since we desire to offer it and are prevented solely due to the lack of the Temple and Altar, and 'one who intended to do a mitzvah and was prevented, Scripture credits him as though he did it' (.), (as stated in the Gemara there, Kiddushin 40a), and all the more so since here applies 'so will we render the calves of our lips',. and it is credited as though we offered the Musaf through the love and desire to perform it.,: And so too prayer, for on Shabbat the core of prayer is: ", ‘Sanctify us with Your commandments, and grant our portion in Your Torah, and purify our hearts to serve You in truth’, and we do not pray at all for physical bodily needs, only for spiritual needs of the soul,. to merit purity of heart and to be spared from the accusation of the evil inclination.,. And this is the prayer He sought to give the Generation of the Flood to avail for the future, as we explained., And on Shabbat we merit all four things that the Generation of the Flood refused to accept, and the time on Shabbat is propitious to merit rectifying the entire blemish of the Flood generation, which is the root blemish of the Serpent which they were tasked to rectify,. and on Shabbat we are empowered to merit its rectification.,

sections.title: Noach, Adam, and Three Mitzvot of Repair
sections.summary: The mitzvot of women and the Torah’s spiritual archetypes reveal a path to repair the sin of Adam.

topics.h: Challah, Niddah, and Shabbat Candle Lighting
topics.en: In Midrash Tanchuma at the beginning of this parashah it opens:, ‘Let our master teach us: for how many transgressions do women die, etc.?’, For three, etc., and all three are from the Torah, etc.;. and one must understand the connection of this opening discourse to this parashah. ):, Now behold, in the Mishnah this is taught in tractate Shabbat (31b), and presumably all three have intrinsic relevance to tractate Shabbat,. even though the mitzvot of challah and niddah apply constantly.,: Indeed, the matter is as stated in the Midrash: " She spilled his blood, etc.—let her shed her blood and observe her niddah, etc.; she defiled the challah of the world, etc.; she extinguished the candle of man, etc.’—,: these three things that he enumerated correspond to the body, the nefesh, and the neshamah: ", ‘She defiled the challah of the world’ corresponds to the physical body,:, and as is stated: just as a woman mixes her dough with water, etc.,: so the Holy One, blessed be He, did with Adam the First, etc.: ", ‘And Hashem God formed man of the dust, etc.’,. and this refers to the body of Adam the First, who is the challah-offering of the world. And it said ‘she defiled the challah of the world’ ): based on what they said (Shabbat 146a): when the Serpent came upon Eve he injected contamination into her;, Israel who stood at Mount Sinai, their contamination ceased, etc.,: and this disputes the view of Rabbi Abba bar Kahana, etc.:. until three generations contamination did not cease from our Forefathers, etc., And we have already explained that ‘both these and those are the words of the living God’, for Jacob our father, peace be upon him, from his own personal perspective contamination had already ceased from him,. for he was like Adam the First prior to the corrupting sin., And he said that which the lightest of the light does not say, ), as stated (in Rashi's commentary, Vayeitzei, from Bereishit Rabbah), because he felt no bodily physical pleasure whatsoever, and felt no shame in this,:, just as with Adam the First prior to the fall, concerning whom it is written: ‘and they were not ashamed’,. and he fathered twelve tribes in whom there was no blemish. Nevertheless, in outward manifestation it was not yet the case that contamination ceased from all his seed, until they stood at Mount Sinai,:. as it is written: ‘I said: You are godlike beings’., And this is what it meant that she ‘defiled the challah of the world’, in that because the Serpent injected contamination into her, the contamination spread through Adam the First and through his seed until Jacob our father, peace be upon him, and through his seed until the Giving of the Torah;. yet even so there still remains the evil inclination. ", ‘And she spilled his blood’ corresponds to the nefesh,:. and as is stated: ‘for the blood is the nefesh’. ", ‘She extinguished the candle of the world’ corresponds to the neshamah,:. and as stated in Midrash Tanchuma, for it is written: ‘The spirit of man is the lamp of Hashem’., And Shabbat is the appointed time to rectify the entire corruption of Adam the First, for the initial blemish of the Serpent occurred through eating, and the eating of Shabbat, being in holiness, comes to rectify this, ).: and as is stated (Sanhedrin 38a): Adam was created on the eve of Shabbat, etc., so that he should enter directly into the banquet;: and in Avot DeRabbi Natan (chapter 1) the textual variant is: ", ‘that he should enter into the Sabbath meal immediately’, which means precisely in order to rectify the corruption;. and this is the deep connection of this Mishnah to tractate Shabbat.

topics.h: Noach’s Trial and Adam’s Spiritual Legacy
topics.en: Now behold, concerning Noah it is taught in the holy Zohar in this parashah (73a end, and see there 76a beginning):, Noah sought to examine that very sin which Adam the First had probed, not to cleave to it, rather to know and to rectify the world, etc., in that he desired to rectify the blemish and corruption of Adam the First;:. and this is what is stated: ‘Noah was a man, righteous, wholehearted’. " ):: ‘Man’ (ish) we find (Berakhot 54b):, they stood over a man—this is Moses,: as it is written: ‘Now the man Moses was exceedingly humble’; ): and so they stated in the Mekhilta (Yitro):, when Scripture states ‘and they asked each man of his fellow’, who is called 'man'? None other than Moses,: as it is said: ‘Now the man Moses’; ).: and so was expounded (Sotah 14a): " – ", and no man knew’ refers to Moses our teacher, ‘the man of God’; and in several places they expounded ‘the man of God’— and in several places they expounded 'ish' as referring to Moses. in Midrash Rabbah and the holy Zohar. ", ‘Righteous’ (tzaddik)—the attribute of Joseph,. who was the Chariot for the attribute of the Righteous One, Foundation of the World. ", ‘Wholehearted’ (tamim)—complete, the attribute of Jacob, ‘a simple/wholesome man’ (ish tam),:. which we translate in the Targum: ‘a complete man’.: And all three embody the sanctity of Shabbat: ): for regarding Jacob our father, peace be upon him, it is taught (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 11): yet Jacob, concerning whom Shabbat observance is written, etc.’;, for even though Abraham our father likewise fulfilled the mitzvah of Shabbat, ):, seeing that he fulfilled the entire Torah as stated (Yoma 28b), and according to the reading of the Rashba in his Responsa and in Sefer HaEshkol who read 'eiruvei techumin', it is explicit that he observed Shabbat, and even according to our reading of 'eiruv tavshilin' the rationale is likewise so that he select a choice portion for Shabbat ):, as stated (Beitzah 15b),:, nonetheless they said: Abraham, in whom Shabbat observance is not written, meaning that it was not written regarding him in the Torah specifically that he kept Shabbat;:, whereas regarding Jacob, in whom Shabbat observance is written specifically: ‘and he encamped, etc.’,. this demonstrates that the sanctity of Shabbat was permanently established within him., And regarding Joseph we likewise find that he prepared a Sabbath feast, ): as expounded (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 92): ":,. ‘and "prepare" means nothing other than Shabbat, as you say: "And it shall come to pass on the sixth day that they shall prepare"’., And so when the Zohar Chadash (Toldot) counted the seven Musaf offerings of the festivals corresponding to the seven Shepherds, he counted the Musaf offering of Shabbat corresponding to Joseph,. for the additional holiness of Shabbat derives from the dimension of Joseph., And Moses likewise embodies the sanctity of Shabbat,": as is said: ‘Moses rejoiced in the gift of his portion’, which is Shabbat;, for Moses selected and instituted the Sabbath day for Israel in Egypt, ), as stated (Midrash Rabbah, Shemot 1:32); ): and it is taught in Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 13):, behold Moses was there, but he was from the interior aspect; this one (Jacob) from the body and that one (Moses) from the soul;, in that Jacob our father, peace be upon him, is the body,. and from him issues the bodily sanctity of all Israel who descended from him., And Jacob and Joseph are as one, ), as written in the holy Zohar (Part I, 176b end);, and the soul of the blood is the vitality of the body, and Joseph is called 'the Life of the Worlds' as is known, and his dimension is the vitality of the body corresponding to the nefesh,. and he refines the souls (nefashot) of Israel that they be in holiness., And Moses is the neshamah, which is the holy root of the souls of Israel, which stem from the words of Torah,:. as is stated: ‘The spirit of man is the lamp of Hashem’., And every single Jewish soul has a root in the Torah, a letter or a fragment of a letter,. and Moses our teacher is the root of all words of Torah, which is called 'the Torah of Moses'.,. And these three came to rectify the blemish of Adam the First in body, nefesh, and neshamah., And Noah, concerning whom it is written 'a man, righteous, wholehearted',, which alludes to the aspects of Jacob, Joseph, and Moses as explained, sought likewise to rectify the world from the blemish of Adam the First,. and as stated in the holy Zohar. ): And so it is brought (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 25): –, as soon as Noah arose, they rested; and whence do we know this?, It is stated here an expression of resting,:, and stated elsewhere: ‘that your ox may rest, etc.’, alluding that within him was likewise a semblance of Sabbath rest, for he was 'a man, righteous, wholehearted,' embodying these three dimensions,. which are Jacob, Joseph, and Moses., Therefore he also desired to rectify the blemish of Adam the First," yet 'he was not able', as stated in the holy Zohar;, for even though he possessed these three dimensions, it was only 'in his generations', for in the generation of Moses he would have been considered as nothing relative to Moses, and likewise he would have been considered as nothing relative to Jacob and Joseph,:, for on the contrary, unto him it was said: ‘and day and night they shall not cease’;: and this is the connection of this opening discourse to Parashat Noach.

topics.h: Noach Walked with God: His Spiritual Stature
topics.en: And in Zohar Chadash in this parashah (22b): "' Noah walked with God"—. above all spiritual levels. ' And Noah begot three sons"—: Rabbi Kruspedia taught:: these are three modes of conduct within man:, the guidance of the neshamah to serve as an aid in the service of his Creator, and this is called Shem;, and the conduct of lust and the evil inclination that drives and heats the body, and this is called Ham; and the conduct of the good inclination, etc., and to beautify his deeds in Torah and fear of Hashem,". and this is called Japheth, etc.’, see there., And this likewise corresponds to the three designations written: 'a man, righteous, wholehearted',. which are the sanctities of Moses, Jacob, and Joseph, as we said., Namely, through his 'walking with God' above all levels,: he merited these three dimensions: the conduct of the neshamah;, and to subdue the evil inclination and conquer it,:, concerning which it is said: ‘with all your heart’—with both your inclinations, the good and the evil, ). as stated at the start of chapter HaRoeh (Berakhot 54a);. and the conduct of the good inclination.: And he enumerated them in the order of development:, for the neshamah is placed in man from the moment of conception, and the evil inclination rules over man from the moment of birth, ): as stated (Sanhedrin 91b);, and the good inclination enters a person once he reaches thirteen years of age, ). as stated in the holy Zohar (start of Parashat Vayeishev 179a)., And he counted the conduct of the neshamah corresponding to the holiness of Moses our teacher,, for he is the neshamah, as stated in the Tikkunim, being the root of all words of Torah, whence is the root of the souls of Israel,. and he is called 'man' (ish)., And Ham corresponds to the conduct of bodily desire, namely to be a hero who conquers his inclination,. and this corresponds to the holiness of Joseph who was the Chariot for the attribute of Tzaddik., And Japheth corresponds to the good inclination, and corresponds to the aspect of Jacob who is called 'a wholehearted man', who possessed no evil inclination at all, for he was like Adam the First prior to the fall, and knew nothing at all of the counsel of the Serpent, which is the self-centered experience of one's own pleasure, as explained; and this is the conduct of the good inclination like completely righteous ones ):, whom only the good inclination judges (as stated in Berakhot 61b), and not like the holiness of Joseph in the aspect of Tzaddik, which consists of the presence of an evil inclination. and the righteous one overpowers his inclination through awe and subdues it., Only that all these sanctities Noah possessed solely in his generations, and did not merit them on the supreme level of Moses, Joseph, and Jacob,: who are the foundational root of the holiness of Shabbat, as we explained.

topics.h: The Sweet Fragrance After the Flood
topics.en: And it is brought afterward in Zohar Chadash (23a)::, Rabbi opened: ‘"And Hashem smelled the sweet savor, etc."; when Noah went forth, etc., he began weeping over the world, etc., and arose and prayed before Him,. and that fragrance ascended before the Holy One, blessed be He, and was pleasing to Him.:: Rabbi said: Three fragrances ascended before Him:, the fragrance of his burnt-offering, the fragrance of his prayer, and the fragrance of his deeds;, and there was no fragrance in the world so pleasing before Him as that fragrance,:, and therefore He commanded and said: "My sweet savor shall you observe to offer unto Me"—:: meaning: the fragrance that Noah offered before Me shall you observe to offer unto Me:,. the fragrance of burnt-offering, prayer, and virtuous deeds.’ Namely, when Noah went forth and saw the destruction of the world, he wept over them and prayed for them, as is stated further on there at length;: and Hashem answered him: Only now do you say this, and not at the time I spoke to you in gentle language,:, where it is written: "For you have I seen, etc.",. in order that you plead for mercy upon the world, etc.?’, And had he prayed then, he would have annulled the decree, ), as written there and in the holy Zohar (Part I, 67b);, and once Noah saw this,. he offered burnt-offerings and sacrifices, etc.:, And this is what it meant: ‘three fragrances ascended before Him’, which likewise correspond to the three sanctities of Moses, Jacob, and Joseph, alluded to in the verse 'a man, righteous, wholehearted',: and as we said, they are the root of the holiness of Shabbat: The fragrance of his burnt-offering corresponds to the holiness of Joseph, counter to whom stands the Musaf offering of Shabbat,. as stated in Zohar Chadash, Toldot. And the fragrance of his prayer corresponds to the holiness of Moses our teacher, who prayed for his generation and gave his soul for them, unlike Noah, whose subsequent prayer was not in its proper time;, nonetheless that fragrance was pleasing to Hashem,. as stated in Zohar Chadash. And the fragrance of his deeds corresponds to the holiness of Jacob our father, peace be upon him, who is the body, and from him derives the sanctity of the body of all Israel who are his seed,. and good deeds are executed in the body. And then the sweet fragrance ascended,. which encompassed a semblance of these three aforementioned sanctities. And all of them are the root of the holiness of Shabbat, which is the attribute of Malchut.

topics.h: The Offering Made for the Sake of Heaven
topics.en: The fragrance of his burnt-offering—the sacrifices, ", ‘for a sweet savor’—for the sake of divine satisfaction, for the sake of He Who spoke and the world came into being, ): as stated (Zevachim 46b);, and the primary purpose of Creation is that the glory of His sovereignty be revealed, ): as stated (end of Avot 6:11): ", ‘Everything that the Holy One, blessed be He, created in His world He created solely for His glory, etc., and for My glory have I created it’; and so they expounded on the verse ‘Hashem made everything for His sake’— ",", ‘for His praise’, that they should praise Him, ) as stated (Shocher Tov, Tehillim 148); ):: and elsewhere (Shabbat 31b): " The Holy One, blessed be He, created His world only, so that they should fear before Him,:. as it is said: "And God has made it that men should fear before Him"’.: Yet both are true: for 'to fear' refers to man, who is the ultimate intended goal of Creation,: as is stated: ‘I have made the earth, and created man upon it’;, and the entire world was created solely for the sake of this, etc., the entire world was created solely to accompany this one (:); (as stated in Berakhot 6b);, and he was created for awe,:. and as is stated: ‘What does Hashem your God ask of you but to fear’., And the creation of the entire universe is for His glory, meaning that man should attain from it His glory; and this is the primordial light created on the first day, wherein man could gaze and see from one end of the world to the other, )., as stated (Chagigah 12a),. meaning to recognize from all of Creation the glory of His kingship.: ), And this is Shabbat: for Friday eve is awe, and awe rests within it (Zohar Part I, 5b),. a king, whose dread should be upon you., And from this likewise derives the fragrance of prayer which stems from this attribute,:, and as is stated: ‘O Lord (Adonai), open my lips’, and this Name denotes awe,:. as is stated: ‘And if I be a Master, where is My fear?’:: And in the Gemara (Berakhot 9b) it was expounded: ‘They shall fear You with the sun’— referring to prayer; ):: and likewise (there, 10b): ", ‘Let one not withhold himself from mercy, etc., for he fears God’, the terminology of fear is expounded regarding prayer and mercy; ):: and so too it was expounded (there, 6b): "' Who among you fears Hashem, etc."—,". referring to one accustomed to come to the synagogue, etc.’, see there., And likewise the fragrance of good deeds is from this attribute, ), as stated in the holy Zohar (Part III, 123a beginning). that the lower Hei corresponds to mitzvah. And throughout the entire Sabbath day a Jew is considered as performing a mitzvah, by virtue of being saved from the sin of Sabbath desecration, and like one who offers the Musaf sacrifice through love and yearning to perform it,. and was prevented by circumstance, wherein Scripture credits him as though he performed it., And prayer on Shabbat is deeply acceptable, for it is only for the needs of the soul, for mitzvot and Torah and purity of heart for the service of Hashem in truth ( and as explained in Discourse 3);, and Israel merit all three fragrances concerning which it said that there was no fragrance in the world so pleasing before Him as that fragrance;: and He commanded for all generations: " You shall observe to offer unto Me’—,: the fragrance of burnt-offering, prayer, and virtuous deeds.,

sections.title: Shabbat Lights and the Restoration of the Soul
sections.summary: Candle lighting, challah, and niddah are connected to the refinement of nefesh, ruach, and neshamah.

topics.h: Shabbat Candles and the Light of Judgment
topics.en: In Midrash Tanchuma (there, 2): ", ‘The lighting of the candle —: for it is written: "And you shall call the Sabbath a delight"—this is the lighting of the candle on Shabbat;, and if you say to sit in darkness, this is not delight, for those descending to Gehenna are judged only in darkness,:. as it is said: "A land of thick darkness, as darkness itself"’. ): And elsewhere (Midrash Tanchuma, start of Parashat Bo 2):?. With what are the wicked covered in Gehenna? In darkness., Just like this tub, etc.,:, so the wicked: ‘and their works are in the dark’, therefore the Holy One covers over them that which is darkness,:. as it is said: ‘and darkness was upon the face of the deep’—this is Gehenna. Yet in the Gemara (Pesachim 54a) it is called 'the light of Gehenna'; ), and so in the holy Zohar (Part III, 34b), where it enumerates seven lights that were created before the world was created,. it counts the light of Gehenna, see there. ).: And the matter is according to what they said in the Gemara (Eruvin 19a): that transgressors among the idolaters, even at the very entrance of Gehenna do not return in repentance, and for them Gehenna is darkness;, and just as in this world ‘their works are in the dark, and they say: Who sees us and who knows us?’, so also in Gehenna they do not repent,: and as is stated: ‘that have transgressed against Me’—. that they continue transgressing forever., In contrast, regarding transgressors of Israel, who justify the divine judgment upon themselves:, and say before Him: Master of the Universe,, well have You judged, well have You acquitted, well have You condemned, etc., for them Gehenna is termed 'the light of Gehenna';, for once they enter it—it illuminates for them,. and they acknowledge the righteousness of the judgment upon them. And as we heard from a certain pious man: who said prior to his passing:, why should he fear Gehenna,. since therein he will merit to recite such exquisite praise: 'well have You judged, etc.', Therefore it is called 'the light of Gehenna' that shines for them, and it is only for one hour that they are condemned in Gehenna,. and Abraham our father comes, raises them up, and receives them.

topics.h: Shabbat as the Garden of Divine Illumination
topics.en: And he stated this rationale for candle lighting on Shabbat:, for on Shabbat all Israel are called 'she that dwells in the gardens', ),: as stated (in Shir HaShirim Rabbah 8:13):, that on Shabbat they arise early to the synagogue and recite the Shema, etc.,:, and the Holy One says to them: My children, raise your voice, etc., meaning that on Shabbat all Israel are like one dwelling in the Garden of Eden,. which signifies that then it shines for them.: And ONEG ( - delight) is the acronym of:, Eden (, River (, Garden (, (as stated in Zohar Part I, 26a), which are the three sanctities of Shabbat;,. and it is light, the absolute opposite of Gehenna which is darkness.: And it said: What did women see to be commanded regarding these three mitzvot, etc.? She spilled his blood, etc.—let her shed her blood and observe her niddah, etc.; challah—she defiled the challah of the world, etc.; candle lighting—she extinguished the candle of man, etc.; ).: and in the Gemara (Shabbat 32a): ", ‘The soul that I gave within you is called a candle;,". concerning matters of the candle I warned you’, see there. And these three things correspond to the blemish of Adam the First, which manifested in nefesh, ruach, and neshamah,. and came about through the cause of Eve.:, And this is what it meant: she defiled the challah of the world—corresponding to the nefesh,:, and as they said: so the Holy One did with Adam the First,:, for it is written: ‘and a mist rose from the earth.. and Hashem God formed man of the dust, etc.’, and it corresponds to the nefesh,:, for it is written: ‘Let the earth bring forth living nefesh’, ),: and it is taught in the holy Zohar (Part II, 12a): ". ‘this is the nefesh of primordial man’., And even though Scripture there speaks of animals,. there is subsumed within it also the nefesh of man which is the vitality of the physical body. And that which was written ‘she spilled his blood’ corresponds to the ruach which resides in the heart.:, And in the Gemara the formulation is: ‘A revi'it of blood I placed within you’, meaning the revi'it of blood in the heart, ).: and as Tosafot wrote (Sotah 5a):,. a revi'it of blood is the pure blood from which the heart's foundation is formed, etc., see there.:, And even though it is written: ‘for the blood is the nefesh’, that refers to the blood in the liver and the blood of all limbs; whereas the revi'it of blood is the clear blood in the heart, and there is the dwelling place of the ruach,:, and corresponding to this it said: ‘let her observe her niddah’,. so that it atone for her for the blood of man that she spilled., And candle lighting corresponds to the blemish of the neshamah,:, and as they said in the Gemara: the soul I placed in you is called a candle, etc.,:. and it is written: ‘The spirit of man is the lamp of Hashem’.

topics.h: Three Mitzvot and Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah
topics.en: And the three mitzvot were given to rectify the blemish in nefesh, ruach, and neshamah., Therefore the mitzvot of challah and niddah apply every day, while candle lighting is uniquely on Shabbat, ): based on what is written in the holy Zohar in this parashah (62a):, nefesh and ruach are intertwined with one another, etc.; when a man comes to purify himself— they assist him with a holy neshamah, etc.,. and sanctify him, and he is called holy. And on every weekday a person possesses nefesh and ruach; ),: whereas on Shabbat, as is taught in the holy Zohar (Part II, 88b):, on Shabbat they grant man an additional soul, etc., a soul wherein is all perfection like the archetype of the World to Come,. for every single Jew merits this neshamah. )., And so in the Gemara (Beitzah 16a),:, even though they derived it from the verse 'and He rested' (vayinafash)—woe, the soul is lost,: nonetheless they used the terminology: ", ‘An additional neshamah the Holy One, blessed be He, places in man, etc.’;, and this is ‘they sanctify him and he is called holy’, ':. in the manner of that which is stated: ‘to know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you’. Therefore, the mitzvot of challah and niddah, which came to rectify the blemish of the nefesh and the ruach, their obligation applies on all days; while the mitzvah of candle lighting is on Shabbat,. to rectify the blemish of the neshamah stemming from the Serpent's fall.:, And as we recite in the Sabbath hymns: ‘and with a good menorah shining upon our heads’, which refers to the neshamah,: just as one merits in his mother's womb: ", ‘and a candle is lit above his head, and he gazes and sees by it from one end of the world to the other,: as it is said: "When His lamp shined upon my head"’ (:); (as written in Niddah 30b);, and this is ‘The spirit of man is the lamp of Hashem’, for it is termed 'the lamp of Hashem' to radiate unto him this illumination, of recognizing the glory of His sovereignty from all Creation, and as we said, this is the light created on the first day, whereby man gazed and saw from one end of the universe to the other,. namely to perceive from all of Creation the glory of His sovereignty., And in his mother's womb the lamp is above his head, for while still in his mother's womb he does not yet possess an evil inclination,: as stated (Sanhedrin 91b) from the verse ‘sin couches at the door’;, and the neshamah is pure, a portion of God, being drawn from His light,. which is the first revelation of creation ex nihilo accessible to human comprehension.

topics.h: The Additional Soul of Shabbat
topics.en: And likewise on Shabbat the additional neshamah, concerning which they said in the holy Zohar that all perfection is within it like the World to Come, is also the lamp above the head, which is an encompassing light (Ohr Makif). such that the evil inclination has no dominion on Shabbat. ): Therefore they said (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 11):, ‘He blessed it with luminaries’, see there,. which indicates that on Shabbat there is a revelation of that light of the first day. ): And it is explicit also in Sefer HaBahir (section 160):, He took the seventh and set it for them in its place,. and the rest He concealed for the righteous. And through the Sabbath candle we rectify the blemish of man's neshamah, and are saved from the evil inclination,:. and this is what is meant by ‘and with a good menorah shining upon our heads’., And on weekdays, where there is one who has not merited and possesses only two levels, nefesh and ruach, as written in the holy Zohar, the mitzvot of challah and niddah come,. to rectify the blemish of the Serpent in the two levels of nefesh and ruach, as explained. And this opening discourse appears at the beginning of Parashat Noach, based on what we explained from the holy Zohar and Midrash Rabbah, that in the Generation of the Flood the soul of Moses our teacher was present, and it was the time to give them the Torah, ) and there is an allusion to this in the Gemara as well (as explained above); and presumably it was then the time to rectify the entire blemish of the Serpent,. across all three levels: nefesh, ruach, and neshamah. And after they corrupted their ways and the waters turned into raging waters and the waters of the Flood— ". ‘for these three transgressions women die, etc.’, And on Shabbat is the time to rectify the entire blemish, and had all Israel kept the Sabbath according to its halakhot—they would immediately be redeemed entirely, for the rectification would be completely accomplished;. only that the world is judged according to its majority.,: Nonetheless, every individual soul who observes Shabbat according to its halakhah—is immediately redeemed.,

sections.title: The Sixth Millennium and the Gates of Wisdom
sections.summary: The Zohar’s teaching on the six-hundredth year becomes a meditation on knowledge, covenant, and redemption.

topics.h: The Opening of Wisdom’s Gates in the Sixth Millennium
topics.en: In the holy Zohar (Vayeira 117a): ", ‘And in the six hundredth year of the sixth millennium, the gates of wisdom above shall open and the wellsprings of wisdom below, etc.;: and your mnemonic sign is: "In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, etc.,. all the fountains of the great deep burst open"’., And one must understand the allusion and the mnemonic sign: how does it point to the year six hundred of the sixth millennium?, And the matter is, that the root of exiles is on account of the blemish of the Covenant, ) and as written in Zohar Chadash (Ki Tavo), that the admonitions in Deuteronomy pertain to the final exile, and the Ari of blessed memory wrote. that the number ninety-eight (the 98 curses) alludes to this blemish. ),: And it is taught in the holy Zohar (Part I, 219b):,. that he has no repentance and shall not behold the countenance of the Shekhinah, see there.,: And elsewhere (Zohar Part II, 214b) it is taught:, and these words apply when he has not performed complete repentance,. repentance that is fitting to cover over all his deeds.: And the meaning is: whoever is able to rectify the entire root corruption of the Serpent which occurred through this blemish when he injected contamination into Eve (.), (as written in Shabbat 146a), and from this the contamination adhered to Adam the First as well, and through this he became stretched in his foreskin (:), (as stated in Sanhedrin 38b), meaning that he was certainly created circumcised, and through the corruption he became stretched in his foreskin;, and since this occurred on the sixth day within the days of Creation, it is as though he was created thus;. therefore all his descendants are born uncircumcised. And through the contamination that the Serpent injected and which adhered to Adam the First,. it caused corruption and blemish during the 130 years of his separation. And one who rectifies the entire root corruption of the Serpent's blemish— ought to live forever;:, for to Adam the First it was said: ‘for in the day that you eat thereof you shall surely die’, yet he lived 930 years;, and this is because the day of the Holy One, blessed be He, is one thousand years,:. as it is said: ‘For a thousand years in Your sight are but as yesterday’., Namely, the seven days of Creation are the seven sefirotic attributes, and 'refined sevenfold'—seven times seven, which equals the forty- nine gates of understanding; and when all ten attributes are each comprised of ten,, it equals one hundred years, a complete number, ), and as written in the holy Zohar (Part I, 123a), and this applies to each attribute; and when all attributes are comprised of ten,. it equals one thousand years, the day of the Holy One, blessed be He. And Adam the First was able to live nine hundred years and into the tenth century as well; yet to live one thousand years in completeness, he would have needed to rectify the entire blemish of the Serpent totally,. and then he would have lived forever., And likewise whoever would rectify the entire corruption in completeness,: which is the meaning of that which is stated: " repentance that is fitting to cover over all his deeds’—. he would live forever. And since there was not yet anyone who rectified thus the entire blemish totally, such that he merit to live forever,. the holy Zohar wrote that he has no repentance.

topics.h: The Seven Millennia and the Seven Attributes
topics.en: Now behold, seven thousand years correspond to the seven days of Creation, which are the seven attributes;, and the world lies desolate for one thousand years, which is the day that is entirely Shabbat (. (as stated in Sanhedrin 97a end)., And this explains why 'that it was good' was not said on the second day, which alludes to the second millennium, in which occurred the Generation of the Flood and the Generation of the Dispersion;, and 'good' means nothing other than Tzaddik (the righteous),: as it is said: ‘Say of the righteous that he is good’ (.). (as stated in Chagigah 12a)., And the Generation of the Flood were the antithesis of the attribute of Tzaddik, for they blemished the Covenant, the aspect of Tzaddik; and they represent evil which is the opposite of good;:. and this blemish is called in the Gemara (Niddah 13b) 'offspring of the Flood'., And likewise the Generation of the Dispersion, ): it is taught (Midrash Tanchuma in this parashah 16): they instituted eiruvei chatzeirot solely for the sake of peace;, and so indicates the term 'eiruv', that it blends together the minds of people and makes them as one;: and it concludes in the Midrash: I make peace in My world,: and these wicked ones arise to bring discord into the world, etc.: ". "And the whole earth was of one language, etc."’ And even though it is taught in Bereishit Rabbah on this verse that they loved one another, and therefore a remnant survived from them, nonetheless Hashem foresaw, that their gathering would cause division and strife, for afterward each one would seek to dominate his fellow;, and their gathering was solely to rebel against the Omnipresent, blessed be He, and this is ‘a gathering of the wicked is bad for them and bad for the world’ (:); (as stated in Sanhedrin 71b); and so afterward they were killing one another;, and they were likewise opposing the attribute of Tzaddik which is called peace,. as is known from the holy Zohar.

topics.h: Very Good: The Hidden Role of Opposites
topics.en: And on the sixth day it is written: ‘And God saw everything that He had made, and behold, it was very good’, ) which was expounded (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 9) concerning every opposite of the good;, for the sixth day corresponds to the attribute of Tzaddik, Foundation of the World, and the time therein is to rectify the entire blemish and corruption of the Serpent which occurred through eating and caused the blemish through the contamination he injected into Eve;. and the Tzaddik is the one who guards the Covenant. And likewise the six thousand years came to rectify all the attributes from above to below;, and afterward Hashem will rectify from His side in the dimension of the first three Sefirot,. and we shall merit the Days of the Messiah and the day that is entirely Shabbat.: And as we explained regarding the Haftarot:, the three of affliction and the seven of consolation, which are to rectify the seven attributes from below to above;, only that there the three of affliction corresponded to the first three Sefirot beforehand, while here the seven thousand correspond to the seven attributes from above to below;. and thus the sixth millennium corresponds to the attribute of Yesod.

topics.h: The Meaning of the Sixth Century
