topics.en: And in the year six hundred of the sixth millennium, meaning when the sixth century has passed, which corresponds to Yesod of Yesod, and then is the time to rectify the entire blemish;. and this is what it meant that the gates of wisdom below shall open., And it is as we explained, that what is written in the holy Zohar that he has no repentance, ).: is in the manner of what they said regarding the sons of Eli (Rosh Hashanah 18a):, by animal sacrifice and meal offering it is not atoned, but it is atoned through Torah;, and similarly regarding this blemish he has no repentance,, for the root of repentance derives from Binah—the heart, as is known, and this is impossible to rectify completely, for had he rectified the entire blemish he would live forever, as we explained;,, yet through Torah, which stems from the attribute of Chokhmah, it is atoned,: and this is what is stated: ‘and health to all his flesh’—, meaning to this blemish which is called 'flesh',:, as is stated: ‘his flesh run, etc.’, and in holiness 'holy flesh', and in the opposite it is termed 'the flesh of donkeys',. and the Torah brings healing even to this blemish.

topics.h: When Supernal and Earthly Wisdom Open
topics.en: Therefore when six hundred years of the sixth millennium pass, corresponding to Yesod of Yesod, the gates of wisdom shall open, and whoever desires to repent in truth, will feel the heavenly assistance of how the gates of supernal wisdom have opened, which is the Written Torah corresponding to the attribute of Chokhmah, and the utterance ‘Let there be light’, ): and as stated (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 3): five times 'light', etc., corresponding to the Five Books of the Torah;:, and it is written: ‘Light is sown for the righteous’, for Hashem bestows upon one who overpowers his inclination, which is from the aspect of Tzaddik, from the primordial light which is supernal Chokhmah,. just as it receives from the apex of the supernal Yod which hints to Keter Elyon. ", ‘And the wellsprings of wisdom below’ is the Oral Torah, which is 'much wisdom' to rectify 'much grief',. and this avails to straighten the heart and empty the evil from the heart of a fool as well. ).: And this is what they said (Ta'anit 15a)::, righteous ones—unto light, for it is written: ‘Light is sown for the righteous’, meaning the primordial light which Hashem bestows upon the Tzaddik from Hashem's side from the light that was concealed for the World to Come; ":,", ‘and to the upright’, for it is written: ‘and gladness to the upright in heart’,:, and this is as it is written: ‘The light of the righteous rejoices’,, for through the light of the righteous—the light of the Oral Torah, the wellsprings of wisdom below,. which avails to straighten the heart—one merits joy.

topics.h: Noach and the Covenant of Yesod
topics.en: And regarding this the holy Zohar said: ‘and your sign is: In the six hundredth year of Noah's life’, for Noah is called 'a righteous man', because he did not corrupt himself like the blemish of his generation, the Generation of the Flood, and merited likewise to be the Chariot for the attribute of Tzaddik, Foundation of the World;, and when he lived six hundred years it was corresponding to Yesod of Yesod, and then was the time to give the Written Torah through the soul of Moses our teacher ), who was present then, as stated in Ra'aya Meheimna (Zohar Part III, 216b);, yet the Generation of the Flood refused to receive it,. and as written (Shemot Rabbah, Parashah 30) on the verse ‘And the knowledge of Your ways we do not desire’—this is Torah.:, Therefore it was hinted: ‘all the fountains of the great deep burst open’, which alludes to the wellsprings of wisdom below, for since they did not want to receive the Written Torah,, Hashem radiated to them the wellsprings of wisdom below, which is the light of the Oral Torah, perhaps it would avail them if they willed it;, yet even this did not avail them,:, and this is likewise hinted in the verse: ‘And the knowledge of Your ways, etc.’, ",. ‘and knowledge’ specifically, as we explained above.

topics.h: The Outpouring of Wisdom and the Future Redemption
topics.en: And this is what it stated in the holy Zohar: that in the six hundredth year of the sixth millennium the gates of wisdom above and the wellsprings of wisdom below shall open;, it stated the supernal wisdom first, for this is already after the Giving of the Torah, and then is the time to open the gates of supernal wisdom which is 'light sown for the righteous',. and the Oral Torah which is 'the light of the righteous rejoices', as explained.: And it concludes in the holy Zohar: ", ‘and the world will be prepared to enter into the seventh,. like a man who prepares on the sixth day from the setting of the sun to enter into Shabbat’. Namely, the number six hundred, corresponds to the six attributes, the six days of Creation, where each is comprised of ten times ten, as we said;, and these are the six attributes wherein man must refine himself from his own initiative,. to rectify the blemish in the aspect of Tzaddik which lies in eating and desires. And afterward the four hundred years,,: wherein Hashem bestows from the first three Sefirot—Chokhmah, Binah, Da'at: the gates of wisdom above and the wellsprings of wisdom below;, and afterward the final one hundred years corresponding to the attribute of Malchut, and these are the Days of the Messiah which exist within the extension of the Sabbath,: leading into the seventh millennium, the day that is entirely Shabbat.,

sections.title: The Haftarah of Noach and the Power of Intercession
sections.summary: The prophetic promise after the Flood emphasizes prayer, mercy, and the covenant that preserves the world.

topics.h: The Haftarah: From Barreness to Consolation
topics.en: We read as the Haftarah on this Shabbat: "Sing, O barren woman" (Isaiah 54:1) ),. and "O afflicted, storm-tossed one" (ibid. 54:11).: And the direct textual connection to the parashah appears to be solely the verse: "), For this is as the waters of Noah unto Me, etc." (ibid. 54:9);. however, the inner theme of both of these consolations derives fundamentally from this parashah., For regarding the consolation of "Sing, O barren woman, etc., for more are the children of the desolate, etc.", one might ask: how does this consolation avail, ),: seeing as it is taught (in Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:22): She raised up for Me more righteous ones during her destruction, than the righteous ones she raised up for Me during her construction’, see there; and how does this console when we see that the generations progressively diminish and decline?, And likewise, how do the promises of the prophet in the consolation of "O afflicted, storm-tossed one" avail, when we see that vast time has already elapsed and we are still not redeemed?, And the true comfort for this stems from this parashah,: as is stated: "For this is as the waters of Noah unto Me,. that I have sworn that the waters of Noah should no more pass over the earth". ),: For it is taught (in the holy Zohar Part I, 67b):, once He told him that he and his sons would be saved, he did not plead for mercy upon the world, and they perished;, and on account of this the waters of the Flood were called by his name,:. as it is stated: "For this is as the waters of Noah, etc." And nonetheless, Hashem swore that the waters of Noah should never again flood the earth; ),: and this operates in the manner of what is stated (Isaiah 59:16): ", "And He saw that there was no man, and wondered that there was no intercessor;. therefore His own arm brought salvation unto Him, etc." And "maphgia" (intercessor) was explained by the holy master (the Chozeh of Lublin) of blessed memory: to mean one who entreats insistently before the Omnipresent and says: " I will not budge from here until You have compassion upon Your children’;, and when there is no such intercessor and prayer warrior,. then Hashem, blessed be He, Himself has mercy upon Israel.

topics.h: The Oath That the Flood Will Not Return
topics.en: And so was it in the Generation of the Flood:, after Noah failed to pray on behalf of the generation,: afterward Hashem, blessed be He, swore: ", ‘I will not again curse the ground anymore for man's sake;. for the inclination of man's heart is evil from his youth’ (Genesis 8:21)., And even though this very rationale was the initial cause that brought the Flood,:), for it is written (ibid. 6:5): ‘and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually’, Hashem, blessed be He, used this exact reality to find merit for mankind, namely that the evil inclination enters from the moment he stirs to emerge from his mother's womb, ),. and as they expounded in the Yerushalmi (Berakhot 3:5) and in Bereishit Rabbah (34:10). And this is an advocacy of merit akin to the plea derived from the verse ‘and whom I have dealt ill with’ (Micah 4:6) ):. which is cited in the Gemara (Berakhot 32b). And similarly, the prolongation of the wait for salvation is certainly, in order that Israel awaken themselves through active repentance, ). and it be: ‘if they merit it, I will hasten it’ (Sanhedrin 98a)., And if, Heaven forbid, they do not awaken of their own accord, then Hashem, blessed be He, will Himself advocate merit on behalf of Israel, and declare that everything stems from Him,:, in the manner of that which is stated: ‘and whom I have dealt ill with’,:),. and as is stated (Ezekiel 36:27): ‘and cause you to walk in My statutes’.

topics.h: Noach and Moshe as Models of Intercession
topics.en: Now behold, the holy Zohar stated regarding the reason Noah did not pray for his generation:, Moses did not rely upon his own merit, but upon the merit of the early Patriarchs;. whereas Noah had no one upon whose ancestral merit he could rely, unlike Moses., And this is what is meant by ‘for this is as the waters of Noah, etc.’, in that he failed to pray for the world, and they were named after him 'the waters of Noah';. and the reason he did not pray was because he lacked the merit of the Patriarchs.: And nonetheless Hashem, blessed be He, aroused Himself on His own accord: ". ‘so have I sworn that I would not be wroth with you, nor rebuke you, etc.’:, And concerning this the prophet declared: ‘For the mountains may depart, and the hills be removed’, ),: which is expounded (Vayikra Rabbah 36:2):, ‘the mountains’—these are the Patriarchs; and the hills’—these are the Matriarchs; ": ‘yet My kindness shall not depart from you, neither shall the covenant of My peace be removed, etc.’

sections.title: Motzaei Shabbat: Eliyahu and the Hope of Redemption
sections.summary: The remembrance of Eliyahu binds covenant, good tidings, and the salvation of the world to come.

topics.h: Eliyahu, Messenger of the Covenant
topics.en: We mention on Saturday night Elijah, the angel of the Covenant.: And likewise in the Grace After Meals (Birkat HaMazon) we recite: ", ‘May the Merciful One send us Elijah the Prophet, remembered for good,. and announce to us good tidings, salvations, and consolations’., And this is as we explained, that optional, mundane eating triggers the accusation of the evil inclination, ) -, -,: and as is stated (Deuteronomy 8:10-12; 11:15-16): ", ‘And you have eaten and are full.. Take heed to yourselves, lest your heart be deceived, etc.’, for the evil inclination dominates only out of satiety, ) and as written in the Sifrei (Eikev 43) ). and in the Gemara (Berakhot 32a), ). and in the holy Zohar (Part II, 154b).:, And it is written: ‘And you shall eat and be satisfied, and bless Hashem your God’, which is the divine counsel that satiety not lead to the accusation of the evil inclination;, in that through the Grace After Meals, where one recognizes the power of the Giver, it contains none of the intermingling of evil at all,. and it stems purely from the side of good. Therefore ‘Take heed to yourselves, etc.’ is not appended to it. Thus Birkat HaMazon is the rectification for the root blemish of the Serpent which occurred through eating; )., and he came upon Eve and injected contamination into her (Shabbat 146a), and caused contamination in her seed,. and caused the corruption of the 130 years of Adam's separation., Therefore in the Grace After Meals, which is the rectification for the Serpent's blemish,:, we say: ‘May the Merciful One send us Elijah’, who is the angel of the Covenant, " and announce to us good tidings’—, and 'good' means nothing other than Tzaddik,: ):, as it is said: ‘Say of the righteous that he is good’ (Yoma 38b),:, and it is written: ‘Light is sown for the righteous’, the light that is 'very good', for then Elijah and the Messiah will unveil all secrets of the Oral Torah,:. as it is written: ‘The law of Your mouth is better unto me’ (Psalms 119:72). ),: And it is brought in the Midrash (Kohelet Rabbah 2:1):, all the Torah that you study in this world is vanity before the Torah of the World to Come,. namely in the Messianic era.

topics.h: The Meaning of Salvation After Shabbat
topics.en: ‘Salvations’—meaning salvation over all the past, ),: in the manner of what they said in Midrash Rabbah (Vayikra Rabbah 21:4): ". ‘My salvation’—on Yom Kippur., And likewise indicates ‘and consolations’, in that then Israel will be consoled over all the past,. which existed solely in order that it become 'very good'., And we have already explained that the sixth millennium corresponds to the sixth day, the attribute of Tzaddik, Foundation of the World, and then is the auspicious time for rectifying the blemish, and Elijah, the angel of the Covenant, will arrive; ),: and as is stated (Malachi 3:23): " ‘Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet. before the coming of the great and dreadful day of Hashem’. ", ‘The great’—the attribute of Abraham our father, peace be upon him, which is Greatness (Gedulah), ‘Lovingkindness to Abraham’;, and Abraham our father rectified the blemish of Adam the First, as written in Bereishit Rabbah (14:6), that Abraham would come and rectify in his place;, and according to the creation that existed after Hashem joined the attribute of Mercy with the attribute of Judgment,:, it is written: ‘when they were created’ (be-hibar'am),":), and expounded (Bereishit Rabbah 12:9): ‘in Abraham’ (be- Avraham), in his merit, etc.;:, and it is written: ‘The world shall be built in lovingkindness’ (Psalms 89:3),. in lovingkindness, which is the sanctity of the attribute of Abraham our father.

topics.h: The Attribute of Yaakov and the Promise of Good Tidings
topics.en: And ‘the dreadful’ (ha-nora)—the attribute of Jacob our father, peace be upon him, ), as written (in the holy Zohar Part II, 79a), which signifies that it integrates the holiness of Abraham and Isaac;, for Isaac's attribute is the Dread of Isaac (Gevurah), and Jacob our father encompasses also the holiness of Abraham our father which is Love, and out of love is born genuine awe;, and this is the attribute of 'Nora', where awe descends naturally through love,. and therefore he is the perfection of the Patriarchs, as written in the holy Zohar.: And in the Days of the Messiah the world will be rectified in both dimensions:, in the sanctity of Abraham our father which was to rectify the blemish and corruption of Adam the First as written in Bereishit Rabbah, and in the sanctity of Jacob our father who was born in holiness. and was like Adam the First prior to the corrupting fall, as we explained. And this is ‘the great and dreadful day of Hashem’;, and before the coming of this day shall arrive Elijah, the angel of the Covenant,. after the blemish has been rectified in the attribute of Tzaddik during the sixth millennium which corresponds to this attribute., And so too on Shabbat, wherein through the observance of Shabbat they are immediately redeemed, for Shabbat is rooted in the mystery of the Covenant as written in the holy Zohar, and it is the designated time to rectify this blemish and the fall of Adam the First, we mention Elijah, the angel of the Covenant;, for every individual soul who merits to observe Shabbat according to its halakhot is redeemed completely,: and we beseech that Elijah come and announce unto us good tidings.
